title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
嘉靖甲子惟
皇統天四十三禩
制當天下大比惟茲三晉秋八月
例得合試先期巡按御史楊
〔衍慶〕肅將
===
明命禮聘文彥俾司校閱百惟簾
務罔弗飭備視舊有虔思以
對
聖天子右文崇化之洪庥而盡以
人事
君之大義監臨之事實主之及期
矢於衆以〔紹周〕學正吳〔廸〕爲
考試官教諭黃〔鍼岡〕侯〔旻〕張
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

嘉靖甲子，惟皇統天四十三禩，制當天下大比。惟茲三晉，秋八月，例得合試。先期，巡按御史楊〔衍慶〕肅將明命，禮聘文彥，俾司校閱。百惟簾務，罔弗飭備，視舊有虔，思以對聖天子右文崇化之洪庥，而盡以人事君之大義。監臨之事，實主之。及期，矢於衆，以〔紹周〕、學正吳〔廸〕爲考試官，教諭黃〔鍼岡〕、侯〔旻〕、張
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year of Jiajing, the forty-third year of the Emperor’s rule under Heaven, the regulations called for the great triennial examination throughout the realm. Here in the Three Jin regions—that is, Shanxi—the candidates were, according to established practice, assembled for examination in the eighth month of autumn. Before the appointed time, the Regional Inspector, Yang Yanqing, reverently carried out the imperial command, courteously inviting distinguished scholars to oversee the reading and assessment of the papers. All arrangements within the examination enclosure [?] were put in proper order and fully prepared, with even greater care than before. His intention was to respond to the august beneficence of the sage Son of Heaven in honoring letters and promoting moral transformation, and to fulfill the great duty of serving the ruler by providing worthy men. He personally took charge of the work of supervision. When the appointed time arrived, he announced to the assembled company that [surname and title missing] Shaozhou [?] and Wu Di, an Instructor, would serve as Examiners, and that Huang Zhengang, Hou Min, and Zhang, Instructors …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
〔國華〕徐〔守倫〕李〔用賓〕羅〔誠〕爲
同考試官左布政使吳〔三榮〕
右參政馮〔惟訥〕知提調按察
使孟〔養性〕僉事陳〔觀衡〕監試
事與百執事皆遴選入院裒
提學副使周〔新感〕所簡士一
千六百有奇三試之拔其尤
六十五人迺錄其文二十篇
===
以
獻〔紹周〕序諸首簡曰古昔帝王之
感人心而和平天下也莫不
崇德象賢以輔理成化求厥
寧而覯厥成一時英儁之士
皆欲奮庸以熙
punctuated:
〔國華〕、徐〔守倫〕、李〔用賓〕、羅〔誠〕爲同考試官，左布政使吳〔三榮〕、右參政馮〔惟訥〕知提調，按察使孟〔養性〕、僉事陳〔觀衡〕監試事，與百執事皆遴選入院。裒提學副使周〔新感〕所簡士一千六百有奇，三試之，拔其尤六十五人，迺錄其文二十篇以獻。
〔紹周〕序諸首簡曰：「古昔帝王之感人心而和平天下也，莫不崇德象賢，以輔理成化，求厥寧而覯厥成。一時英儁之士，皆欲奮庸以熙
translation_en:
…Guohua, Xu Shoulun, Li Yongbin, and Luo Cheng served as Associate Examiners. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Wu Sanrong and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Feng Weine oversaw the duties of Proctor; Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Meng Yangxing and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Guanheng supervised the examination proceedings. Together with all the other functionaries, they were carefully selected to enter the examination compound. More than sixteen hundred candidates selected by Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhou Xin’gan were assembled and examined in three sessions. Sixty-five of the most outstanding were chosen, and twenty of their essays were then transcribed for presentation.
Shaozhou wrote a preface on the opening leaves, saying: “In antiquity, when emperors and kings moved people’s hearts and brought peace and harmony to all under Heaven, they invariably honored virtue and took worthy men as models, thereby assisting governance and accomplishing moral transformation. They sought tranquility and witnessed its attainment. The outstanding men of their age all wished to exert themselves in service and bring splendor to …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
帝載而成德爲行明試以功敷奏
以言以鳴
國家治化之隆之盛使德之所
積不厚不博雖有璀璨之章
華藻之辭用易賈而往有德
己是知才之進也固先於文
然必一德絕如而後峻大可
===
幾投之盤錯利器自別授以
大任而謨明弼諧之偉烈見
矣故際熙洽而造興五人元
愷四友十臣之倫能致格天
孚聖之洪業皆其中德裕而
道爲歸施設奇絕自炳炳彿
類而天下後世之言治者以
punctuated: 帝載，而成德爲行，明試以功，敷奏以言，以鳴國家治化之隆之盛。使德之所積不厚不博，雖有璀璨之章、華藻之辭，用易賈而往有德己。是知才之進也，固先於文，然必一德絕如，而後峻大可幾。投之盤錯，利器自別；授以大任，而謨明弼諧之偉烈見矣。故際熙洽而造興，五人、元愷、四友、十臣之倫，能致格天孚聖之洪業，皆其中德裕而道爲歸，施設奇絕，自炳炳彿類，而天下後世之言治者以
translation_en:
…the imperial undertaking, making perfected virtue the basis of conduct, demonstrating their abilities through achievements, and presenting their words for consideration, thereby proclaiming the flourishing greatness of the state's governance and civilizing influence. If their accumulated virtue were neither deep nor broad, then, despite dazzling compositions and ornate expressions, they would go forth to seek a price for them among the virtuous [?]. From this we know that advancement of talent certainly takes precedence over literary accomplishment. Yet only when virtue is wholly unified [?] can lofty greatness be hoped for. Set them amid tangled roots and gnarled joints, and the sharp instruments distinguish themselves; entrust them with great responsibilities, and their mighty achievements in enlightened planning and harmonious assistance become manifest.

Thus, amid flourishing peace, there arose the Five Men, the Yuan and Kai, the Four Friends, and the Ten Ministers [?]. Such men could accomplish great undertakings that reached Heaven and won the sage ruler's trust because their inner virtue was abundant and the Way was their ultimate guide. Their undertakings were extraordinary, their brilliance naturally resembling that of one another [?]; and those throughout the realm and in later generations who discuss good government take …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
唐虞成周爲稱首匪文之華
惟德之良也逮我
明隆興
列聖垂統汲汲於人紀之肇脩求
賢養士以圖天下之治作天
下之才者視昔有加迺羣之
以地聯之師儒董之章程格
致誠正脩齊治平之學諄切
誨育而又大比有定期選舉
有定名嚴臨以稽組織而觀
宣吐故天下人才圓於陶鎔
鼓鑄之中者無不德以爲輿
禮以爲御篤朴睦而脫矯飾
敦本尚質之風四方攸同焉
punctuated:
唐虞、成周爲稱首，匪文之華，惟德之良也。
逮我明隆興，列聖垂統，汲汲於人紀之肇脩，求賢養士，以圖天下之治、作天下之才者，視昔有加。迺羣之以地，聯之師儒，董之章程，格致誠正、脩齊治平之學，諄切誨育。而又大比有定期，選舉有定名，嚴臨以稽組織而觀宣吐。故天下人才圓於陶鎔鼓鑄之中者，無不德以爲輿，禮以爲御，篤朴睦而脫矯飾。敦本尚質之風，四方攸同焉。
translation_en:
…rank the ages of Tang and Yu and the flourishing Zhou foremost: this was due not to literary brilliance, but to excellence in virtue.
When our Ming rose to greatness, successive sage emperors established the line of succession, striving urgently to put human relationships in order. In seeking worthy men and nurturing scholars to bring order to the realm and develop its talent, they surpassed earlier times. They therefore assembled scholars by locality, connected them with learned teachers, and supervised them through regulations. They earnestly instructed and nurtured them in the learning of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world. Moreover, the triennial examinations had fixed dates, and selection had established designations. Under strict supervision, candidates’ compositions were scrutinized and their expression examined. Thus, talented men throughout the realm, perfected through this process of molding and casting, all took virtue as their carriage and ritual propriety as their driver, cultivated simplicity and concord, and cast off affectation. The spirit of attending to fundamentals and esteeming substance prevailed alike in every quarter.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
洪惟
聖天子纘承丕緒神道設教而文
治精液濡沐醞釀雍郁純瑩
匪藻思之爲懿而一德之豐
植其來也有自且
執中之傳
敬一之箴昭回雲漢士談孔孟而
===
說仁義者咸相與正心而向
道彬彬彬然盛矣況今三晉之
地比屬近服而譽髦斯士又
得
聖人以爲依歸被化尤深是以文
采呈灼於覲錄之餘者無異
其醇粹明博雄渾雅健體裁
punctuated: 洪惟聖天子纘承丕緒，神道設教，而文治精液濡沐醞釀，雍郁純瑩。匪藻思之爲懿，而一德之豐植，其來也有自。且執中之傳、敬一之箴，昭回雲漢，士談孔孟而說仁義者，咸相與正心而向道，彬彬彬然盛矣。況今三晉之地，比屬近服，而譽髦斯士，又得聖人以爲依歸，被化尤深。是以文采呈灼於覲錄之餘者，無異其醇粹明博、雄渾雅健、體裁
translation_en:
We reverently reflect that the sage Son of Heaven has inherited the great imperial enterprise and established instruction through the divine Way. The vital essence of civil governance bathes and nurtures all, fostering harmony, richness, purity, and brilliance. What is prized is not ornate literary invention but the abundant cultivation of undivided virtue: this has its source. Moreover, the transmission of Holding Fast to the Mean and the Admonition on Reverent Unity shine like the celestial River of Stars. Scholars who discuss Confucius and Mencius and expound benevolence and righteousness all join in rectifying their minds and turning toward the Way. How flourishing is their cultivated refinement!
How much more so now in the lands of the Three Jin, situated within the nearby domains of the throne! These renowned and outstanding scholars also have the sage ruler as their support and guide, and have been especially deeply imbued with his transforming influence. Thus the literary brilliance displayed beyond the record of audience [?] is alike in its purity and refinement, clarity and breadth, grandeur and fullness, elegance and vigor, and in its literary forms …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
風致悉根諸理道然後知翔
蔚於蘊攄必其中有實物譬
之容光隙照波流瀠洄合明
與瀾而觀之其本固自有在
矣是故因言以考德掄才而
需用顒顒昂昂極一時之選
而名登
===
天府其
清廟瑚璉之器
明堂棟梁之材乎矧彈冠彙征共
際
熙時而美之在於中日可見之行
也將必詳以居方鯁以立
朝廉以生威正以秉節文附衆
punctuated: 風致，悉根諸理道。然後知翔蔚於蘊攄，必其中有實物。譬之容光隙照、波流瀠洄，合明與瀾而觀之，其本固自有在矣。是故因言以考德，掄才而需用，顒顒昂昂，極一時之選，而名登天府，其清廟瑚璉之器、明堂棟梁之材乎？矧彈冠彙征，共際熙時，而美之在於中，日可見之行也。將必詳以居方，鯁以立朝，廉以生威，正以秉節，文附衆
translation_en:
…bearing and style are all rooted in moral principle and the Way. Only then do we understand that such flourishing richness in what is held within and expressed outwardly must have genuine substance at its heart. It is like light shining through a crevice or flowing waters swirling in eddies: when we consider the brightness together with the ripples, their source assuredly lies somewhere. Thus, through their words we assess their virtue, selecting talent to await employment. Dignified and high-spirited, they represent the finest selection of their age, their names entered in the imperial registers. Are they not the precious hu and lian sacrificial vessels of the pure ancestral temple, the beams and pillars of the Hall of Enlightenment?

Moreover, they dust off their official caps and advance together into service, all enjoying an age of flourishing rule; the beauty within them can daily be seen in their conduct. They will surely be circumspect [?] in their local communities, forthright in taking their place at court, incorruptible so as to command respect, and upright in maintaining their integrity, winning the allegiance of the multitude through civil accomplishments…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
武嚴敵愾惟
天子使而一毫計功謀利之心罔
參於其中則才與誠合忠結
主知經綸於
密勿之間翼爲宣力之際御
於家邦而推行於天下若稷
契元愷之篤棐寅亮而疏附
而先後而奔走禦侮奭旦閎
===
散之爲楨爲幹以致庶績之
咸熙而臻鳧鷖旣醉之休可
比隆也則知我
皇上軼文武而媲堯舜名世繼作
有出於文言之外者豈非繼
德爲之本耶夫晉之十以紀
punctuated: 武嚴敵愾，惟天子使，而一毫計功謀利之心罔參於其中，則才與誠合，忠結主知，經綸於密勿之間，翼爲宣力之際，御於家邦而推行於天下。若稷契元愷之篤棐寅亮，而疏附，而先後，而奔走禦侮，奭旦閎散之爲楨爲幹，以致庶績之咸熙，而臻鳧鷖旣醉之休，可比隆也。則知我皇上軼文武而媲堯舜，名世繼作，有出於文言之外者，豈非繼德爲之本耶？夫晉之十以紀
translation_en:
…In military affairs, they sternly confront the enemy, acting solely at the Son of Heaven’s command, without the slightest thought of calculating merit or seeking gain entering their hearts. Then ability accords with sincerity, and loyalty wins the ruler’s recognition. They conduct affairs amid the ruler’s confidential deliberations and render assistance when called upon to exert their strength [?], administering households and the state and extending their work throughout the realm. Like Ji and Xie and the Eight Worthies and Eight Talents, they offer steadfast assistance and reverent aid: drawing the distant near, assisting before and behind, hastening to serve and warding off aggression. Like Shi, Dan, Hong, and San, they serve as posts and supports, bringing all undertakings to flourishing completion and attaining blessings like those celebrated in “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fuyi) and “Already Drunk” (Jizui). Their achievements may rival those ancient glories.
Thus we know that our August Sovereign surpasses Kings Wen and Wu and matches Yao and Shun. Eminent men arise in succession, and there is something here that goes beyond what words can express. Is not the perpetuation of virtue its foundation? Now, as for Jin, “its ten, by which to record” [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
德理治而
聖天子壽考作人之化溥被涵育
賁乎人文類固可見山川流
峙北紀黃河之靈鍾而爲才
郁然可徵堯舜禹之授受一
道餘韻流澤百世而下風猶
可師孔子曰有德者必有言
===
是故晉之才之文也植本固
而發源深〔紹周〕竊幸卓犖琦
瑋之英逢兹
久道化成之世而期以建正大光
明之業者也第恐一日染翰
之長不能以槩生平之守爾
二三子又自謂以言進而意
punctuated:
德理治，而聖天子壽考作人之化溥被涵育，賁乎人文，類固可見。山川流峙，北紀黃河之靈鍾而爲才，郁然可徵。堯舜禹之授受一道，餘韻流澤，百世而下，風猶可師。孔子曰：「有德者必有言。」
是故晉之才之文也，植本固而發源深。〔紹周〕竊幸卓犖琦瑋之英逢兹久道化成之世，而期以建正大光明之業者也。第恐一日染翰之長，不能以槩生平之守爾。二三子又自謂以言進，而意
translation_en:
…virtue and orderly government [?]. The sage Son of Heaven’s enduring influence in nurturing worthy men spreads everywhere, sustaining and cultivating them and lending brilliance to human culture: this is surely evident. Rivers flow and mountains stand; the numinous power of the northern mountain ranges and the Yellow River gathers to produce talent, abundantly manifest. The single Way transmitted from Yao to Shun and Yu leaves lingering echoes and blessings; even a hundred generations later, its legacy remains a model to follow. Confucius said: “Those who possess virtue invariably have something to say.”
Thus the talents and writings of Jin have firmly planted roots and deep sources. I, 〔Shaozhou〕, privately rejoice that these outstanding and extraordinary men have encountered an age in which the Way, long sustained, has brought transformation to fruition; I look to them to accomplish upright and illustrious deeds. My only fear is that skill displayed in taking up the brush on a single day cannot encompass the principles upheld throughout a lifetime. You gentlemen, moreover, consider yourselves to have advanced through your words, yet think …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
或至於忘筌一旦榮寵炫於
目利祿惑於念守移淸約而
志易紛靡醇粹明博者爲浮
薄雄渾雅健者爲委靡隱居
求志之實德中道而捐之不
少自愛顧以枝葉汗漫之談
而欲求功業之烜赫如五人
===
元愷之於唐虞四友十臣之
於豐鎬宣都俞而陳賡歌奏
雅頌而詠追琢〔紹周〕固知其
必難也斯之謂親
明聖之敎化而不能率性以歸極
聞往聖之德風而不能私淑
以成身適足遺河嶽羞是學
punctuated: 或至於忘筌，一旦榮寵炫於目，利祿惑於念，守移淸約而志易紛靡，醇粹明博者爲浮薄，雄渾雅健者爲委靡，隱居求志之實德中道而捐之，不少自愛，顧以枝葉汗漫之談，而欲求功業之烜赫，如五人元愷之於唐虞、四友十臣之於豐鎬，宣都俞而陳賡歌，奏雅頌而詠追琢，〔紹周〕固知其必難也。斯之謂親明聖之敎化而不能率性以歸極，聞往聖之德風而不能私淑以成身，適足遺河嶽羞。是學
translation_en:
…perhaps even coming to forget the fish trap once the fish is caught. Once honors and favor dazzle their eyes, and profit and emoluments bewitch their thoughts, they abandon their commitment to purity and frugality, and their aspirations turn toward extravagance. Those once pure, clear-minded, and broadly learned become shallow and frivolous; those once vigorous, profound, refined, and strong become feeble and dispirited. They cast aside halfway the genuine virtue of living in retirement to pursue their aspirations, showing not the slightest regard for their own worth. Yet through rambling talk of mere peripheral matters, they hope to achieve brilliant deeds like the Five Worthies and the Yuan and Kai under the rulers of Tang and Yu, or the Four Friends and Ten Ministers at Feng and Hao. They would voice assent with cries of “du” and “yu” and offer songs in response to their ruler; they would perform the Elegantiae and Hymns and sing of “chasing and carving.” I, 〔Shaozhou〕, know full well that this must be difficult indeed.

This is what it means to receive personally the transforming instruction of an enlightened sage ruler yet fail to follow one’s nature and return to the ultimate standard; to hear of the virtuous influence of former sages yet fail to learn from them indirectly and perfect oneself. This serves only to bring shame upon our rivers and mountains. Is this learning…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖也者私便身圖之捷徑而
章縫也者欺世盜名之媒妁
與孔子曰有言者不必有德
信夫故才一也成於
聖而不詭隨於俗敬其事而能靖
共於
上雖謂天下之才可也晉何得而
===
限之始而以涵
聖化而入終而以違
聖化而出求爲晉才且不可得何
天下之能云是一時之才固
將以期異日之成而今之人
有同於古者亦以其德之造
爲自樹之地也德不德之間
punctuated: 聖也者，私便身圖之捷徑，而章縫也者，欺世盜名之媒妁與？孔子曰：「有言者不必有德。」信夫！故才一也，成於聖而不詭隨於俗，敬其事而能靖共於上，雖謂天下之才可也，晉何得而限之？始而以涵聖化而入，終而以違聖化而出，求爲晉才且不可得，何天下之能云？是一時之才，固將以期異日之成，而今之人有同於古者，亦以其德之造爲自樹之地也。德不德之間，
translation_en: …is studying the sages a shortcut to personal advantage and self-serving designs, and wearing the Confucian scholar’s cap a means of deceiving the world and stealing a reputation? Confucius said: “Those who have eloquence do not necessarily possess virtue.” How true! Talent, then, is one and the same. If a man is brought to maturity by the sage ruler without blindly following prevailing customs, attends reverently to his duties, and serves his sovereign with diligence and respect, he may indeed be called a talent of the whole realm. How could Jin confine him within its bounds? If, at the outset, he enters service nurtured by the sage ruler’s transforming influence, but ultimately leaves having turned against that influence, he cannot even qualify as a talent of Jin—how could one speak of him as a talent of the whole realm? Thus, in the talented men of the present, we must look forward to the accomplishments of another day. If men today equal those of antiquity, it is likewise because they make their attainment in virtue the foundation on which to establish themselves. Between possessing virtue and lacking it…

初易之是舉也總督軍務太

translation_en:
…and thus men of talent are distinguished. Why should the talented men of Jin not spur themselves on through virtue? Why abandon themselves through lack of virtue? This is indeed the subtle intent of this earnest admonition, yet at the outset of these scholars’ entry into service, they take it lightly [?].

For this examination, Jiang Dong, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and concurrently Left Vice Censor-in-Chief; Yang Zongqi, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Mao Peng, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, who had received orders to take over the post; and Zhang Bangxiao, Grand Coordinator of Datong and Censor-in-Chief, secured and pacified the territory. All the outstanding scholars benefited from their protection.

Hu Weixin, Regional Inspector of Zhili, and Hu Lun, Salt-control Censor, vigorously promoted exemplary conduct and sound principles, thereby honoring the foundations of education. Li Congjiao, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Liu Zongdai, a Secretary in that ministry, happened to witness this splendid occasion.

Wang Jiluo, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Li Qiao, Left Administration Vice Commissioner…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者樂仁者壽
天地之道可一言而盡也其爲物不貳則
其生物不測天地之道博也厚也高也
明也悠也久也今夫天斯昭昭之多及
其無窮也日月星辰繫焉萬物覆焉今
夫地一撮土之多及其廣厚載華嶽而
不重振河海而不洩萬物載焉
存其心養其性所以事天也
===
易
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
天施地生其益无方
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛乾之策二百一十有六坤之策百四
十有四凡三百有六十當期之日
神而化之使民宜之
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

知者樂，仁者壽。

天地之道，可一言而盡也：其爲物不貳，則其生物不測。天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。今夫天，斯昭昭之多；及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多；及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。

存其心，養其性，所以事天也。

易

大哉乾元！萬物資始，乃統天。

天施地生，其益无方。

歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。

神而化之，使民宜之。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The wise find joy; the benevolent enjoy longevity.

The Way of Heaven and Earth can be expressed fully in a single statement: because their activity is undivided, their generation of things is unfathomable. The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, substantial, lofty, luminous, far-reaching, and enduring. Now Heaven, viewed in one small part, is merely this patch of brightness; yet in its boundlessness, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended within it, and all things are sheltered beneath it. Now Earth, viewed in one small part, is merely a handful of soil; yet in its breadth and depth, it bears Mount Hua and the other sacred peaks without feeling their weight, holds the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and carries all things.

Preserving one's mind and nurturing one's nature are the means by which one serves Heaven.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginning, and it governs Heaven.

Heaven bestows and Earth brings forth; their benefit knows no bounds.

Place the remaining stalks between the fingers to symbolize an intercalary month. There are two intercalary months in five years; therefore perform the placing between the fingers twice before setting aside a stalk again. The stalk-number of Qian is two hundred and sixteen, and that of Kun is one hundred and forty-four, making three hundred and sixty in all, corresponding to the days of a year.

Work transformations through spiritual efficacy, enabling the people to live in fitting accord with them.

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣
協于克一俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一
哉王心
會其有極歸其有極
懋昭周公之訓惟民其乂我聞曰至治馨
香感于神明黍稷非馨明德惟馨爾尚
式時周公之猷訓
詩
羔羊之皮素絲五紽退食自公委蛇委蛇
===
羔羊之革素絲五緎委蛇委蛇自公退
食羔羊之縫素絲五總委蛇委蛇退食
自公
殖殖其庭有覺其楹噲噲其正噦噦其冥
君子攸寧
蓺之荏菽荏菽旆旆禾役穟穟麻麥幪幪
瓜瓞唪唪
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王曰商是常
春秋
punctuated:
萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣。

協于克一，俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」

會其有極，歸其有極。

懋昭周公之訓，惟民其乂。我聞曰：「至治馨香，感于神明。黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」爾尚式時周公之猷訓。

詩

羔羊之皮，素絲五紽。退食自公，委蛇委蛇。羔羊之革，素絲五緎。委蛇委蛇，自公退食。羔羊之縫，素絲五總。委蛇委蛇，退食自公。

殖殖其庭，有覺其楹。噲噲其正，噦噦其冥，君子攸寧。

蓺之荏菽，荏菽旆旆。禾役穟穟，麻麥幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。

莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。

春秋
translation_en:
The worthy men among the people of the myriad states are all servants of the sovereign.

Unite in attaining oneness, so that all the people say, “Great are the king’s words!” and also, “Single is the king’s heart!”

Gather toward the supreme standard; return to the supreme standard.

Strive to make manifest the Duke of Zhou’s teachings, and the people will be well governed. I have heard it said: “The fragrance of perfect government moves the spirits. Millet is not what gives fragrance; illustrious virtue alone gives fragrance.” May you follow these counsels and teachings of the Duke of Zhou.

Book of Poetry

A lambskin robe, with five white silk braids. Withdrawing from public duty to eat, at ease, at ease. A lambskin robe, with five white silk seam-bindings. At ease, at ease, withdrawing from public duty to eat. The seams of a lambskin robe, with five white silk bindings. At ease, at ease, withdrawing from public duty to eat.

Level and spacious is its courtyard; lofty are its pillars. Bright are its front chambers; secluded are its inner recesses. Here the gentleman rests in peace.

They plant the large beans; the large beans grow luxuriantly. The grain hangs heavy with ripening ears [?]; hemp and wheat grow thickly; gourds large and small abound.

None dares fail to come with offerings; none dares fail to come and acknowledge the king, saying, “This is Shang’s constant rule.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三〕
〔年〕春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯
鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于
陘〔僖公四年〕
冬鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳〔襄公二十五年〕
九月戊辰諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕公會
晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾
子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭
魚〔襄公十有一年〕
鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮　冬楚公子貞帥
師伐鄭〔俱襄公八年〕夏公會齊侯于夾
谷　齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十〕
〔年〕
===
禮記
樂事勸功尊君親上
故天降膏露地出醴泉山出器車河出馬
圖鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷龜龍在宮沼其
餘鳥獸之卵胎皆可俯而闚也
punctuated:
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三〕〔年〕。春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘〔僖公四年〕。
冬，鄭公孫夏帥師伐陳〔襄公二十五年〕。
九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕。
鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮。冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔俱襄公八年〕。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田〔俱定公十〕〔年〕。
禮記
樂事勸功。
尊君親上。
故天降膏露，地出醴泉，山出器車，河出馬圖，鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷，龜龍在宮沼，其餘鳥獸之卵胎皆可俯而闚也。
translation_en:
In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed; they then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
In winter, Gongsun Xia of Zheng led an army against Chen. 〔Twenty-fifth year of Duke Xiang.〕
In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
The men of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Xie, a son of the ruler of Cai. In winter, Zhen, a son of the ruler of Chu, led an army against Zheng. 〔Both passages: eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Both passages: tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Book of Rites
Take pleasure in one's tasks and strive for accomplishment.
Honor the ruler and feel affection for one's superiors.
Thus Heaven sends down rich dew, Earth brings forth springs of sweet water, the mountains produce wondrous chariots, and the Yellow River produces the horse bearing the diagram. Phoenixes and qilin are all found in the woodlands outside the city; tortoises and dragons dwell in the palace ponds. As for the other birds and beasts, one can simply bend down and look upon their eggs and unborn young.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
仁以愛之義以正之
天地四方者男子之所有事也
第貳場
論
聖人神化與天地同流
詔誥表〔内科一道〕
擬漢令公卿以下議可以佐百姓詔〔後元年〕
擬唐以馬周爲監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕
===
擬禮部右侍郎丘濬
進大學衍義補表〔成化二十三年〕
判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏
虛出通關硃鈔
致祭祀典神祇
懸帶關防牌面
失時不修隄防
第叄場
punctuated:
仁以愛之，義以正之。
天地四方者，男子之所有事也。

第貳場。
論：聖人神化，與天地同流。
詔誥表〔内科一道〕：
擬漢令公卿以下議可以佐百姓詔〔後元年〕。
擬唐以馬周爲監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬禮部右侍郎丘濬進大學衍義補表〔成化二十三年〕。
判語〔五條〕：
舉用有過官吏。
虛出通關硃鈔。
致祭祀典神祇。
懸帶關防牌面。
失時不修隄防。

第叄場。
translation_en:
Love them through benevolence; set them right through righteousness.
Heaven and earth and the four quarters are all within the sphere of a man's responsibilities.

Second Session
Discourse: The sage's wondrous transforming influence flows together with Heaven and Earth.
Imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [one topic from this category [?]]:
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor ordering the dukes, ministers, and officials below them to deliberate on measures that could assist the common people [first year of the Later Era].
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor [third year of Zhenguan].
Compose a memorial in the voice of Qiu Jun, Right Vice Minister of Rites, presenting his Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi bu) [twenty-third year of Chenghua].
Legal judgments [five items]:
Recommending and appointing officials and clerks with prior offenses.
Fraudulently issuing vermilion customs-clearance certificates [?].
Offering sacrifices to deities listed in the sacrificial canon.
Displaying or carrying official identification plaques [?].
Failing to repair dikes and embankments at the proper time.

Third Session

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
策〔五道〕
問自古聖王垂統貽謀以燕翼於後世者
豈但備物軌飭制度已哉以弘文教將
必有以著道化之菁華焉以創鴻圖將
必有以立迪哲之景範焉考諸詩書文
謨武烈丕顯丕承卓哉不可尚矣洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝當締造之初投戈講藝統會百王
神謨懿訓煥然備矣至我
===
成祖文皇帝纘弘丕緒著爲
永樂大典而古今之文獻具焉文之謨也
睿宗獻皇帝龍潛郢邸
積德累仁
崇文好禮而
有懿鑠與我
中興之大業啓焉武之烈也視詩書所稱不尤
皇上大孝建極善繼善述其
制作之盛有未易殫究者然宣昭
punctuated:
策〔五道〕

問：自古聖王垂統貽謀，以燕翼於後世者，豈但備物軌、飭制度已哉？以弘文教，將必有以著道化之菁華焉；以創鴻圖，將必有以立迪哲之景範焉。考諸詩書，文謨武烈，丕顯丕承，卓哉不可尚矣！洪惟我太祖高皇帝當締造之初，投戈講藝，統會百王，神謨懿訓，煥然備矣。至我成祖文皇帝纘弘丕緒，著爲《永樂大典》，而古今之文獻具焉，文之謨也。睿宗獻皇帝龍潛郢邸，積德累仁，崇文好禮，而有懿鑠與我中興之大業啓焉，武之烈也。視詩書所稱，不尤？皇上大孝建極，善繼善述，其制作之盛，有未易殫究者。然宣昭
translation_en:
Policy questions 〔five questions〕

Question: From antiquity, when sage kings established a succession and bequeathed plans to secure and protect later generations, was this merely a matter of providing material standards and ordering institutions? In advancing cultural instruction, they must have had means to manifest the finest flowering of moral transformation; in founding a great imperial enterprise, they must have had means to establish lofty models for guiding men toward wisdom. Examining the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, we find King Wen’s counsels and King Wu’s achievements, gloriously manifested and grandly carried forward—so lofty that nothing could surpass them!

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, at the beginning of his founding enterprise, laid aside his weapons to expound the classical arts, bringing together the traditions of the kings of all ages. His inspired counsels and excellent instructions were splendidly complete. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen then continued and enlarged this great legacy, compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia, in which the textual records of antiquity and the present were comprehensively assembled. These were counsels like King Wen’s.

Emperor Ruizong Xian, while still a hidden dragon at his princely residence in Ying, accumulated virtue and benevolence, esteemed culture, and delighted in ritual. His splendid virtue and our great enterprise of dynastic resurgence had their inception therein [?]: these were achievements like King Wu’s. Compared with what the Odes and Documents praise, were they not still more [glorious] [?]?

His Majesty, through his supreme filial devotion, establishes the highest standard, skillfully carrying forward his predecessors’ undertakings and intentions. The magnificence of his institutions and enactments cannot readily be explored in full. Yet, in making manifest …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖訓繹思
芳德
聖意每惓惓焉乃取
秘閣所藏
永樂大典
命儒臣校錄又
允禮部之請纂集
承天大誌是二書者固
金匱之宏編
===
聖朝之彝制垂之億萬年者其篇目之詳著述
之美可得而敷陳之與
聖天子所以煥耿光揚大烈者雖非臣下所能
仰窺而
聖孝所在亦可揚榷其萬一乎爾諸士莊誦之
餘其悉心焉以鳴
國家之盛
問班固漢書立儒林傳以識丁寬轅固諸
人范曄嗣之乃分立儒林文苑二傳觀
punctuated:
聖訓，繹思芳德，聖意每惓惓焉。乃取秘閣所藏《永樂大典》，命儒臣校錄；又允禮部之請，纂集《承天大誌》。是二書者，固金匱之宏編、聖朝之彝制，垂之億萬年者。其篇目之詳、著述之美，可得而敷陳之與？聖天子所以煥耿光、揚大烈者，雖非臣下所能仰窺，而聖孝所在，亦可揚榷其萬一乎？爾諸士莊誦之餘，其悉心焉，以鳴國家之盛。

問：班固《漢書》立《儒林傳》，以識丁寬、轅固諸人。范曄嗣之，乃分立《儒林》《文苑》二傳。觀
translation_en:
…the sacred teachings and reflect upon the glorious virtue: these matters constantly occupy His Majesty’s thoughts. He therefore took the Great Compendium of the Yongle Era (Yongle dadian), held in the imperial library, and ordered scholarly officials to collate and transcribe it. He also approved the Ministry of Rites’ request to compile the Great Gazetteer of Chengtian (Chengtian dazhi). These two works are indeed magnificent compilations for preservation in the golden coffers, enduring institutions of the sagely dynasty, to be handed down for countless ages. Can you set forth the comprehensiveness of their contents and the excellence of their composition? Although the means by which the sagely Son of Heaven makes radiant glory shine and exalts great achievements lie beyond what his subjects can fathom, might you nevertheless outline even a tiny part of what his sagely filial devotion encompasses? You scholars, after reverently reading these works, should devote your utmost attention to this, so as to proclaim the flourishing greatness of the state.

Question: In his History of the Han, Ban Gu established the “Biographies of Confucian Scholars” to record Ding Kuan, Yuan Gu, and others. Fan Ye followed him, but established two separate sections, “Confucian Scholars” and “Men of Letters.” Examining…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
其撰贊輕昂意以一乃傳經之學一乃
摛文之技嘩之品第亦較然矣自今觀
之有學爲儒宗八世博士而自伏多贓
之咎者有待詔公車博通經記而自嘆
察察之患者有著尚書雜記四十萬言
而輒以法免者有世習韓詩推長當世
而坐連楚獄者有從代郡受易說經鏗
鏗而自矜任情者有習公羊春秋沉思
精專博覽書傳而坐被貴戚之薦者豈
===
經術不足以致用與抑其人之無得於
經與有爲文勵學謚曰宣明君子而再
著太山之績者有博學能文號曰天下
無雙而克稱臺閣之任者有以文記知
名而蕩陰臨汾皆有聲稱者有系出宗
裔除長新城而儒化大行者有以禮自
牧而啓敬重於西河者有畫像東觀而
昭德政於內黃者豈文辭固足以自見
與抑其人之天資近道而無事於文辭
punctuated: 其撰贊輕昂，意以一乃傳經之學，一乃摛文之技，嘩之品第亦較然矣。自今觀之，有學爲儒宗、八世博士，而自伏多贓之咎者；有待詔公車、博通經記，而自嘆察察之患者；有著《尚書雜記》四十萬言，而輒以法免者；有世習《韓詩》、推長當世，而坐連楚獄者；有從代郡受《易》、說經鏗鏗，而自矜任情者；有習《公羊春秋》、沉思精專、博覽書傳，而坐被貴戚之薦者。豈經術不足以致用與？抑其人之無得於經與？有爲文勵學、謚曰宣明君子，而再著太山之績者；有博學能文、號曰天下無雙，而克稱臺閣之任者；有以文記知名，而蕩陰、臨汾皆有聲稱者；有系出宗裔、除長新城，而儒化大行者；有以禮自牧，而啓敬重於西河者；有畫像東觀，而昭德政於內黃者。豈文辭固足以自見與？抑其人之天資近道，而無事於文辭
translation_en:
…Considering the relative weight he assigns in his concluding appraisals, his intention is to distinguish learning that transmits the Classics from skill in literary composition; the ranking he assigns them [?] is also quite clear. Viewed from the present, there was one whose learning made him a leading Confucian authority, whose family had held appointments as Erudites for eight generations, yet who himself admitted guilt for extensive illicit gains. There was one who awaited an imperial summons at the Office of the Majors in Charge of Official Carriages, thoroughly versed in the Classics and their records, yet who lamented the troubles caused by his own excessive scrutiny. There was one who wrote Miscellaneous Notes on the Book of Documents in four hundred thousand words, yet was dismissed under the law. There was one whose family studied the Han tradition of the Book of Poetry over successive generations, who was acknowledged as foremost in his age, yet was implicated in the Chu prison case. There was one who studied the Book of Changes under a teacher from Dai Commandery and expounded the Classic with ringing conviction, yet was conceited and gave free rein to his feelings. There was one who studied the Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, reflected deeply and with concentrated attention, and read widely in books and commentaries, yet incurred blame for receiving a recommendation from imperial relatives. Could learning in the Classics be insufficient for practical service? Or had these men gained no true understanding of the Classics?

There was one who composed writings and studied diligently, received the posthumous designation “Gentleman of Manifest Enlightenment,” and twice achieved distinction in Taishan. There was one who was widely learned and skilled in writing, was called “without equal under Heaven,” and proved equal to his duties in the central government. There was one who became known for his prose writings and won acclaim in both Dangyin and Linfen. There was one descended from the imperial clan who was appointed Magistrate of Xincheng, where Confucian moral instruction flourished. There was one who disciplined himself through ritual propriety and inspired respect in Xihe. There was one whose portrait was displayed in the Eastern Pavilion and whose virtuous administration shone forth in Neihuang. Could literary accomplishment indeed suffice to distinguish a man? Or were these men naturally close to the Way, with no need of literary accomplishment…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
者與此皆若不無可疑倘諸士有槩於
中即以蔚宗之意見得失吾人之嚮往
決擇併一詳之可也
問古者作樂欲審聲音必本於律呂尚矣
其作者孰始文以五聲播以八音或分
月令或配卦爻而損益相生之法可詳
言與律呂長短史記漢書不同上下之
生班固京房有異律各六矣何又有六
十律調六十矣胡又有八十四調孰得
===
孰失與有所謂七始有所謂五聲二變
有所謂正聲變聲中聲子聲者其義何
居與夫還相爲宮飛灰候氣之說果皆
然與或謂黃鍾爲萬事根本先求聲氣
之元而諸律自定若徒求之金石秬黍
謬矣王朴李照之所定范鎮司馬光之
所議以及阮逸和峴胡瑗其論紛紛孰
爲是與乃若析衷千古確然可據者惟
蔡季通之新書已爾朱子固嘗取之而
punctuated:
者與？此皆若不無可疑。倘諸士有槩於中，即以蔚宗之意見得失、吾人之嚮往決擇，併一詳之可也。

問：古者作樂，欲審聲音，必本於律呂，尚矣。其作者孰始？文以五聲，播以八音，或分月令，或配卦爻，而損益相生之法，可詳言與？律呂長短，《史記》《漢書》不同；上下之生，班固、京房有異。律各六矣，何又有六十律？調六十矣，胡又有八十四調？孰得孰失與？有所謂七始，有所謂五聲二變，有所謂正聲、變聲、中聲、子聲者，其義何居與？夫還相爲宮、飛灰候氣之說，果皆然與？或謂黃鍾爲萬事根本，先求聲氣之元，而諸律自定；若徒求之金石秬黍，謬矣。王朴、李照之所定，范鎮、司馬光之所議，以及阮逸、和峴、胡瑗，其論紛紛，孰爲是與？乃若析衷千古、確然可據者，惟蔡季通之《新書》已爾。朱子固嘗取之，而
translation_en:
…were they such men? All these points seem open to doubt. If you candidates have formed some understanding of them, you may explain fully both the merits and shortcomings of Weizong’s views and the judgments we should make about what to follow.

Question: In antiquity, those who created music necessarily based their examination of sounds and pitches upon the yang and yin pitch standards, the lü and lü. This practice is ancient indeed. Who first established it? Music was patterned through the five notes and sounded through the eight classes of instruments. The pitch standards were variously assigned to the months or correlated with the hexagrams and their component lines. Can you explain in detail the method by which pitches generate one another through diminution and augmentation? The Records of the Grand Historian and the History of the Han differ concerning the lengths of the pitch pipes; Ban Gu and Jing Fang differ concerning upward and downward generation. There are six pitch standards in each of the two sets: why, then, are there also sixty pitch standards? There are sixty modes: why, then, are there also eighty-four modes? Which accounts are correct, and which mistaken? There are what are called the “seven beginnings,” the “five notes and two altered notes,” and the “regular tones,” “altered tones,” “middle tones,” and “higher-octave tones.” What do these terms mean? Are the theories of successively taking each pitch as the gong, or fundamental note, and of observing seasonal qi through flying ashes indeed both valid?

Some say that Huangzhong, the Yellow Bell pitch, is the foundation of all things: first seek the origin of sound and qi, and the other pitch standards will establish themselves. To seek them merely in metal, stone, and black millet grains is mistaken. Among the standards established by Wang Pu and Li Zhao, the arguments advanced by Fan Zhen and Sima Guang, and the many conflicting theories of Ruan Yi, He Xian, and Hu Yuan, which are correct? As for a work that weighs the discussions of past ages and reaches a sound judgment upon which one can firmly rely, there is only Cai Jitong’s New Book [on Pitch Standards]. Master Zhu did indeed adopt it, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
又著遡解鍾律篇可得聞其槩與其亦
有所受而互相發明與夫律呂放失衆
言淆亂古樂之絶響久矣我
國朝禮樂明備即今九奏樂章洋洋極盛玆
欲登雅樂用之以復太古之初可乎幸
相與訂之亦考古審音者之一助也
問字學切於民用大矣伏羲畫卦書契未
興至黄帝時始制以代結繩而文字立
矣文字立而聲韻因之矣後一變而爲
===
大篆再變而爲小篆自秦隸興而日趨
簡便有謂篆之廢由於秦自晉隸作而
遂務姿媚有謂宋之能多於唐何也字
有六義而又有八體六體及古今篆隸
文體可得聞與晉人擅其能者衆矣孰
爲最善臨川乃不之取若朱子獨取襄
之與芾而病蘇黄者又何與至於字有
五音四韻而音與韻何以別三十六字
母俗本傳訛而廢與增何所考禮部韻
punctuated:
又著遡解鍾律篇，可得聞其槩與？其亦有所受而互相發明與？夫律呂放失，衆言淆亂，古樂之絶響久矣。我國朝禮樂明備，即今九奏樂章，洋洋極盛。玆欲登雅樂，用之以復太古之初，可乎？幸相與訂之，亦考古審音者之一助也。
問：字學切於民用，大矣。伏羲畫卦，書契未興；至黄帝時，始制以代結繩，而文字立矣。文字立，而聲韻因之矣。後一變而爲大篆，再變而爲小篆。自秦隸興，而日趨簡便，有謂篆之廢由於秦；自晉隸作，而遂務姿媚，有謂宋之能多於唐，何也？字有六義，而又有八體、六體，及古今篆隸文體，可得聞與？晉人擅其能者衆矣，孰爲最善？臨川乃不之取；若朱子獨取襄之與芾，而病蘇黄者，又何與？至於字有五音四韻，而音與韻何以別？三十六字母，俗本傳訛，而廢與增何所考？禮部韻
translation_en:
…and further wrote the essay Tracing and Explaining Bells and Pitch Standards [?]. May we hear its essentials? Did this, too, draw upon received teachings, the works illuminating one another? The pitch standards have been lost, and competing accounts have become confused; the sound of ancient music has long ceased to be heard. Our dynasty’s rites and music are clearly established and complete. Even now, the musical compositions for the nine performances are magnificent and flourishing. Could we now promote elegant music and use it to restore the pristine condition of highest antiquity? Please examine these matters together; this, too, would assist those who investigate antiquity and scrutinize musical tones.
Question: The study of written characters is of great and immediate importance to the people’s practical needs. When Fuxi drew the trigrams, written records had not yet arisen. Only in the time of the Yellow Emperor were they first devised to replace knotted cords, and writing was established. Once writing was established, the study of sounds and rhymes followed from it. Subsequently, one transformation produced the large-seal script, and a second produced the small-seal script. With the rise of Qin clerical script, writing became increasingly simple and convenient; some say that the abandonment of seal script was attributable to Qin. With the emergence of Jin clerical script, writers came to pursue graceful, pleasing forms; some say that the achievements of the Song exceeded those of the Tang. Why is this? Written characters have six principles, yet there are also eight styles, six styles, and the ancient and modern forms of seal and clerical writing. May we hear an account of these? Many people of the Jin excelled in this art: who was the finest? Yet Linchuan did not approve of them. And why did Master Zhu approve only of Cai Xiang and Mi Fu, while finding fault with Su Shi and Huang Tingjian? As for the five sounds and four rhyme categories of characters, how are sounds distinguished from rhymes? Popular editions have transmitted errors in the thirty-six initials: what evidence should guide their removal or addition? The Ministry of Rites’ Rhymes…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
略與切韻須知其得失何如也自唐以
來修詞之子多宗沈約而吳棫又從而
患之何與我
國家稽古考文
聖祖以字韻多訛
特命儒臣校正彙而成書名曰
洪武正韻誠不刊之典也但其中字畫以何
文爲正而音韻以何聲定之諸子遵
制之餘諒究心於此矣請詳言之以觀博古之
===
學
問帝王制馭夷狄自舜格有苗其後無聞
焉周有昆夷之征玁狁之伐漢唐有五
郡之雄三城之築無非以戰守爲事其
詳可得聞與我
國家大一統之盛威武奮揚鞭撻四夷乃至
三犂虜庭亦古今僅見矣何邇年以來
武備玩愒蠢茲匪茹頃山後諸夷勾連
漠北沿邊數被侵掠不知將何以制之
punctuated:
略》與《切韻須知》，其得失何如也？自唐以來，修詞之子多宗沈約，而吳棫又從而患之，何與？我國家稽古考文，聖祖以字韻多訛，特命儒臣校正，彙而成書，名曰《洪武正韻》，誠不刊之典也。但其中字畫以何文爲正，而音韻以何聲定之？諸子遵制之餘，諒究心於此矣。請詳言之，以觀博古之學。

問：帝王制馭夷狄，自舜格有苗，其後無聞焉。周有昆夷之征、玁狁之伐，漢唐有五郡之雄、三城之築，無非以戰守爲事，其詳可得聞與？我國家大一統之盛，威武奮揚，鞭撻四夷，乃至三犂虜庭，亦古今僅見矣。何邇年以來，武備玩愒，蠢茲匪茹？頃山後諸夷勾連漠北，沿邊數被侵掠，不知將何以制之
translation_en:
…the Abridged Rhymes of the Ministry of Rites and Essential Knowledge of Phonetic Spelling (Qieyun xuzhi): what are their respective merits and shortcomings? Since the Tang, writers have mostly followed Shen Yue, yet Wu Yu subsequently found fault with this. Why? Our dynasty investigates antiquity and examines written forms. Because characters and rhymes contained many errors, the sagely founder specially commanded Confucian officials to collate and correct them, compiling them into a book entitled Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu zhengyun). It is truly an authoritative work admitting of no alteration. Yet what script provides its standard for the written forms of characters, and what pronunciation determines its sounds and rhymes? In the time remaining after your prescribed studies, you gentlemen have surely devoted thought to these matters. Please explain them in detail, so that we may assess your learning in antiquity.

Question: As for emperors and kings bringing the foreign peoples under control, since Shun brought the Youmiao to submission through his moral influence, nothing comparable has been heard of. The Zhou undertook expeditions against the Kunyi and campaigns against the Xianyun; the Han and Tang had the martial strength of the five commanderies [?] and the construction of three fortified cities. All these measures concerned warfare and defense. May we hear the details? Our dynasty, in the splendor of its great unity, displayed its military might and scourged the foreign peoples of the four quarters, even three times laying waste to the enemy’s court—something rarely witnessed in either ancient or modern times. Why, then, have military preparations been neglected in recent years, while these peoples stir in defiance? Recently, the various foreign peoples beyond the mountains have joined forces with those north of the desert, and the frontier has repeatedly suffered incursions and plunder. We do not know by what means they are to be brought under control…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
與豈分闇者猶有遺誅與夫兵家所尚
惟戰與守今日兵勢積弱臨敵望風而
戰弗可言矣築堡戍守動遭蹂躪而守
弗可恃矣議者以將帥匪人戎伍多缺
芻糧未充技藝弗閑賞罰未信間諜不
明之所致其果然與今發言盈庭材官
具集竟未聞有出一奇奮一戰而䇿虜
之情者茲欲講求六者行之將何道而
可臻實效與抑別有出於數者之外與
===
諸子生長於斯目擊茲患有憤於中乂
矣豈無抱請纓之志者乎願敎我良策
無煩執事
punctuated: 與？豈分闇者猶有遺誅與？夫兵家所尚，惟戰與守。今日兵勢積弱，臨敵望風而，戰弗可言矣；築堡戍守，動遭蹂躪，而守弗可恃矣。議者以將帥匪人、戎伍多缺、芻糧未充、技藝弗閑、賞罰未信、間諜不明之所致，其果然與？今發言盈庭，材官具集，竟未聞有出一奇、奮一戰而䇿虜之情者。茲欲講求六者行之，將何道而可臻實效與？抑別有出於數者之外與？諸子生長於斯，目擊茲患，有憤於中乂矣。豈無抱請纓之志者乎？願敎我良策，無煩執事。
translation_en: …? Could it be that among those entrusted with regional military command [?], some have still escaped the punishment of execution? What military strategists esteem is simply fighting and defense. Today our military forces have grown weak through accumulated decline; when facing the enemy, they falter at the mere sight of them [?], so fighting is out of the question. Forts are built and garrisoned, yet they are repeatedly overrun, so defense cannot be relied upon either. Those discussing the matter attribute this to unsuitable commanders, numerous vacancies in the ranks, insufficient fodder and grain, lack of proficiency in military skills, unreliable rewards and punishments, and ineffective intelligence. Is this indeed the case? Now proposals fill the court, and military men of talent are all assembled, yet we have heard of no one devising a single ingenious maneuver, vigorously fighting a single engagement, and fathoming the enemy’s circumstances. If we now wish to investigate these six matters and act upon them, by what means can we obtain practical results? Or is there some other approach beyond these several matters? You gentlemen were born and raised here and have witnessed these troubles firsthand; indignation has long [?] filled your hearts. Can there be none among you who cherishes the resolve to volunteer for military service? Please instruct me with a sound strategy, without troubling the officials.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者樂仁者壽
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭黃　批〔知仁所好固原於體之異矣樂壽是椎其自然之效耳註意自明場中作者顧以樂水樂山入講劃〕
考試官學正吳　批〔氣象宏大〕
考試官教授吳　批〔義精詞雅〕
〔述時文詞多重複獨此篇得之宜錄以式〕
===
聖人論知仁而其效各有所得焉夫知得其樂
仁得其壽皆本於動靜者也豈非理之所必致
者哉夫子言知仁而及之其意以爲知仁之
在天下其體固不可以強同而其效亦因之以
類應何則人心自有眞樂有所滯斯累於物矣
知者惟有得於動也而樂自生焉利用安身旣
能知天之命見大心泰自有樂天之誠心通乎
造化而相爲游衍怡然俯仰之無歉也智周乎
萬物而同其卷舒悠然內外之兩忘也雖所遇
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「知者樂，仁者壽。」
潘雲祥

同考試官教諭黃批〔知仁所好，固原於體之異矣；樂壽，是椎其自然之效耳。註意自明，場中作者顧以樂水樂山入講劃。〕
考試官學正吳批〔氣象宏大。〕
考試官教授吳批〔義精詞雅。〕
〔述時文詞多重複，獨此篇得之，宜錄以式。〕

聖人論知仁，而其效各有所得焉。夫知得其樂，仁得其壽，皆本於動靜者也，豈非理之所必致者哉？夫子言知仁而及之，其意以爲知仁之在天下，其體固不可以強同，而其效亦因之以類應。何則？人心自有眞樂，有所滯，斯累於物矣。知者惟有得於動也，而樂自生焉。利用安身，旣能知天之命；見大心泰，自有樂天之誠。心通乎造化，而相爲游衍，怡然俯仰之無歉也；智周乎萬物，而同其卷舒，悠然內外之兩忘也。雖所遇
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The wise find joy; the benevolent enjoy long life.”
Pan Yunxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔The different things that wisdom and benevolence delight in certainly originate in differences in their essential character. Joy and longevity merely indicate [?] their natural effects. The meaning of the commentary is clear in itself, yet candidates in the examination hall brought delight in water and delight in mountains into their exposition [?].〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔Grand in scope and bearing.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: 〔Precise in meaning and elegant in diction.〕
〔The examination essays were often repetitive in their wording [?]. This piece alone grasped the point; it should be recorded as a model.〕

The Sage discusses wisdom and benevolence, each of which attains its own particular result. Wisdom attains joy, and benevolence attains longevity: both are rooted in activity and stillness. Are these not results that principle must necessarily bring about? When the Master speaks of wisdom and benevolence and proceeds to these results, his meaning is that, as wisdom and benevolence exist in the world, their essential characters certainly cannot be forced into uniformity; their effects likewise follow from these characters, responding according to their respective kinds. Why is this so? The human heart inherently possesses true joy. Whenever it becomes obstructed, it is encumbered by external things. It is precisely because the wise attain something through activity that joy arises of itself. Making beneficial use of things and securing themselves, they are already able to understand Heaven’s mandate; seeing what is great and possessing an untroubled heart, they naturally have the sincerity of one who delights in Heaven. Their hearts communicate with the workings of creation and roam freely alongside them: contentedly looking down and up, they feel no lack. Their wisdom encompasses the myriad things and shares in their contraction and expansion: serenely, they forget both the inner and the outer. Although the circumstances they encounter…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
容有弗一然既動而不括將無入而不自得矣
其天下之至樂者乎人情孰不欲壽有所擾斯
役於形矣仁者惟有得於靜也而壽自致焉恒
以一德元善爲之常存艮以厚終元神自能可
久保之以孔固得天地之委和而氣自我凝也
錫之以無疆得天地之委順而命自我立也雖
其數或有弗齊然既靜而有常自恒久而不能
已矣其天下之至壽者乎吁樂得之於已者也
觀其樂而智益深矣壽得之於天者也觀其壽
===
而仁益至矣知仁之妙如此非聖人焉能形容
至此哉雖然知仁所好固以其體之異矣實一
理也其效寧有二乎蓋人生而靜天之性也感
物而動樂斯形焉樂生乎動動極而靜知者未
甞不壽也壽本乎靜靜極而動仁者未甞不樂
也此動靜循環之理仁智合一之說也昔夫子
自敘終身經歷次第亦曰七十而從心所欲不
踰矩則樂與壽孔子兼之矣噫非知道者孰能
識之
punctuated: 容有弗一，然既動而不括，將無入而不自得矣。其天下之至樂者乎！人情孰不欲壽？有所擾，斯役於形矣。仁者惟有得於靜也，而壽自致焉。恒以一德，元善爲之常存；艮以厚終，元神自能可久。保之以孔固，得天地之委和而氣自我凝也；錫之以無疆，得天地之委順而命自我立也。雖其數或有弗齊，然既靜而有常，自恒久而不能已矣。其天下之至壽者乎！吁！樂得之於已者也，觀其樂而智益深矣；壽得之於天者也，觀其壽而仁益至矣。知仁之妙如此，非聖人焉能形容至此哉！雖然，知仁所好固以其體之異矣，實一理也，其效寧有二乎？蓋人生而靜，天之性也；感物而動，樂斯形焉。樂生乎動，動極而靜，知者未甞不壽也；壽本乎靜，靜極而動，仁者未甞不樂也。此動靜循環之理，仁智合一之說也。昔夫子自敘終身經歷次第，亦曰：「七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」則樂與壽，孔子兼之矣。噫！非知道者孰能識之？
translation_en:
…may indeed differ, yet once active without being confined, they will find contentment wherever they go. Is this not the highest joy under Heaven? Who among humankind does not desire longevity? Yet when disturbed by something, one becomes enslaved to bodily existence. Only because the benevolent find fulfillment in stillness does longevity come to them of itself. Through constancy in a single virtue, primal goodness is perpetually preserved; through stillness that brings a substantial conclusion, the primal spirit can itself endure. Preserving it with utmost firmness, they receive the harmony bestowed by Heaven and Earth, and their vital energy becomes concentrated through their own efforts. Endowed with boundlessness, they receive the accord bestowed by Heaven and Earth, and establish their own destiny. Though their allotted spans may differ, once they are still and constant, they naturally endure without ceasing. Is this not the greatest longevity under Heaven? Ah! Joy is attained within oneself: observe their joy, and their wisdom is all the more profound. Longevity is received from Heaven: observe their longevity, and their benevolence is all the more consummate. Such are the subtleties of wisdom and benevolence. Who but a sage could describe them so fully?

Nevertheless, although the different preferences of the wise and the benevolent arise from differences in their essential character, they are in fact grounded in one principle. Could their effects really be two? Human beings are still at birth: this is their Heaven-given nature. When stirred into activity by external things, joy takes form. Joy arises from activity; when activity reaches its utmost, it turns to stillness. Thus the wise are never without longevity. Longevity is rooted in stillness; when stillness reaches its utmost, it turns to activity. Thus the benevolent are never without joy. This is the principle of the recurring cycle of activity and stillness, and the teaching that benevolence and wisdom are united as one. Formerly, when the Master recounted the successive stages of his lifelong experience, he also said: “At seventy, I followed my heart’s desires without transgressing the bounds.” Thus Confucius possessed both joy and longevity. Ah! Who could recognize this unless he understood the Way?

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
天地之道可一言而盡也其爲物不貳則
其生物不測天地之道博也厚也高也
明也悠也久也今夫天斯昭昭之多及
其無窮也日月星辰繫焉萬物覆焉今
夫地一撮土之多及其廣厚載華嶽而
不重振河海而不洩萬物載焉
趙于敏
同考試官教諭侯　批〔題本冠冕場中作者往往失之〕
〔浮泛是作詞簡意盡得其旨矣錄之〕
===
考試官學正吳　批〔純粹可誦〕
考試官教授吳　批〔說理精到〕
中庸論天地以誠而成化必詳其盛而著其功
也甚矣一誠貫天地之道也誠則自無不盛矣
而生物之功孰得而限量之哉子思發明天道
及此若曰大哉誠乎天地之所以爲天地者此
也聖人之所以爲聖人者此也觀乎天地則見
聖人矣何則天地之道散之雖極於至賾而約
之可盡於一言亦曰誠而已蓋其二氣之綱維
punctuated:
天地之道，可一言而盡也：其爲物不貳，則其生物不測。天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。今夫天，斯昭昭之多；及其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多；及其廣厚，載華嶽而不重，振河海而不洩，萬物載焉。
趙于敏
同考試官教諭侯　批〔題本冠冕，場中作者往往失之〕〔浮泛。是作詞簡意盡，得其旨矣，錄之。〕
考試官學正吳　批〔純粹可誦。〕
考試官教授吳　批〔說理精到。〕
《中庸》論天地以誠而成化，必詳其盛而著其功也。甚矣，一誠貫天地之道也！誠則自無不盛矣，而生物之功，孰得而限量之哉？子思發明天道及此，若曰：大哉，誠乎！天地之所以爲天地者，此也；聖人之所以爲聖人者，此也。觀乎天地，則見聖人矣。何則？天地之道，散之雖極於至賾，而約之可盡於一言，亦曰誠而已。蓋其二氣之綱維
translation_en:
“The Way of Heaven and Earth can be fully expressed in a single word: in their being they are undivided, and thus their generation of things is unfathomable. The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, deep, lofty, luminous, far-reaching, and enduring. Now Heaven, taken in one small portion, is merely this patch of brightness; yet in its infinity, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended within it, and all things are covered by it. Now Earth, taken in one small portion, is merely a handful of soil; yet in its breadth and depth, it bears Mount Hua without feeling its weight, holds the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and supports all things.”
Zhao Yumin
Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently grand, but candidates in the examination hall often err〕〔by treating it superficially. This composition is concise in wording and complete in meaning, capturing its purport. We include it here.〕
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and refined, worthy of recitation.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Its exposition of principle is precise and thorough.〕
In discussing how Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation through sincerity, the Doctrine of the Mean necessarily elaborates upon their plenitude and makes manifest their achievements. How profound it is that sincerity alone pervades the Way of Heaven and Earth! With sincerity, their plenitude naturally lacks nothing; who, then, could set bounds to their achievement in generating things? When Zisi elucidated the Way of Heaven to this point, it was as though he said: “Great indeed is sincerity! It is what makes Heaven and Earth Heaven and Earth; it is what makes the sage a sage. By observing Heaven and Earth, one can perceive the sage.” Why is this so? Although the Way of Heaven and Earth, unfolded in detail, extends to the utmost intricacy, when reduced to its essentials it can be fully expressed in a single word: sincerity, and nothing more. For the ordering framework of their two vital forces…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
無非眞實之貫徹而太極神發育之妙者莫得
以識其端也兩儀之主宰要皆无妄之充周而
貞元運化生之機者莫能以知其故也夫天地
惟其不貳故其盛也含弘靜深地得之而博厚
焉峻極昭融天得之而高明焉以高明則無止
息以博厚則無終窮而乾坤合德極其悠久焉
何如其盛也原其所以爲之基者孰非一誠之
所致也哉夫天地惟其盛故其生物也觀天於
昭昭之象而推極於無窮之表則明而爲日月
===
麗而爲星辰以至纖悉而爲萬物無一不爲之
覆幬矣觀地於撮土之形而推極其廣厚之體
則峙而爲華嶽流而爲河海以至森列而爲萬
物無一不爲之持載矣何如其不測也原其所
以爲之本者孰非一誠之所爲也哉夫物莫踰
於天地而天地不外於一誠信乎天地之道可
以一言而盡也然則聖人以至誠而弘功業又
何以異於是哉雖然造化無全功裁成輔相實
賴聖人以成能也是故聖人在上而至誠感通
punctuated: 無非眞實之貫徹，而太極神發育之妙者，莫得以識其端也。兩儀之主宰，要皆无妄之充周，而貞元運化生之機者，莫能以知其故也。夫天地惟其不貳，故其盛也，含弘靜深，地得之而博厚焉；峻極昭融，天得之而高明焉。以高明則無止息，以博厚則無終窮，而乾坤合德，極其悠久焉。何如其盛也！原其所以爲之基者，孰非一誠之所致也哉？夫天地惟其盛，故其生物也，觀天於昭昭之象，而推極於無窮之表，則明而爲日月，麗而爲星辰，以至纖悉而爲萬物，無一不爲之覆幬矣。觀地於撮土之形，而推極其廣厚之體，則峙而爲華嶽，流而爲河海，以至森列而爲萬物，無一不爲之持載矣。何如其不測也！原其所以爲之本者，孰非一誠之所爲也哉？夫物莫踰於天地，而天地不外於一誠，信乎天地之道可以一言而盡也。然則聖人以至誠而弘功業，又何以異於是哉？雖然，造化無全功，裁成輔相，實賴聖人以成能也。是故聖人在上，而至誠感通
translation_en:
…is nothing other than the thorough penetration of genuine reality; yet no one can discern the beginnings of the Supreme Ultimate’s wondrous, mysterious nurturing of life. What governs the Two Modes—Heaven and Earth—is, in essence, the all-pervading presence of freedom from falsity; yet no one can know why the passage from completion to renewal sets the workings of transformation and generation in motion. It is precisely because Heaven and Earth are undivided that they possess such fullness. All-embracing, capacious, still, and profound: Earth acquires these qualities and becomes broad and substantial. Lofty to the utmost, luminous and radiant: Heaven acquires these qualities and becomes high and bright. Through its height and brightness, Heaven never ceases; through its breadth and substance, Earth knows no exhaustion. Qian and Kun unite their powers and attain the utmost enduring constancy. How great is their fullness! If we trace what establishes their foundation, what is there that is not brought about by this single sincerity?

It is precisely because of their fullness that Heaven and Earth generate things. Observe Heaven in its visibly shining aspect, then extend this contemplation to the boundless reaches beyond: its lights become the sun and moon, its adornments become the stars, and, extending down to the smallest particulars, there are the myriad things. Not one is left outside its covering. Observe Earth in the form of a handful of soil, then extend this contemplation to the full breadth and depth of its substance: rising aloft, it forms Mount Hua and the other great peaks; flowing, it forms rivers and seas; and, extending to all that stands densely arrayed, there are the myriad things. Not one is left unsupported by it. How unfathomable this is! If we trace what constitutes their root, what is there that is not the work of this single sincerity?

Nothing surpasses Heaven and Earth, yet Heaven and Earth do not go beyond this single sincerity. Truly, the Way of Heaven and Earth can be exhausted in a single word. How, then, does the sage’s expansion of his achievements through utmost sincerity differ from this? Nevertheless, the work of creation and transformation is not complete in itself. Shaping and bringing it to completion, assisting and supporting it, truly depend upon the sage to fulfill its capacities. Thus, when the sage occupies the position above and, through utmost sincerity, evokes a response and establishes communion…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
以三辰則順度以雨暘則時若以品彙則咸亨
是聖人非獨有同於天地而實有功於天地也
故曰天地萬物之祖聖人天地之用
存其心養其性所以事天地
栗永壽
同考試官教諭張　批〔題本精邃作者類撥拾浮泛可〕
考試官學正吳　批〔似知學者　厭此作簡切錄之〕
考試官教授吳　批〔明順〕
===
君子脩其天之所與者而事天之道得矣夫心
也性也皆天之所以與我者也君子存養而無
失焉謂非善事其天者乎此孟子示人以知行
之全功也意曰斯道之原出於天而體道之功
存乎己知天固由於知性矣而事天之功當何
如耶彼心具於人而不知所以存之非所以收
盡心之功也故必操持於定靜以全其明覺之
良審察於幾微不累於物交之感夫是則存於
中以應於外而大體立矣性統於心而不知所
punctuated:
以三辰則順度，以雨暘則時若，以品彙則咸亨。是聖人非獨有同於天地，而實有功於天地也。故曰：「天地，萬物之祖；聖人，天地之用。」

存其心，養其性，所以事天地。
栗永壽
同考試官教諭張　批〔題本精邃，作者類撥拾浮泛可〕
考試官學正吳　批〔似知學者，厭此作簡切，錄之〕
考試官教授吳　批〔明順〕

君子脩其天之所與者，而事天之道得矣。夫心也，性也，皆天之所以與我者也。君子存養而無失焉，謂非善事其天者乎？此孟子示人以知行之全功也。意曰：斯道之原出於天，而體道之功存乎己。知天固由於知性矣，而事天之功當何如耶？彼心具於人，而不知所以存之，非所以收盡心之功也。故必操持於定靜，以全其明覺之良；審察於幾微，不累於物交之感。夫是則存於中以應於外，而大體立矣。性統於心，而不知所
translation_en:
…the sun, moon, and stars follow their proper courses; rain and sunshine arrive in due season; and all kinds of beings flourish. Thus the sage not only resembles Heaven and Earth but actually contributes to their work. Hence it is said: “Heaven and Earth are the progenitors of all things; the sage puts Heaven and Earth into operation.”

“To preserve one's mind and nourish one's nature is the means of serving Heaven and Earth.”
By Li Yongshou.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently subtle and profound. Writers generally gather superficial material [?]. Acceptable.〕
Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He seems to understand learning. Scholars find this tiresome [?]. This composition is concise and pertinent; admit it.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕

When the gentleman cultivates what Heaven has bestowed upon him, he attains the way of serving Heaven. Mind and nature are both what Heaven has given us. If the gentleman preserves and nourishes them without loss, can he be said not to serve his Heaven well? Here Mencius shows people the complete work of knowing and acting. His meaning is this: the source of this Way lies in Heaven, but the work of embodying the Way rests with oneself. Knowing Heaven certainly proceeds from knowing one's nature; but what should the work of serving Heaven be like? The mind is inherent in human beings, yet if one does not know how to preserve it, one cannot achieve the work of fully realizing the mind. One must therefore hold it firm in settled stillness, preserving intact its innate clarity and awareness; one must scrutinize the slightest incipient stirrings, remaining unencumbered by the responses aroused through contact with things. In this way, one preserves what is within in order to respond to what is without, and the greater part of oneself is established. Human nature is governed by the mind, yet if one does not know how…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
以養之非所以踐知性之實也故必涵泳日深
以復其湛一之本作爲不害一順其生息之機
夫是則制於外以養其中而所性定矣此固君
子脩道之功而何以謂之事天也哉蓋天賦以
理人得之而爲心放其心者違其天者也天降
以衷人得之而爲性戕其性者褻其天者也夫
旣存心於推致之餘而奉若之弗違者儼乎天
明之是察是小心之翼翼卽上帝之昭事也非
所謂善述其事者乎養性於精研之後而率履
===
之弗越者肅乎天鑒之是承是成性之存存卽
明命之顧諟也非所謂善繼其志者乎噫學至
於事天則知行竝懋仁知兼體聖人之能事其
庶幾矣雖然心與性非二物也知與行非二事
也故存心卽所以養性而事天不外於知天考
之中庸知天者盡性之事也事天者戒懼之功
也此固孔門授受之微言聖賢合一之正學也
學者其合而觀之
易
punctuated:
以養之，非所以踐知性之實也。故必涵泳日深，以復其湛一之本；作爲不害，一順其生息之機。夫是則制於外以養其中，而所性定矣。此固君子脩道之功，而何以謂之事天也哉？蓋天賦以理，人得之而爲心，放其心者，違其天者也；天降以衷，人得之而爲性，戕其性者，褻其天者也。夫旣存心於推致之餘，而奉若之弗違者，儼乎天明之是察，是小心之翼翼，卽上帝之昭事也，非所謂善述其事者乎？養性於精研之後，而率履之弗越者，肅乎天鑒之是承，是成性之存存，卽明命之顧諟也，非所謂善繼其志者乎？噫！學至於事天，則知行竝懋，仁知兼體，聖人之能事，其庶幾矣。雖然，心與性非二物也，知與行非二事也。故存心卽所以養性，而事天不外於知天。考之《中庸》，知天者，盡性之事也；事天者，戒懼之功也。此固孔門授受之微言，聖賢合一之正學也。學者其合而觀之。

易
translation_en:
…how to nourish it is no way to put knowledge of one’s nature into practice. Thus one must immerse oneself ever more deeply in it each day, restoring its original clarity and unity; one’s actions must do it no harm, following entirely its workings of generation and growth. In this way, one regulates outward conduct to nourish what is within, and one’s inherent nature becomes firmly established. This is indeed the gentleman’s work of cultivating the Way; but why is it called serving Heaven?

Heaven bestows principle, which human beings receive as the mind. Those who let their minds go astray defy their Heaven. Heaven sends down an inner norm, which human beings receive as their nature. Those who injure their nature profane their Heaven. Having preserved the mind after extending knowledge to its utmost, one reverently follows without deviation, solemnly attending to Heaven’s luminous wisdom. Such careful reverence is itself the illustrious service of the Lord on High. Is this not what is called skillfully carrying forward his undertakings? Having nourished one’s nature after thoroughly investigating it, one follows its course without transgression, reverently receiving Heaven’s scrutiny. Such constant preservation of one’s perfected nature is itself keeping the luminous mandate always in view. Is this not what is called skillfully continuing his intentions?

Ah! When learning reaches the point of serving Heaven, knowledge and action advance together, and benevolence and wisdom are embodied alike. One may then come close to the full accomplishments of the sage. Nevertheless, mind and nature are not two separate things, nor are knowledge and action two separate affairs. Thus preserving the mind is precisely the means of nourishing one’s nature, and serving Heaven does not lie outside knowing Heaven. Examining this in light of the Doctrine of the Mean, knowing Heaven is the task of fully realizing one’s nature; serving Heaven is the work of vigilance and apprehension. These are indeed the subtle teachings transmitted within the school of Confucius, the orthodox learning in which sages and worthies are united. Students should consider them together.

Book of Changes

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
趙于敏
同考試官教諭侯　批
乾道甚大此聖人首釋乾元之
義其旨微矣作者多翻摭浮詞又以顯微有無前後貫講意多纏繞
至統天處又著於物與天德似不相涉惟此篇詞理精確結尤出人
意表特錄之
考試官教授吳　批
詞不費而理獨到
考試官學正吳　批
明瑩無疵
象傳贊乾元之大以其具造化之全也蓋肇萬
===
類而貫天德者造化之全功也乾元以之斯其
所以爲大乎今夫卦名曰乾蓋乾即天也而元
則天德之首也大矣哉乾之元乎發育萬物綱
紀造化其至大而無以加者乎何則萬物生而
不窮必有所以始之者乾元也鼓化機於初動
以啓先天之功涵生意於甚微以立羣物之命
理雖未立凡賴之以化醇者不外天載之神氣
雖未定凡藉之以成象者莫非絪緼之化蓋不
惟始乎一物而且爲萬物之資始矣然非止始
punctuated:
大哉乾元！萬物資始，乃統天。
趙于敏
同考試官教諭侯批：乾道甚大，此聖人首釋乾元之義，其旨微矣。作者多翻摭浮詞，又以顯微、有無、前後貫講，意多纏繞。至統天處，又著於物，與天德似不相涉。惟此篇詞理精確，結尤出人意表，特錄之。
考試官教授吳批：詞不費而理獨到。
考試官學正吳批：明瑩無疵。
象傳贊乾元之大，以其具造化之全也。蓋肇萬類而貫天德者，造化之全功也。乾元以之，斯其所以爲大乎！今夫卦名曰乾，蓋乾即天也，而元則天德之首也。大矣哉，乾之元乎！發育萬物，綱紀造化，其至大而無以加者乎！何則？萬物生而不窮，必有所以始之者，乾元也。鼓化機於初動，以啓先天之功；涵生意於甚微，以立羣物之命。理雖未立，凡賴之以化醇者，不外天載之神；氣雖未定，凡藉之以成象者，莫非絪緼之化。蓋不惟始乎一物，而且爲萬物之資始矣。然非止始
translation_en:
“Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! The myriad things draw upon it for their beginning, and it encompasses Heaven.”
Zhao Yumin
Comment by Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor: “The Way of Qian is exceedingly great. Here the sage first explains the meaning of Qian’s primal power, and his intent is subtle. Writers commonly rummage about for empty phrases, then link the manifest and the hidden, being and nonbeing, and before and after into a continuous exposition, leaving their meaning tangled. When they reach ‘encompasses Heaven,’ they remain fixated on things, seemingly without engaging with Heaven’s virtue. This essay alone is precise in both expression and reasoning; its conclusion is particularly unexpected. I have therefore specially selected it for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: “Economical in words, yet singularly penetrating in reasoning.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Lucid and luminous, without blemish.”
The Commentary on the Images [?] praises the greatness of Qian’s primal power because it possesses the entirety of creation and transformation. To originate the myriad kinds of beings and pervade Heaven’s virtue is the complete achievement of creation and transformation. Qian’s primal power possesses this capacity: is this not why it is great? Now, the hexagram is named Qian. Qian is Heaven, and the primal is foremost among Heaven’s virtues. Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! It brings forth and nurtures the myriad things and orders creation and transformation. Is its greatness not unsurpassable? Why is this so? The myriad things come into being without end; there must be that which gives them their beginning. This is Qian’s primal power. It stirs the workings of transformation at their first movement, initiating an achievement that precedes Heaven; it harbors the impulse of life in the utmost subtlety, establishing the allotted nature of all beings. Though principle is not yet established, whatever relies upon it to blend and mature does not lie outside the spiritual efficacy of Heaven’s workings. Though vital energy is not yet settled, whatever draws upon it to take form is invariably a transformation wrought by the intermingling of vital energies. Thus it does not merely initiate a single thing: it supplies the beginning upon which the myriad things depend. Yet it does not merely give a beginning …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬物而已又能統乎天焉天德運而不息必有
所以統之者乾元也命之流行不已有以體之
而不遺誠之通復無端有以貫之而無外各全
其理而神功之迭運皆一元之周流各足其氣
而化育之相宣皆一元之貫徹蓋不惟專乎一
德而且爲四德之統會矣吁知大始則能盡化
統天德則能盡神此乾元之至妙者也其大爲
何如哉彖傳贊之宜矣抑此所謂君道也春秋
繫王於天正次王王次春蓋元者天之仁氣也
天不言而品物亨歲功成者元也四時五行不
過宣其氣焉爾聖無爲而庶績熙治功成者亦
元也四岳九官不過佐其職焉爾是故體元居
正聖王之所以法天也觀於乾元而其義益明
矣故曰聖人與昊天同一道信夫
神而化之使民宜之
劉守仁
同考試官教諭張　批
聖人通變使民不倦之妙正在
神化宜民處兒之士子不能體貼率記誦模擬詞煩而意反晦惟此
punctuated:
萬物而已，又能統乎天焉。天德運而不息，必有所以統之者，乾元也。命之流行不已，有以體之而不遺；誠之通復無端，有以貫之而無外。各全其理，而神功之迭運，皆一元之周流；各足其氣，而化育之相宣，皆一元之貫徹。蓋不惟專乎一德，而且爲四德之統會矣。吁！知大始則能盡化，統天德則能盡神，此乾元之至妙者也。其大爲何如哉！《彖傳》贊之宜矣。抑此所謂君道也。《春秋》繫王於天，正次王，王次春，蓋元者天之仁氣也。天不言而品物亨、歲功成者，元也；四時五行，不過宣其氣焉爾。聖無爲而庶績熙、治功成者，亦元也；四岳九官，不過佐其職焉爾。是故體元居正，聖王之所以法天也。觀於乾元，而其義益明矣。故曰：「聖人與昊天同一道。」信夫！

神而化之，使民宜之。
劉守仁

同考試官教諭張　批：
聖人通變使民不倦之妙，正在神化宜民處。兒之士子不能體貼，率記誦模擬，詞煩而意反晦。惟此
translation_en:
…the myriad things alone; it can also encompass Heaven. Heaven’s virtue operates without ceasing, and what unifies it is the primal principle of Qian. It embodies the unceasing flow of Heaven’s mandate without omission and pervades the endless circulation and return of sincerity, leaving nothing outside it. Each thing possesses its principle in full, and the successive workings of divine efficacy are all the circulation of this single primal principle. Each thing possesses its vital force in sufficiency, and the mutually unfolding processes of transformation and nurture are all the thorough penetration of this single primal principle. Thus it does not preside over just one virtue: it unites all four virtues.

Ah! To comprehend the great beginning is to fathom transformation; to encompass Heaven’s virtue is to fathom the numinous. This is the utmost subtlety of Qian’s primal principle. How great it is! The Commentary on the Judgments rightly praises it. Moreover, this is what is called the Way of the ruler. The Spring and Autumn Annals links the king to Heaven: “first month” follows “king,” and “king” follows “spring.” For the primal principle is Heaven’s benevolent vital force. Heaven does not speak, yet the various things flourish and the year’s work is accomplished: this is the work of the primal principle. The four seasons and five phases merely diffuse its vital force. The sage takes no deliberate action, yet every undertaking flourishes and the work of government is accomplished: this too is the work of the primal principle. The Four Mountain Chiefs and nine officials merely assist in its functions. Thus embodying the primal principle and occupying the rightful position is how the sage king models himself on Heaven. Looking to Qian’s primal principle makes this meaning still clearer. Hence the saying, “The sage and August Heaven share a single Way.” How true!

“Transform them through numinous efficacy, and enable the people to find it fitting.”
By Liu Shouren.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor:
The subtlety with which the sage adapts to change and keeps the people from growing weary lies precisely in transforming through numinous efficacy and making this fitting for the people. The candidates [?] cannot grasp this intimately; they mostly rely on memorization and imitation, multiplying words while only obscuring the meaning. Only this…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
篇脫去俗態不落時文常套佳作也
考試官學正吳　批　〔淸勁讀之灑然〕
考試官教授吳　批　〔文氣疏達〕
聖人妙於治而天下安之可以見其盛矣蓋化
之弗神者未必其民之安之也神則能使天下
順治矣玆聖帝之所以爲獨盛與大傳論聖人
制器尚象而及此意謂古者聖王之繼天而治
也皆因時以立政而弗强民以難從黃帝堯舜
所以通其變使民不倦者夫何爲哉吾知順風
===
氣之宜顯之於經綸者神妙莫測而以自然爲
功知太朴之散施之於化導者神應無方而以
不勞爲用質敝而救之以文非故强之也時之
既至道不相沿惟隨時變易焉耳聖人無心也
俗儉而示之以禮非有矯之也世之所趨禮不
相襲惟與世推移焉耳聖人何與也神而化之
如此民其有不宜之者耶蓋法之制於上也既
緣人情以設敎故民之從於下也自順帝則而
不知喜其文之足尚而相率以成風者翕如也
punctuated:
篇脫去俗態，不落時文常套，佳作也。
考試官學正吳，批：〔淸勁，讀之灑然。〕
考試官教授吳，批：〔文氣疏達。〕
聖人妙於治而天下安之，可以見其盛矣。蓋化之弗神者，未必其民之安之也；神則能使天下順治矣。玆聖帝之所以爲獨盛與！大傳論聖人制器尚象而及此，意謂古者聖王之繼天而治也，皆因時以立政，而弗强民以難從。黃帝堯舜所以通其變，使民不倦者，夫何爲哉？吾知順風氣之宜，顯之於經綸者，神妙莫測，而以自然爲功；知太朴之散，施之於化導者，神應無方，而以不勞爲用。質敝而救之以文，非故强之也；時之既至，道不相沿，惟隨時變易焉耳，聖人無心也。俗儉而示之以禮，非有矯之也；世之所趨，禮不相襲，惟與世推移焉耳，聖人何與也？神而化之如此，民其有不宜之者耶？蓋法之制於上也，既緣人情以設敎，故民之從於下也，自順帝則而不知。喜其文之足尚，而相率以成風者，翕如也。
translation_en:
…this essay sheds commonplace mannerisms and avoids the conventional formulas of contemporary examination prose. It is an excellent work.
Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and vigorous; reading it leaves one refreshed.〕
Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: 〔The prose flows freely and expansively.〕
The sage governs with wondrous skill, and all under Heaven rest content in his rule: here we can see his greatness. For transformation that lacks spiritual efficacy does not necessarily bring the people contentment; with such efficacy, however, one can bring all under Heaven into harmonious order. Is this not what makes the sage emperors uniquely great? The Great Commentary, discussing how the sages fashioned implements by taking the images as their models, reaches this point. Its meaning is that the sage kings of antiquity, carrying on Heaven’s work in their government, all established policies according to the times and did not force upon the people what was difficult to follow. What, then, were Huangdi, Yao, and Shun doing when they adapted institutions through change and kept the people from growing weary? I understand that, by following what suited the prevailing temper of the age, they manifested in their ordering of affairs a spiritual subtlety beyond fathoming, achieving their results through naturalness. Recognizing that primordial simplicity had dispersed, they brought to their transforming guidance a spiritual responsiveness unrestricted by any fixed method, accomplishing its work without toil. When simplicity became defective, they remedied it with refinement; they were not deliberately imposing constraints. The time for change had arrived, and the ways of government could not simply be carried forward unchanged: they merely altered them with the times. The sage had no private intention in this. When customs were spare, they showed the people ritual; they were not intentionally forcing a correction. Given the direction of the age, rites could not simply be inherited unchanged: they merely shifted with the world. What personal intervention did the sage make? With transformation accomplished through spiritual efficacy in this way, could any among the people fail to find it fitting? For when laws were established above, instruction was already founded upon human feelings; thus, when the people complied below, they naturally followed the emperor’s standards without knowing it. Delighting in refinement as worthy of esteem, they led one another to make it customary, joining together in harmony…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
是雖民之各從其欲若或有以使之者矣樂其
禮之可嘉而相安以同俗者謞如也是雖民之
各適其性若或有以鼓之者矣吁觀神化則知
通變之妙觀民宜則知不倦之機非聖人而能
若是乎大柢法之敝也風之會起之也文質易
尚如循環然要不可拘者當黄帝堯舜適文明
之會去榛狉之俗遠矣故衣裳之制取諸乾坤
其亦風之會乎如十三卦古聖人制器尚象者
皆時之所爲也爲其所當爲民習而安之矣是
以垂衣裳而天下治也嗚呼三聖之法備矣後
有作者其弗可及也與
===
書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭黄 批
〔題本渾融作者多於願爲帝臣發揮欠當是篇思緻精密詞理懇到虞廷得人氣象宛然在目矣佳〕
士佳士
考試官學正吳 批
〔黎獻即忠直挑剔明盡〕
punctuated:
是雖民之各從其欲，若或有以使之者矣。樂其禮之可嘉，而相安以同俗者謞如也。是雖民之各適其性，若或有以鼓之者矣。吁！觀神化，則知通變之妙；觀民宜，則知不倦之機。非聖人而能若是乎？大柢法之敝也，風之會起之也。文質易尚，如循環然，要不可拘者。當黄帝堯舜適文明之會，去榛狉之俗遠矣，故衣裳之制取諸乾坤，其亦風之會乎？如十三卦，古聖人制器尚象者，皆時之所爲也。爲其所當爲，民習而安之矣，是以垂衣裳而天下治也。嗚呼！三聖之法備矣，後有作者，其弗可及也與！

書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣。
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭黄批〔題本渾融，作者多於願爲帝臣發揮，欠當。是篇思緻精密，詞理懇到，虞廷得人氣象宛然在目矣。佳〕
士佳士。
考試官學正吳批〔黎獻即忠直，挑剔明盡。〕
translation_en:
…Although the people each follow their own desires, it is as though something were directing them. Delighting in the excellence of these rites, they settle contentedly into shared customs with exuberant accord [?]. Although the people each find satisfaction in their own nature, it is as though something were inspiring them. Ah! In observing this wondrous transformation, one recognizes the subtlety of adapting to change; in observing how well the people are suited, one recognizes the workings of tireless activity. Could anyone but a sage accomplish this?

Generally, when institutions become worn out, a convergence of prevailing influences revives them. Refinement and simplicity alternate as the objects of esteem, like a revolving cycle; the essential point is that one must not adhere rigidly to either. When Huangdi, Yao, and Shun encountered an age of cultural illumination, the customs of wilderness life had long been left behind. Thus the institution of upper and lower garments took its pattern from Qian and Kun. Was this not also a convergence of prevailing influences? As with the thirteen hexagrams, the ancient sages’ fashioning of implements in accordance with the images was entirely a response to the times. They did what ought to be done, and the people became accustomed to it and found contentment in it. Thus they let their robes hang down, and all under Heaven was well governed. Alas! The institutions of the three sages were complete. Could those who arose afterward ever equal them?
