“The worthy men of the myriad states all wished to be the emperor’s servants.”

Pan Yunxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor (jiaoyu): 〔The topic is fundamentally an integrated whole. Most writers elaborate on the wish to become the emperor’s servants, which is not quite appropriate. This essay’s thought is subtle and precise, its language and reasoning earnest and thorough. The scene of the court of Shun securing worthy men appears vividly before our eyes. Excellent.〕

A scholar, a fine scholar [?].

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor (xuezheng): 〔“The worthy men” means those who are loyal and upright. The distinctions are drawn clearly and exhaustively.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授吳　批〔精細純雅〕
盡天下之賢而樂爲之用君德之所感者深矣
蓋賢者用世之心相時而動者也今咸有帝臣
之願焉非聖德有以感之而能然乎昔禹告舜
之意若曰致治莫大於用賢而感化莫先於修
德誠使帝德之光至於海隅蒼生則其得於觀
感者當何如哉將見黎獻之生於時者夫固潛
德而隱也今也瞻帝德之重華而欲用世以自
見衆賢之伏於野者夫固見可而進也今也仰
===
聖人之在上而欲乘時以有爲至德光被乎萬
方則丕應允翕乎衆忘必將曰茲誠不世之遇
也而可上負吾君矣乎德輝無遠而弗屆則感
通不疾而自速必將曰茲適大行之會也而可
下負所學矣乎或以抱堅貞之節恩有以盡其
忠竭股肱耳目之力以成亮工熙載之業殆畎
畝之所預待者矣或以秉精白之操思有以效
其直際都俞吁咈之盛以賛謨明弼諧之風固
身心之所深慶者矣跡未離於側陋而志已期
punctuated:
考試官教授吳批〔精細純雅〕

盡天下之賢而樂爲之用，君德之所感者深矣。

蓋賢者用世之心，相時而動者也。今咸有帝臣之願焉，非聖德有以感之而能然乎？昔禹告舜之意若曰：致治莫大於用賢，而感化莫先於修德。誠使帝德之光至於海隅蒼生，則其得於觀感者當何如哉？將見黎獻之生於時者，夫固潛德而隱也，今也瞻帝德之重華，而欲用世以自見；衆賢之伏於野者，夫固見可而進也，今也仰聖人之在上，而欲乘時以有爲。至德光被乎萬方，則丕應允翕乎衆忘，必將曰：「茲誠不世之遇也，而可上負吾君矣乎？」德輝無遠而弗屆，則感通不疾而自速，必將曰：「茲適大行之會也，而可下負所學矣乎？」或以抱堅貞之節，恩有以盡其忠，竭股肱耳目之力，以成亮工熙載之業，殆畎畝之所預待者矣；或以秉精白之操，思有以效其直，際都俞吁咈之盛，以賛謨明弼諧之風，固身心之所深慶者矣。跡未離於側陋，而志已期
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔Meticulous, pure, and elegant.〕

When all the worthy men throughout the realm delight in serving their ruler, profound indeed is the influence of his virtue.

Worthy men, in their desire to serve the world, assess the times before acting. Now they all wish to become the emperor’s ministers. Could this occur unless sagely virtue had moved them? What Yu once told Shun meant something like this: nothing is greater in achieving good government than employing worthy men, and nothing takes precedence in morally transforming others over cultivating virtue. If the radiance of imperial virtue truly reaches the common people in the remotest coastal regions, what must they gain from witnessing it and being moved by it?

We shall see worthy men born among the common people in this age, who had concealed their virtue and lived in retirement, now beholding the renewed splendor of imperial virtue and wishing to serve the world and make themselves known. The many worthy men dwelling unnoticed in the countryside, who would advance only when they saw a fitting opportunity, now look up to the sage occupying the throne and wish to seize the moment to accomplish something. When the radiance of consummate virtue envelops every region, it evokes a mighty response and truly unites the hopes of all [?]. They will surely say: “This is indeed an opportunity seldom encountered in any age. Could we fail our ruler above?” When virtue’s brilliance reaches everywhere, however distant, its moving influence spreads swiftly without haste. They will surely say: “This is precisely the occasion for putting our principles fully into practice. Could we, for our part, betray what we have learned?”

Some, holding steadfastly to their integrity, seek [?] a means to fulfill their loyalty. They exhaust their strength as the ruler’s limbs, eyes, and ears, helping accomplish the work of faithfully discharging duties and making every undertaking flourish. This is surely what they have anticipated while living among the fields. Others, maintaining conduct of unblemished purity, think of ways to demonstrate their uprightness. Encountering a flourishing age in which ruler and ministers freely assent and remonstrate, they help sustain a tradition of enlightened counsel and harmonious assistance. This is indeed something they celebrate profoundly in body and mind. Though they have not yet left their obscure and humble surroundings, their aspirations already look toward…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
於奔虒違違焉將慮從事之或失矣而寧俟於
四門之闢哉向雖樂於潛居而今則殷於許國
汲汲焉惟恐聖世之或遺矣而奚憂於庶官之
曠哉至是舉用之典行而比遜之化洽彼頑讒
者且胥爲黎獻矣明德之效若是其大夫豈也
恐足以與此抑考帝舜之時凡德咸事俊乂在
官而好生之仁罔愆之德固已洽民心而徧海
隅矣而禹也拳拳以明德致賢爲言者良以聖
世之治以德化爲極而人臣事君無已之心當
如是也迨禹三苗之征益復贊之以脩德其旨
若相授受焉虞廷之事君其萬世人臣之準也
與
===
會其有極歸其有極
楊燔
同考試官教諭李　批〔會歸二字乃王言訓人切要者最難形容是作詞氣悠揚旨趣雋永非有心得之學者不能〕
考試官學正吳　批〔詞雅理切得諷詠體〕
考試官教授吳　批〔縝密精純〕
punctuated:
於奔虒，違違焉將慮從事之或失矣，而寧俟於四門之闢哉？向雖樂於潛居，而今則殷於許國，汲汲焉惟恐聖世之或遺矣，而奚憂於庶官之曠哉？至是，舉用之典行，而比遜之化洽，彼頑讒者且胥爲黎獻矣。明德之效若是其大，夫豈也恐足以與此？抑考帝舜之時，凡德咸事，俊乂在官，而好生之仁、罔愆之德，固已洽民心而徧海隅矣。而禹也拳拳以明德致賢爲言者，良以聖世之治以德化爲極，而人臣事君無已之心當如是也。迨禹三苗之征，益復贊之以脩德，其旨若相授受焉。虞廷之事君，其萬世人臣之準也與！

會其有極，歸其有極。
楊燔
同考試官教諭李　批〔會歸二字乃王言訓人切要者，最難形容。是作詞氣悠揚，旨趣雋永，非有心得之學者不能。〕
考試官學正吳　批〔詞雅理切，得諷詠體。〕
考試官教授吳　批〔縝密精純。〕
translation_en:
…on hastening into service [?]. Anxiously [?], they would worry that they might err in carrying out their duties; how could they wait for the opening of the four gates? Though formerly they delighted in living in retirement, now they are earnest in pledging themselves to the state. Eagerly, they fear only that they might be overlooked in this sage age; why, then, worry that the various offices will remain vacant? At this point, the established practice of selecting and appointing men is carried out, and the transforming influence of harmony and deference spreads everywhere. Even the obstinate and slanderous will all become worthy men among the people. So great is the efficacy of manifesting virtue! Could [an unclear phrase] suffice to match this [?]?

Yet consider the time of Emperor Shun: all men of virtue served, and men of outstanding ability held office. His benevolence in cherishing life and his faultless virtue had already won the people’s hearts and extended to the remotest shores. That Yu nevertheless spoke so earnestly of manifesting virtue to attract worthy men was truly because government in a sage age takes transformation through virtue as its highest attainment, and because a minister’s unceasing devotion in serving his ruler ought to be like this. When Yu undertook his campaign against the Sanmiao, Yi again assisted him with counsel to cultivate virtue. Their purport seems to have been handed down from one to the other. Surely the manner of serving the ruler at Shun’s court is the model for ministers in all ages!

“Assemble around the Ultimate Standard; return to the Ultimate Standard.”
By Yang Fan.

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The two words ‘assemble’ and ‘return’ are crucial to the king’s words of instruction to his people and are exceptionally difficult to express fully. This composition’s language and cadence are flowing and resonant, and its meaning has lasting savor. Only a scholar with understanding gained through personal reflection could achieve this.”

Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The language is elegant and the reasoning apt; it achieves the manner of expressive recitation.”

Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: “Closely wrought, meticulous, refined, and pure.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
王者約言以訓人欲其知所趨而得所止也蓋
皇極之理臣民之所當共守者也會之歸之則
與極爲一矣敷言之訓何其善哉昔箕子衍之
以告武王也意謂人君繼天而爲皇極之主也
固當率之以身而端感化之本亦必誘之以言
而妙鼓舞之機敷言以訓臣民固有以節其淫
比而示之標準矣然未必其能會而歸之也乃
復訓之曰王義王道王路此皇極之用而人之
所共由者也惟存之於心者未能無邪思斯從
入之途乖矣凡我臣民尚會其有極矣乎審幾
於一念之微而向往惟勤求合乎大中至正之
矩辨志於羣動之先而進脩匪懈率循乎民彝
物則之常偏陂之皆忘翕然王義之遵惟恐後
也好惡之不作確然道路之由無敢渝也蓋有
其人不同其趨則一者矣寧可志惑於他岐而
不知所以會之也哉不但已也蕩蕩平平正直
此皇極之體而人之所同具者也惟見之於事
者未能無邪行斯歸宿之地遠矣凡我臣民尚
punctuated: 王者約言以訓人，欲其知所趨而得所止也。蓋皇極之理，臣民之所當共守者也。會之歸之，則與極爲一矣。敷言之訓，何其善哉！昔箕子衍之以告武王也，意謂人君繼天而爲皇極之主也，固當率之以身而端感化之本，亦必誘之以言而妙鼓舞之機。敷言以訓臣民，固有以節其淫比而示之標準矣，然未必其能會而歸之也。乃復訓之曰：「王義、王道、王路，此皇極之用而人之所共由者也。惟存之於心者未能無邪思，斯從入之途乖矣。凡我臣民，尚會其有極矣乎！審幾於一念之微，而向往惟勤，求合乎大中至正之矩；辨志於羣動之先，而進脩匪懈，率循乎民彝物則之常。偏陂之皆忘，翕然王義之遵，惟恐後也；好惡之不作，確然道路之由，無敢渝也。蓋有其人不同，其趨則一者矣。寧可志惑於他岐，而不知所以會之也哉！不但已也，蕩蕩、平平、正直，此皇極之體而人之所同具者也。惟見之於事者未能無邪行，斯歸宿之地遠矣。凡我臣民，尚
translation_en:
The king instructs people in concise words, wishing them to know what to pursue and to attain the proper place of rest. For the principle of the supreme standard (huangji) is what subjects and people alike ought to uphold. By converging upon it and returning to it, they become one with that standard. How excellent is the instruction conveyed through these pronouncements!

Long ago, Jizi elaborated upon this in advising King Wu. His meaning was that the ruler succeeds Heaven as master of the supreme standard. Certainly he ought to lead people by his own conduct, setting right the foundation of their moral transformation; he must also guide them through words, making skillful use of the means of inspiring them. By issuing pronouncements to instruct his subjects and people, he can indeed restrain their excessive partisanship and show them a standard. Yet this does not necessarily mean that they can converge upon it and return to it. Thus he further instructs them, saying:

“The king’s righteousness, the king’s Way, and the king’s road: these are the functioning of the supreme standard and what all people should follow together. Yet, insofar as what they harbor in their hearts is not free of wayward thoughts, their path of entry goes astray. May all my subjects and people converge upon the supreme standard! Discern the first stirrings within the subtlety of a single thought, and diligently direct your aspirations toward it, seeking accord with the rule of perfect centrality and utmost rectitude. Clarify your intent before the many activities begin, and advance in self-cultivation without slackening, following the constant norms of human relationships and the principles inherent in things. Forget all partiality and bias, and with one accord follow the king’s righteousness, fearing only that you may lag behind. Let no personal likes or dislikes arise, and steadfastly follow the Way and the road, never daring to deviate. Though people differ, what they pursue is one. How could you allow your intentions to be confused by divergent paths and fail to understand how to converge upon the standard?

“Nor is this all. Breadth, evenness, and uprightness: these are the substance of the supreme standard, which all people alike possess. Yet, insofar as what they manifest in their affairs is not free of wayward conduct, their ultimate resting place remains distant. May all my subjects and people …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
歸其有極矣乎密深造之功所以共適於彝倫
者務止於至善而不遷協克一之守所以會通
於典禮者務與之渾融而無間偏黨以除而蕩
蕩平平之蘊悉窮其奧也反側以去而正直無
私之理咸詣其極也蓋有其行不同其究則一
者矣寧可功畫於半途而不知所以歸之也哉
夫先之以會極所以開歸極之始繼之以歸極
所以收會極之終王者敷言之訓始終以要其
成反復以致其意諷詠興而孚化速矣彝倫之
===
攸敘也不有由哉雖然此非徒以言語教人也
蓋建極而後使之歸極斂福而後可以錫福至
於念之受之富之羞之亦既勤且勞矣宜會歸
之易而贊頌之神也與故觀於斂時五福之言
而知建極之動天觀於于帝其訓之言而知敷
言之達天噫皇極之君其配天也夫
詩
殖殖其庭有覺其楹噲噲其正噦噦其冥
君子攸寧
punctuated:
歸其有極矣乎？密深造之功，所以共適於彝倫者，務止於至善而不遷；協克一之守，所以會通於典禮者，務與之渾融而無間。偏黨以除，而蕩蕩平平之蘊悉窮其奧也；反側以去，而正直無私之理咸詣其極也。蓋有其行不同，其究則一者矣，寧可功畫於半途，而不知所以歸之也哉？夫先之以會極，所以開歸極之始；繼之以歸極，所以收會極之終。王者敷言之訓，始終以要其成，反復以致其意，諷詠興而孚化速矣。彝倫之攸敘也，不有由哉？雖然，此非徒以言語教人也。蓋建極而後使之歸極，斂福而後可以錫福。至於念之、受之、富之、羞之，亦既勤且勞矣。宜會歸之易而贊頌之神也與！故觀於「斂時五福」之言，而知建極之動天；觀於「于帝其訓」之言，而知敷言之達天。噫！皇極之君，其配天也夫！

詩

殖殖其庭，有覺其楹。噲噲其正，噦噦其冥，君子攸寧。
translation_en:
…return to the standard they possess? They must intensify their efforts toward profound attainment, so that, advancing together toward the enduring moral relationships, they rest in the highest good without departing from it. They must harmonize their commitment to unity, so that, comprehending established norms and rites, they become wholly integrated with them, without any separation. With partiality and factionalism eliminated, they fully fathom the deepest meaning of breadth and evenness; with perversity and instability removed, they all reach the utmost realization of uprightness and impartiality. Though their conduct differs, its ultimate destination is one. How could they halt their efforts halfway and fail to understand how to return to it?

First, gathering at the standard opens the way for returning to it; then, returning to the standard completes the process of gathering at it. In the instruction conveyed through the king’s pronouncements, beginning and end alike aim at fulfillment, while repetition fully expresses his intent. Recitation flourishes, and sincere moral transformation proceeds swiftly. Is there not, then, a reason why the enduring moral relationships come to be properly ordered?

Yet this is not merely teaching people through words. Only after establishing the standard can he cause them to return to it; only after gathering blessings can he bestow them. As for keeping them in mind, receiving them, enriching them, and sustaining them, he has indeed been diligent and painstaking. It is fitting that they should readily gather and return, and that their praise should be so wondrous! Thus, from the words “gather these five blessings,” we know that establishing the standard moves Heaven; from the words “the Supreme Lord’s instruction,” we know that the promulgation of his words reaches Heaven. Ah! The ruler who embodies the August Standard is indeed a counterpart to Heaven!

Book of Odes

Level and even is its courtyard;
Lofty are its pillars.
Spacious and bright are its principal halls;
Deep and secluded are its inner chambers.
Here the noble lord rests in peace.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正吳　批
粟永壽〔制度題難於整齊此作詞不費〕
〔而意已足取之〕
考試官教授吳　批〔詩人為愛之誠讀之尚可想見〕
王者之室備衆美而所居之安在是矣夫作室
以安居其制誠不可以不備也詩人於落成而
美之不可以見中興之氣象乎想其意蓋謂人
君欲以敷外　王之業必先豫內聖之體堂陛之
制既已崇矣其室之美何如哉是故以言其庭
===
則殖殖無頗而矩度之施有以協端平之範也
以言其楹則覺然直大而樸斲之美足以示宣
朗之觀也向明之處謂之正令則天啓光華洞
達而不蔽何如其噲噲矣乎奧窔之間謂之冥
令則地當宥密深廣而莫窺何如其噦噦矣乎
夫庭楹盡制既有以宏大壯之規冥正咸宜又
有以萃元和之氣是誠足以為君子之攸寧者
矣蓋必適萬機之既暇而燕閒於斯以養其恭
默之度當庶事之惟康而游息於斯以紓其日
punctuated:
考試官學正吳批。
粟永壽〔制度題難於整齊，此作詞不費〕〔而意已足，取之。〕
考試官教授吳批〔詩人為愛之誠，讀之尚可想見。〕
王者之室備衆美，而所居之安在是矣。夫作室以安居，其制誠不可以不備也。詩人於落成而美之，不可以見中興之氣象乎？想其意，蓋謂人君欲以敷外王之業，必先豫內聖之體。堂陛之制既已崇矣，其室之美何如哉？是故以言其庭，則殖殖無頗，而矩度之施有以協端平之範也；以言其楹，則覺然直大，而樸斲之美足以示宣朗之觀也。向明之處謂之正，令則天啓光華，洞達而不蔽，何如其噲噲矣乎！奧窔之間謂之冥，令則地當宥密，深廣而莫窺，何如其噦噦矣乎！夫庭楹盡制，既有以宏大壯之規；冥正咸宜，又有以萃元和之氣。是誠足以為君子之攸寧者矣。蓋必適萬機之既暇，而燕閒於斯，以養其恭默之度；當庶事之惟康，而游息於斯，以紓其日
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor.
Su Yongshou. 〔A topic concerning architectural arrangements is difficult to handle with orderly balance. This composition uses words economically〕〔yet conveys its meaning fully. Accept it.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: 〔The sincerity of the poet’s affection can still be imagined when one reads this.〕
The king’s residence possesses every beauty, and herein lies the peacefulness of his dwelling. When building a residence in which to dwell at ease, its arrangements must indeed be complete. The poet praises it upon its completion: can we not discern in this the signs of a dynastic resurgence? His meaning, I imagine, is that a ruler who wishes to extend his outward achievement as king must first prepare his inward foundation as sage. The arrangement of hall and steps is already imposing; how beautiful, then, must his residence be! Thus, speaking of its courtyard, it is level and without slope, and the application of measurements accords with the standard of uprightness and evenness. Speaking of its pillars, they rise straight and tall, and the beauty of their hewn timber suffices to present a spacious, bright prospect. The part facing the light is called the front hall. Here [?], Heaven opens its radiance, which penetrates everywhere without obstruction: how spacious it is! The recesses in the corners are called the dark interior. Here [?], the place is secluded and tranquil, deep and broad beyond what the eye can fathom: how profound it is! The courtyard and pillars fully realize their proper design, giving grandeur to the plan of magnificent strength; the dark interior and bright front hall are both fittingly arranged, gathering the vital breath of primal harmony. This is truly sufficient to be the place where the noble lord rests at ease. Surely, when he has leisure from the myriad affairs of government, he will repose here to cultivate his demeanor of reverence and quietude; when all affairs are well ordered, he will rest and relax here to ease his daily …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
吳之勞輪奐一新正際夫景運方興之日蓋非
徒郎安筦簟而翕受貞元以培萬年之基者固
一人凝命之所矣規畫大備適當夫海宇熙洽
之時蓋非但流光祚僞而宣節和氣以養壽命
之原者固天子有那之居矣夫作室已極其揚
厲之盛而攸寧又寓夫頌禱之誠斯干詩人其
忠愛之至乎抑宣王何以得此於民哉蓋其中
興之政首以還定安集爲務鴻鴈之歌已先乎
鳥革翬飛之詠矣故百堵雖勞皆以上承乎作
===
豐宅鎬之舊而小民之勸工詩人之祝頌有靈
臺之懿範焉周之世德然也是故厚下安宅人
君惟慎所以感民者
莫敢不來享莫敢不來王曰商是常
楊相
考試官學正吳　批〔塲中作此題者王曰商是常處〕
〔語脉不貫是作發明精到寫出氏羌事商之誠可與言詩矣〕
考試官教授吳　批〔清新雅〕
〔健〕
商王郎遠人之朝貢而述其意所以嚴責荊之
punctuated:
吳之勞，輪奐一新，正際夫景運方興之日。蓋非徒郎安筦簟，而翕受貞元，以培萬年之基者，固一人凝命之所矣。規畫大備，適當夫海宇熙洽之時。蓋非但流光祚僞，而宣節和氣，以養壽命之原者，固天子有那之居矣。夫作室已極其揚厲之盛，而攸寧又寓夫頌禱之誠，《斯干》詩人其忠愛之至乎！抑宣王何以得此於民哉？蓋其中興之政，首以還定安集爲務，《鴻鴈》之歌已先乎鳥革翬飛之詠矣。故百堵雖勞，皆以上承乎作豐宅鎬之舊，而小民之勸工、詩人之祝頌，有《靈臺》之懿範焉。周之世德然也是故厚下安宅，人君惟慎所以感民者。
莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。
楊相
考試官學正吳　批〔塲中作此題者王曰商是常處〕〔語脉不貫是作發明精到寫出氏羌事商之誠可與言詩矣〕
考試官教授吳　批〔清新雅〕〔健〕
商王郎遠人之朝貢而述其意，所以嚴責荊之義也。
translation_en:
…the toil of the late afternoon [?]. Its grandeur and beauty are wholly renewed, just as an auspicious age begins to flourish. This is surely not merely a place for resting comfortably upon rush and bamboo mats [?]: by gathering in the powers of constancy and renewal to establish a foundation for ten thousand years, it is indeed where the One Man consolidates Heaven’s mandate. Its planning is fully accomplished precisely when the realm enjoys peace and harmony. Surely it does not merely transmit glory and blessings [?]: by circulating and regulating harmonious vital energy to nourish the source of longevity, it is indeed the Son of Heaven’s spacious dwelling.
The building of the palace already displays magnificence to the utmost, while the words about dwelling there in peace also convey sincere praise and prayer. How consummate was the loyal affection of the poet of “Si Gan” (“The River Banks”)! Yet how did King Xuan win such feelings from his people? In his measures for restoring the dynasty, he made settling and gathering the people in peace his first concern. The song “Hong Yan” (“Wild Geese”) thus preceded the verses describing the palace as a bird spreading its wings and a pheasant taking flight. Although the many walls required toil, the undertaking continued the ancient precedent of building Feng and residing at Hao. The common people’s eagerness to work and the poet’s blessings and praise followed the admirable example of “Ling Tai” (“The Numinous Terrace”). Such was the effect of Zhou’s virtue accumulated over generations. Therefore, to treat those below generously and secure his dwelling, a ruler must attend carefully to how he moves his people.
“None dares fail to come with offerings; none dares fail to come to court, saying: ‘Shang’s rule is constant.’”
Yang Xiang.
Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: “Among those who addressed this topic in the examination hall, the wording at ‘come to court, saying: Shang’s rule is constant’ lacked continuity of sense. This essay elucidates it with precision and fully conveys the sincerity with which the Di [?] and Qiang served Shang. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss the Odes.”
Examiner Wu, a Professor, comments: “Fresh, elegant, and vigorous.”
The king of Shang drew upon [?] the tribute visits of distant peoples and expressed their intentions, thereby setting forth the grounds for sternly rebuking Jing.…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
義也夫朝貢之典王者大一統之制也氐羌且
弗違焉而況荆人乎宜商王舉是以責之也歟
此商人追頌高宗中興之烈及此若曰內夏外
夷者天下之大防也以夷事夏者尊王之大義
也爾荆之不庭久矣獨不觀氐羌之事我成湯
者乎是故備物以貢謂之享先王則壤以賦中
邦似無取乎氐羌之享也彼則賓服之志素懾
於神武之威故歲事之脩自效其奉上之義庭
實於是而供焉方物於是而獻焉惴惴然莫之
===
敢後矣孰有不來享者哉奕世而朝謂之王先
王輯瑞以聯百辟似不賫乎氐羌之王也彼則
內附之心素慕乎綏猷之化故載見之儀恪遵
於繼序之時請命以紹其封焉入覲以稟其度
焉兢兢乎莫之敢違矣孰有不來王者哉若是
者非僞爲也稽於其言而可見其誠矣彼其意
曰天朝如彼其尊也以卑承尊商之常禮也我
之所以來享者乃率由其舊焉耳蓋受之先人
而與商固相爲世守者矣敢爲不恭而自悖其
punctuated: 義也。夫朝貢之典，王者大一統之制也。氐羌且弗違焉，而況荆人乎？宜商王舉是以責之也歟！此商人追頌高宗中興之烈，及此若曰：「內夏外夷者，天下之大防也；以夷事夏者，尊王之大義也。爾荆之不庭久矣，獨不觀氐羌之事我成湯者乎？是故備物以貢謂之享。先王則壤以賦中邦，似無取乎氐羌之享也。彼則賓服之志，素懾於神武之威，故歲事之脩，自效其奉上之義。庭實於是而供焉，方物於是而獻焉，惴惴然莫之敢後矣，孰有不來享者哉？奕世而朝謂之王。先王輯瑞以聯百辟，似不賫乎氐羌之王也。彼則內附之心，素慕乎綏猷之化，故載見之儀，恪遵於繼序之時。請命以紹其封焉，入覲以稟其度焉，兢兢乎莫之敢違矣，孰有不來王者哉？若是者，非僞爲也。稽於其言，而可見其誠矣。彼其意曰：『天朝如彼其尊也，以卑承尊，商之常禮也。我之所以來享者，乃率由其舊焉耳。蓋受之先人，而與商固相爲世守者矣，敢爲不恭而自悖其
translation_en:
…the principle involved. The institutions of court attendance and tribute are the means by which a king establishes comprehensive unity. Even the Di and Qiang do not transgress them; how much less should the people of Jing! Surely the Shang king was justified in invoking their example to reproach Jing! Here the people of Shang, retrospectively praising the achievements of Gaozong’s restoration, speak as though saying: “To treat the Xia as within and the Yi as without is the great dividing line of the realm; for the Yi to serve the Xia is the great duty of honoring the king. You people of Jing have long failed to attend court. Have you alone not observed how the Di and Qiang served our Cheng Tang?
“To furnish goods as tribute is called ‘presenting offerings.’ The former kings assessed the soil to levy taxes upon the central lands, seemingly having no need of offerings from the Di and Qiang. Yet their resolve to submit had long been inspired by awe of the kings’ divine martial might. Thus, in fulfilling their annual obligations, they demonstrated their own commitment to serving their superiors. They supplied the gifts displayed in the court and presented the products of their regions. Anxiously, none dared fall behind. Who among them failed to come and present offerings?
“To attend court generation after generation is called ‘acknowledging the king.’ The former kings gathered the jade credentials to bind together the many lords, seemingly having no need for [?] the Di and Qiang to acknowledge their kingship. Yet their desire to submit had long been inspired by admiration for the transforming influence of the kings’ pacifying policies. Thus they reverently observed the rites of renewed audience whenever a successor inherited his position. They requested royal commands to succeed to their enfeoffments and entered court to receive the king’s standards. Vigilantly, none dared transgress. Who among them failed to come and acknowledge the king?
“Such conduct was no pretense. Examine their words, and their sincerity becomes apparent. Their meaning was this: ‘So exalted is the celestial court! For the lowly to serve the exalted is the enduring ritual norm of Shang. Our coming to present offerings merely follows established precedent. We received this practice from our forebears, and we and Shang have steadfastly maintained it together through the generations. Would we dare act disrespectfully and ourselves violate its …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
禮乎中國如彼其大也以小事大商之常禮也
我之所以來王者乃秪盡其分焉耳蓋傳之子
孫而與商固相爲悠久者矣敢爲不臣而自廢
其常乎斯蓋甘心臣服而形之於言者無慢詞
故委質率從而見之於禮者皆實意茲固成湯
之德足以感召而氐羌之向化亦可嘉矣爾荆
人今乃不然焉豈能免於肆伐也哉嘗論先王
之世有不享則脩德有不王則脩文何武丁之
於荆也而遂以征討加之蓋以其國猶在侯服
===
之内首阻聲教王法之所不容者也故授祖宗
之服遠者以責之無非屈其心俾歸於化也豈
曰黷武云乎哉故誦殷武之詩而知商王中興
之盛
春秋
秋齊侯宋公江人黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯
鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于
陘〔僖公四年〕
punctuated:
禮乎？中國如彼其大也，以小事大，商之常禮也。我之所以來王者，乃秪盡其分焉耳。蓋傳之子孫，而與商固相爲悠久者矣，敢爲不臣而自廢其常乎？」斯蓋甘心臣服而形之於言者無慢詞，故委質率從而見之於禮者皆實意。茲固成湯之德足以感召，而氐羌之向化亦可嘉矣。爾荆人今乃不然焉，豈能免於肆伐也哉？嘗論先王之世，有不享則脩德，有不王則脩文。何武丁之於荆也，而遂以征討加之？蓋以其國猶在侯服之内，首阻聲教，王法之所不容者也。故授祖宗之服遠者以責之，無非屈其心，俾歸於化也，豈曰黷武云乎哉？故誦《殷武》之詩，而知商王中興之盛。

春秋

秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黄人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕

春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。〔僖公四年〕
translation_en:
…the rites? The central realm is so great: for the small to serve the great is the enduring ritual order of Shang. Our coming to acknowledge its king merely fulfills our proper duty. This duty is transmitted to our descendants, and our relationship with Shang is assuredly one of lasting duration. Would we dare to act as disloyal subjects and ourselves abandon this constant rule?”

These words express a willing submission, without a trace of insolence. Thus their acts of pledging allegiance and obediently following, manifested in ritual observances, all express sincere intentions. Certainly Cheng Tang’s virtue was sufficient to move and draw them to him, but the Di and Qiang peoples’ acceptance of his transforming influence also deserves praise. Yet you people of Jing now behave otherwise. How could you escape a punitive campaign?

I have reflected that, in the age of the former kings, when some failed to present offerings, the kings cultivated their virtue; when some failed to acknowledge their kingship, they cultivated their civil accomplishments. Why, then, did Wu Ding immediately subject Jing to a punitive expedition? It was because that state lay within the feudatories’ zone of service, yet took the lead in obstructing royal instruction—something the king’s law could not tolerate. Thus he invoked [?] his ancestors’ success in securing the submission of distant peoples to reproach them. His sole purpose was to humble their hearts and bring them within his transforming influence. How could this be called wanton militarism? Thus, in reciting the ode “Martial Might of Yin” (Yin wu), we recognize the splendor of the Shang king’s restoration.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
王儒
同考試官教諭徐　批　〔齊桓克敵制勝之謀當歸重於　結江黄以爲奇兵上傳意自明士子類作此合殊失輕昂是篇意中　肯綮且文思俊逸氣勢弘大讀之令人灑然夫非蘊藉之深者耶高〕
薦允宜
考試官學正吳　批　〔平順而敷腴非苟作者〕
考試官教授吳　批　〔文有思致高取〕
霸主定奇正之謀以攘外春秋善之也甚矣攘
外成於善謀也即陽穀之會而驗之伐楚謂非
===
謀之善者耶說者謂是之會齊桓遠結江黄以
伐楚而侵蔡次陘之師二國曾不與也君子可
以知齊桓用謀之善矣蓋行師之道固必有正
兵以張撻伐之威尤必有奇兵以藉聲援之勢
謀之不臧未有能克敵而制勝者也齊桓陽穀
之會江黄來矣於是萃羣辟而授經略俾壯乎
外攘之勳結遠國而示約束用貲其內應之助
兵有聚而爲正則屬之八國以當其前先人有
奪人之心也兵有分而爲奇則屬之江黄以擬
punctuated:
王儒

同考試官教諭徐批〔齊桓克敵制勝之謀，當歸重於結江黄以爲奇兵。上傳意自明，士子類作此合，殊失輕昂。是篇意中肯綮，且文思俊逸，氣勢弘大，讀之令人灑然，夫非蘊藉之深者耶？高〕薦允宜。
考試官學正吳批〔平順而敷腴，非苟作者。〕
考試官教授吳批〔文有思致，高取。〕

霸主定奇正之謀以攘外，《春秋》善之也。甚矣，攘外成於善謀也！即陽穀之會而驗之伐楚，謂非謀之善者耶？說者謂是之會，齊桓遠結江黄以伐楚，而侵蔡次陘之師，二國曾不與也。君子可以知齊桓用謀之善矣。蓋行師之道，固必有正兵以張撻伐之威，尤必有奇兵以藉聲援之勢。謀之不臧，未有能克敵而制勝者也。齊桓陽穀之會，江黄來矣。於是萃羣辟而授經略，俾壯乎外攘之勳；結遠國而示約束，用貲其內應之助。兵有聚而爲正，則屬之八國以當其前，先人有奪人之心也；兵有分而爲奇，則屬之江黄以擬

Wang Ru 王儒

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔“In Duke Huan of Qi’s strategy for defeating the enemy and securing victory, the chief emphasis should fall on his alliance with Jiang and Huang as an extraordinary force. The meaning of the commentary above is clear in itself. Candidates generally treat this as a conjunction [?], badly misjudging the relative weight of the elements. This essay’s argument strikes the crucial point; moreover, its conception is graceful and spirited, and its momentum expansive. Reading it leaves one refreshed. Surely this comes from profound cultivation? A high〕recommendation is indeed appropriate.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: 〔“Smooth and fluent, yet ample and rich: this is no careless composition.”〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Professor: 〔“The writing shows thought and refinement. Select it for a high place.”〕

The hegemon devised a strategy employing extraordinary and regular forces to repel external powers, and the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him for it. How greatly success in repelling external powers depends on sound planning! Taking the meeting at Yanggu and testing its results against the campaign against Chu, could one deny the excellence of the strategy? Commentators say that at this meeting Duke Huan of Qi formed alliances with the distant states of Jiang and Huang to attack Chu; yet neither state participated in the army that invaded Cai and encamped at Xing. From this the gentleman can recognize Duke Huan’s skill in strategy. The way to conduct a campaign certainly requires regular forces to display the might of a punitive expedition, but it especially requires extraordinary forces to lend the strength of supporting aid. No one whose planning was unsound has ever been able to defeat the enemy and secure victory.

At Duke Huan of Qi’s meeting at Yanggu, Jiang and Huang attended. He thereupon assembled the various rulers and assigned strategic plans, so as to strengthen their achievement in repelling external powers; he allied with distant states and laid down their obligations, drawing upon their assistance as support from within the enemy’s sphere. Where troops were concentrated to form the regular force, he assigned this role to the eight states, to confront the enemy’s front: taking the initiative could rob the enemy of its resolve. Where troops were divided off to form the extraordinary force, he assigned this role to Jiang and Huang, to threaten …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
其後乘人不乘於人也則夫次陘而諸侯皆集
非觀釁也即陽穀之聚而爲正者也聲罪致討
以震中國之威一運籌之餘已決矣伐楚而江
黃不與非背約也即陽穀之分而爲奇者也各
守其境以爲八國之援一經畫之際已喻矣夏
之多算以克敵二國之不動固八國所恃無恐
也用奇以制勝江黃之掎角乃荊南所由屈服
也使不撓其勢而徒欲以力勝之則陸梁莫制
之楚安能一舉而遂屈也哉是楚之服於齊者
不在用兵而在用謀之善桓之謀乎楚者不始
===
于次陘而始于陽穀之日謀定陽穀而楚可攘
周可尊矣以桓霸安攘大計悉定於此也經於
大會而未言者謂非予之矣乎雖然二國之來
慕桓之義以成桓之謀惜也見滅于楚不能救
焉齊負江黃多矣而管敬仲則固籌之熟者夫
齊霸經營十有八年非仲無成觀親暱不棄之
義賜履實征之烈皆洛之仲父以行焉則攘夷
安夏仲之力也故曰如其仁如其仁
punctuated: 其後，乘人不乘於人也。則夫次陘而諸侯皆集，非觀釁也，即陽穀之聚而爲正者也。聲罪致討，以震中國之威，一運籌之餘已決矣。伐楚而江黃不與，非背約也，即陽穀之分而爲奇者也。各守其境，以爲八國之援，一經畫之際已喻矣。夏之多算以克敵，二國之不動，固八國所恃無恐也；用奇以制勝，江黃之掎角，乃荊南所由屈服也。使不撓其勢，而徒欲以力勝之，則陸梁莫制之楚，安能一舉而遂屈也哉？是楚之服於齊者，不在用兵，而在用謀之善。桓之謀乎楚者，不始于次陘，而始于陽穀之日。謀定陽穀，而楚可攘，周可尊矣。以桓霸安攘大計，悉定於此也。經於大會而未言者，謂非予之矣乎？雖然，二國之來，慕桓之義，以成桓之謀。惜也，見滅于楚，不能救焉！齊負江黃多矣。而管敬仲則固籌之熟者。夫齊霸經營十有八年，非仲無成。觀親暱不棄之義、賜履實征之烈，皆洛之仲父以行焉，則攘夷安夏，仲之力也。故曰：「如其仁！如其仁！」
translation_en:
…at their rear, taking the initiative against others rather than allowing others to take the initiative against them. Thus, when the army encamped at Xing and all the lords assembled, they were not merely watching for an opening: these were precisely the forces concentrated at Yanggu to serve as the regular army. Proclaiming Chu’s offenses and bringing punitive force against it, thereby displaying the might of the Central States—all this had already been decided in the course of strategic deliberation. That Jiang and Huang did not participate in the attack on Chu was no breach of their agreement: these were precisely the forces detached at Yanggu to serve as the unconventional arm. Each was to hold its own territory and provide support for the eight states; this had already been made clear when the plans were drawn up. Through Xia’s ample calculations for defeating the enemy [?], the two states’ remaining stationary was precisely what allowed the eight states to proceed without fear. In securing victory through unconventional forces, the converging pressure exerted by Jiang and Huang was what brought the southern land of Jing into submission. Had they failed to unsettle Chu’s strategic position and sought to overcome it by force alone, how could Chu, rampant and unrestrained, have been subdued in a single undertaking?

Thus Chu’s submission to Qi resulted not from the use of troops but from skillful planning. Duke Huan’s plans against Chu began not with the encampment at Xing, but with the meeting at Yanggu. Once the plans were settled at Yanggu, Chu could be repelled and Zhou accorded honor. For the grand strategy of securing peace and repelling outsiders under Huan’s hegemony was settled entirely there. As for what the Classic left unstated concerning this great meeting, can one say that it did not signify approval?

Nevertheless, the two states came out of admiration for Huan’s righteousness and helped bring his plans to fruition. How regrettable that, when they were destroyed by Chu, he could not save them! Qi owed Jiang and Huang a great deal. Yet Guan Jingzhong was certainly a seasoned planner. Qi’s hegemony took eighteen years of effort to establish; without Zhong, it could not have succeeded. Consider the righteousness of not abandoning close allies and the glorious achievement of actually campaigning throughout the territories granted to him: all were carried out through ‘Father Zhong’ [?]. Repelling the outsiders and bringing peace to the Xia states were therefore Zhong’s achievements. Hence the saying: ‘Such was his benevolence! Such was his benevolence!’

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮　冬楚公子貞帥
師伐鄭〔俱襄公八年〕夏公會齊侯于夾
谷　齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕
楊行之
同考試官教諭徐　批
〔題中頭緒本多而場中作者類浮冗可厭獨此作對待嚴整結構精密意義無毫髮滲漏必沉潛而有得者宜錄以式〕
考試官學正吳　批〔沖雅〕
===
考試官教授吳　批〔得旨〕
春秋紀內外用兵歸地之事而予奪之意見矣
此鄭之侵蔡昧於自守而魯地之來歸則聖人
化強之速也春秋奪之予之也宜哉夫鄭奚爲
而侵蔡也以蔡爲楚與而侵之也已而楚人脩
怨而子貞之兵至焉若是則咎疑在楚矣而君
子罪鄭也何蓋天下莫尚於禮而以小事大古
人所以重交鄰也鄭簡公不聞之乎而胡狡焉
以逞也從耳國之訏謨忽經邦之遠略蔡之侵
punctuated:
鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮；冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔俱襄公八年〕。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷；齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔俱定公十年〕。
楊行之
同考試官教諭徐批〔題中頭緒本多，而場中作者類浮冗可厭，獨此作對待嚴整，結構精密，意義無毫髮滲漏，必沉潛而有得者，宜錄以式〕。
考試官學正吳批〔沖雅〕。
考試官教授吳批〔得旨〕。
《春秋》紀內外用兵、歸地之事，而予奪之意見矣。此鄭之侵蔡，昧於自守，而魯地之來歸，則聖人化強之速也。《春秋》奪之予之也，宜哉！夫鄭奚爲而侵蔡也？以蔡爲楚與而侵之也。已而楚人脩怨，而子貞之兵至焉。若是，則咎疑在楚矣，而君子罪鄭也，何？蓋天下莫尚於禮，而以小事大，古人所以重交鄰也。鄭簡公不聞之乎？而胡狡焉以逞也？從耳國之訏謨，忽經邦之遠略，蔡之侵
translation_en:
“The men of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Xie, a prince of Cai. In winter, Zhen, a prince of Chu, led an army to attack Zheng.” 〔Both entries are from the eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 “In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” 〔Both entries are from the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Yang Xingzhi
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic has many threads, and most candidates’ compositions are tiresomely superficial and prolix. This composition alone sets its contrasting elements in rigorous order and is meticulously structured, without the slightest omission in its meaning. Its author must have gained understanding through deep reflection. It should be recorded as a model.〕
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔Serene and refined.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Grasps the purport.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals records military actions and the return of territory, both within Lu and beyond it, thereby revealing its intent to approve or condemn. Zheng’s invasion of Cai showed ignorance of how to preserve itself, whereas the return of Lu’s lands showed how swiftly the sage could transform the powerful. How fitting are the Annals’ condemnation and approval!
Why did Zheng invade Cai? It invaded because Cai was an ally of Chu. Subsequently, the men of Chu pursued their grievance, and Zhen’s army arrived. In that case, the fault would seem to lie with Chu; yet the gentleman condemns Zheng. Why? Nothing under Heaven ranks above ritual propriety. For a small state to serve a great one was the means by which the ancients gave due weight to relations with neighboring states. Had Duke Jian of Zheng not heard of this? Why, then, did he perversely seek to have his way? Disregarding [?] the grand counsels of the state and neglecting the far-reaching plans for governing the realm, the invasion of Cai …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
燹之獲不相時而怨楚此鄭人皆喜而子産獨
為不順者與卒之鄭兵方旋楚師即繼汲汲焉
請盟之恐後者何昔勇而今怯哉經故於侵蔡
書侵而鄭及楚平不復書者若曰無文德而有
武功甚矣鄭之頗於禮也其責之之意如此齊
魯爲爲而會夾谷也以魯及齊平而會也已而
齊侯悔過而鄆讙龜陰之田歸焉若是則美疑
在齊矣而君子善仲尼也何蓋天下莫大於禮
而以弱化强古人所以貴立國也魯定公亦得
===
之邪而幸安焉以濟也委孔子以相儀具司馬
以從事却夷裔罷享禮仗大義以伸威此齊侯
心慙而晏子亟爲謝過者與卒之魯君甫歸而
侵田隨復章章焉效順之惟謹者何先倨而後
恭哉經故於三田之歸特書曰來若曰有文事
必有武備大哉聖人之達於禮也其序續之意
如此於以見無禮則以鄭之狡而不能得之於
楚有禮則以魯之弱而可以得之於齊春秋據
事直書而爲鑒不旣遠哉抑鄭不足言矣使魯
punctuated:
燹之獲，不相時而怨楚，此鄭人皆喜而子産獨為不順者與？卒之，鄭兵方旋，楚師即繼，汲汲焉請盟之恐後者，何昔勇而今怯哉？經故於侵蔡書侵，而鄭及楚平不復書者，若曰：「無文德而有武功，甚矣鄭之頗於禮也！」其責之之意如此。
齊魯爲爲而會夾谷也？以魯及齊平而會也。已而齊侯悔過，而鄆、讙、龜陰之田歸焉。若是則美疑在齊矣，而君子善仲尼也，何？蓋天下莫大於禮，而以弱化强，古人所以貴立國也。魯定公亦得之邪？而幸安焉以濟也。委孔子以相儀，具司馬以從事，却夷裔，罷享禮，仗大義以伸威，此齊侯心慙而晏子亟爲謝過者與？卒之，魯君甫歸，而侵田隨復，章章焉效順之惟謹者，何先倨而後恭哉？經故於三田之歸特書曰「來」，若曰：「有文事，必有武備。」大哉聖人之達於禮也！其序續之意如此。於以見無禮則以鄭之狡而不能得之於楚，有禮則以魯之弱而可以得之於齊。《春秋》據事直書，而爲鑒不旣遠哉？抑鄭不足言矣，使魯
translation_en:
…the gains from burning [?]; failing to judge the circumstances, they resented Chu. Was this what delighted all the people of Zheng, while Zichan alone considered it contrary to proper order? In the end, Zheng’s troops had scarcely turned homeward before Chu’s army followed. Why were those who had formerly been so bold now so fearful, anxiously seeking a covenant lest they be too late? Thus the Classic records the invasion of Cai as an “invasion,” but does not separately record Zheng’s making peace with Chu. It is as though it said: “To possess military accomplishments without civil virtue—how gravely Zheng deviates from ritual propriety!” Such is the intent of its censure.
Why did Qi and Lu [?] meet at Jiagu? They met because Lu had made peace with Qi. Subsequently, the lord of Qi repented of his wrongdoing, and the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were returned. On this account, the credit might seem to belong to Qi; yet the gentleman praises Zhongni. Why? Nothing under Heaven is greater than ritual propriety. To transform the strong through the weak was why the ancients valued it as the foundation of a state. Had Duke Ding of Lu also grasped this? Fortunately, he rested secure in it and thereby succeeded. He entrusted Confucius with assisting in the ceremonial proceedings and provided a Marshal to attend to affairs. Confucius repelled the non-Chinese tribesmen, stopped the ceremonial feast, and relied on great moral principles to assert his authority. Was this what made the lord of Qi ashamed at heart and Yanzi hasten to apologize? In the end, the ruler of Lu had barely returned when the seized lands were restored. Why did Qi, so visibly scrupulous in demonstrating submission, turn from its earlier arrogance to such deference? Thus, in recording the return of the three territories, the Classic expressly writes “came.” It is as though it said: “Where there are civil affairs, there must be military preparations.” How great was the sage’s mastery of ritual propriety! Such is the intent of its narrative sequence [?]. From this we see that, without ritual propriety, even Zheng’s cunning could gain nothing from Chu, whereas with ritual propriety, even Lu’s weakness could secure its aims with Qi. The Spring and Autumn Annals records events directly as they occurred: does it not provide a mirror for ages far into the future? Yet Zheng scarcely merits further discussion. If Lu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
用孔子終焉則豈獨齊人歸侵疆三家墮郈費
哉東周之兦徵矣而何其未能也夫子産用而
鄭安六卿和而晉昌晏子用而齊霸此皆當時
之可見者賢才之益於世也久矣況夫子耶
禮記
故天降膏露地出醴泉山出器車河出馬
圖鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷龜龍在宮沼其
餘鳥獸之卵胎皆可俯而闚也
慕孟奇
===
同考試官教諭羅　批〔體貼至順處而又以古雅豐健之詞發之必其學識之俱優者錄之〕
考試官學正吴　批〔以大順貫作良是〕
考試官教授吴　批〔精確〕
觀瑞物之駢臻而大順之化見矣蓋和氣足以
致祥也今大順之世而瑞物駢臻焉聖王致治
之盛何如哉記禮運者之意蓋謂聖王以順御
天下也治化雖妙於無爲而功用自徵於有象
豈直三才之協應已乎吾見和氣旁達聿昭夫
punctuated:
用孔子終焉，則豈獨齊人歸侵疆、三家墮郈費哉？東周之兦徵矣，而何其未能也！夫子産用而鄭安，六卿和而晉昌，晏子用而齊霸，此皆當時之可見者。賢才之益於世也久矣，況夫子耶？

禮記
故天降膏露，地出醴泉，山出器車，河出馬圖，鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷，龜龍在宮沼，其餘鳥獸之卵胎皆可俯而闚也。
慕孟奇

考試官學正吴　批〔以大順貫作，良是。〕
考試官教授吴　批〔精確。〕

觀瑞物之駢臻，而大順之化見矣。蓋和氣足以致祥也。今大順之世，而瑞物駢臻焉，聖王致治之盛何如哉？記禮運者之意，蓋謂聖王以順御天下也。治化雖妙於無爲，而功用自徵於有象，豈直三才之協應已乎？吾見和氣旁達，聿昭夫
translation_en:
…had continued to employ Confucius to the end, would the results have been limited to the people of Qi returning the territory they had seized and the three clans demolishing the fortifications of Hou and Fei? The signs of the Eastern Zhou’s demise were evident [?]; yet why was this not accomplished? When Zichan was employed, Zheng enjoyed peace; when the six ministers were in harmony, Jin flourished; when Yanzi was employed, Qi attained hegemony. These were all things observable at the time. Worthy talent has long benefited the world—how much more so would the Master!

Record of Rites
“Thus Heaven sends down rich dew, Earth brings forth springs of sweet liquor, the mountains produce implements and carriages, and the river produces the horse chart. Phoenixes and qilin are all found in the thickets outside the city; tortoises and dragons inhabit the palace ponds. As for the eggs and unborn young of other birds and beasts, one can bend down and look into them.”
Mu Mengqi

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔He apprehends the point of perfect harmony with close sympathy and expresses it in language that is classically elegant, ample, and vigorous. Surely his learning and discernment are both outstanding. Select this essay.〕
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔He makes great harmony the thread running through the essay: very sound.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Precise and exact.〕

Observe the auspicious creatures and objects arriving together, and the transforming influence of great harmony becomes apparent. For harmonious vital energies suffice to bring forth auspicious signs. Now, in an age of great harmony, these auspicious things arrive in profusion: how magnificent must be the sage king’s achievement in bringing about good government! The intention of the author of “The Evolution of Rites” was surely to say that the sage king governs all under Heaven through harmony. Although the transforming power of his government works wondrously through nonaction, its efficacy naturally reveals itself in visible manifestations. Could this amount merely to the concordant responses of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind? I see harmonious vital energies spreading in every direction, thereby making manifest those…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
可致之祥而大化潛孚自萃夫庶徵之應故以
言乎天不特降露已也有濃而若膏者焉融液
以溥其澤與至順而相爲凝結矣以言乎地不
特出泉已也有甘而若醴者焉時出以沛其流
與至順而相爲洋溢矣器車者命世之瑞自山
出之不待揉治而渾然天成之妙順氣之成形
者何如也馬圖者文明之祥自河出之不假人
謀而粲然先天之文順氣之成象者何如也以
至鳳麟必有道而後見難乎其畢至也惟順達
===
於郊棷而鳳凰麒麟皆在焉以鳴國家之盛以
昭仁厚之德若其有以馴之矣龜龍必聖世而
後出難乎其竝見也惟順達於宮沼而龜龍在
焉以兆吉凶之用以妙變化之神若其有以畜
之矣外此而庶物之生而鳥而獸者至多也則
各遂其性親上親下者相若也蓋無一物而不
相忘於大順之中矣其卵胎不可以俯而闚哉
是知物不同而其爲瑞一也瑞不同而爲大順
之徵一也揆厥所自何莫而非禮信以爲之本
punctuated: 可致之祥，而大化潛孚，自萃夫庶徵之應。故以言乎天，不特降露已也，有濃而若膏者焉，融液以溥其澤，與至順而相爲凝結矣。以言乎地，不特出泉已也，有甘而若醴者焉，時出以沛其流，與至順而相爲洋溢矣。器車者，命世之瑞，自山出之，不待揉治，而渾然天成之妙，順氣之成形者何如也！馬圖者，文明之祥，自河出之，不假人謀，而粲然先天之文，順氣之成象者何如也！以至鳳麟，必有道而後見，難乎其畢至也。惟順達於郊棷，而鳳凰麒麟皆在焉，以鳴國家之盛，以昭仁厚之德，若其有以馴之矣。龜龍，必聖世而後出，難乎其竝見也。惟順達於宮沼，而龜龍在焉，以兆吉凶之用，以妙變化之神，若其有以畜之矣。外此而庶物之生，而鳥而獸者至多也，則各遂其性，親上親下者相若也。蓋無一物而不相忘於大順之中矣，其卵胎不可以俯而闚哉？是知物不同而其爲瑞一也，瑞不同而爲大順之徵一也。揆厥所自，何莫而非禮信以爲之本
translation_en:
…the auspicious signs that can be brought forth, while the great transforming influence silently wins a response, naturally gathering the manifestations of manifold portents. Thus, speaking of Heaven, it does more than merely send down dew: there is dew as rich as unguent, melting and flowing to spread its bounty, congealing in concert with perfect harmony. Speaking of Earth, it does more than merely produce springs: there are springs as sweet as sweet wine, issuing in due season with abundant streams, overflowing in concert with perfect harmony. Vessels and carriages are auspicious signs of a sage destined to preside over an age. They emerge from the mountains, requiring no bending or working, wondrously complete through Heaven’s own making. How remarkable is the harmonious vital energy that takes material form in them! The chart borne by a horse is an auspicious sign of cultivated brilliance. It emerges from the river without human contrivance, its radiant pattern preceding Heaven itself. How remarkable is the harmonious vital energy that takes visible configuration in it!

As for phoenixes and qilin, they appear only when the Way prevails; it is difficult indeed for them all to arrive together. Yet harmony extends to the thickets beyond the city, and phoenixes and qilin are all present there, proclaiming the flourishing of the state and displaying the virtue of benevolence and generosity, as though something had tamed them. Tortoises and dragons emerge only in an age of sagely rule; it is difficult indeed for them to appear together. Yet harmony extends to the palace ponds, and tortoises and dragons are present there, serving to foretell good and ill fortune and wondrously manifesting the numinous power of transformation, as though something had reared them.

Beyond these, living creatures—birds and beasts—are exceedingly numerous. Each fulfills its nature: those drawn to what is above and those drawn to what is below fare alike. Indeed, there is not a single creature that does not live in such perfect harmony that each forgets the others. Could one not bend down and peer at their eggs and unborn young? Thus we know that although these creatures differ, they are alike in being auspicious signs; although the auspicious signs differ, they are alike in being evidence of great harmony. Tracing them to their source, how could any fail to have ritual propriety and trustworthiness as its foundation…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
乎柳論天人勢雖相懸而感通之理每捷於影
響古之聖王所以先天而天弗違奉天而天即
應者一念之精誠有以上當天心而潛孚默契
於冥冥之表者固有人不及知而己獨得之者
不專在政治間也故諸福之物可致之祥莫不
畢至而盛德昭格遂與惟皇竝矣詩曰永言配
命自求多福易曰日新之謂盛德富有之謂大
業觀聖神功化者當於斯乎求之
仁以愛之義以正之
賀愈
===
同考試官教諭羅　批〔理精而詞暢非深於禮樂者不能到右養之士也〕
考試官學正吳　批〔有體認〕
考試官教授吳　批〔醇雅〕
先王揭所性之德而爲禮樂之輔焉蓋仁義之
於禮樂相爲流通者也先王欲救禮樂之弊舍
仁義奚以哉記者之意蓋謂禮樂不能以無弊
而救弊不可以無術先王固嘗濟之以禮樂矣
punctuated:
乎？柳論天人，勢雖相懸，而感通之理，每捷於影響。古之聖王所以先天而天弗違，奉天而天即應者，一念之精誠，有以上當天心，而潛孚默契於冥冥之表者，固有人不及知而己獨得之者，不專在政治間也。故諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，而盛德昭格，遂與惟皇竝矣。《詩》曰：「永言配命，自求多福。」《易》曰：「日新之謂盛德，富有之謂大業。」觀聖神功化者，當於斯乎求之。

仁以愛之，義以正之。
賀愈

同考試官教諭羅，批〔理精而詞暢，非深於禮樂者不能到，右養之士也。〕
考試官學正吳，批〔有體認。〕
考試官教授吳，批〔醇雅。〕

先王揭所性之德，而爲禮樂之輔焉。蓋仁義之於禮樂，相爲流通者也。先王欲救禮樂之弊，舍仁義奚以哉？記者之意，蓋謂禮樂不能以無弊，而救弊不可以無術。先王固嘗濟之以禮樂矣。
translation_en:
…could any of these fail to have ritual and trustworthiness as their foundation? In discussing Heaven and humanity [?], although their respective powers are far apart, the principle by which they move and respond to one another operates more swiftly than a shadow or an echo. The sage kings of antiquity could precede Heaven without Heaven opposing them, and follow Heaven with Heaven responding at once, because the perfect sincerity of a single thought accorded above with Heaven’s heart. In their hidden accord and silent communion beyond the unseen, there was indeed something that others could not know but that they alone apprehended; it did not reside solely in political governance. Thus all creatures bearing blessings and all auspicious signs that could be summoned invariably arrived together. Their abundant virtue shone forth and reached on high, until they stood alongside the August Sovereign of Heaven. The Book of Odes says: “Ever accord with the Mandate, and seek abundant blessings for yourself.” The Book of Changes says: “Daily renewal is called abundant virtue; possessing in abundance is called a great undertaking.” Those who contemplate the achievements and transforming influence of the divine sages should seek their explanation here.

“Through benevolence, love them; through righteousness, set them right.”
He Yu 賀愈

Associate Examiner Luo, an Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is refined and the language flows freely. Only someone deeply versed in ritual and music could attain this. He is a man of cultivation [?].”
Examiner Wu, an Instructor (xuezheng), comments: “Shows personal understanding.”
Examiner Wu, a Professor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

The former kings held aloft the virtues inherent in their nature to support ritual and music. Benevolence and righteousness, on the one hand, and ritual and music, on the other, permeate and sustain one another. If the former kings wished to remedy the failings of ritual and music, what could they use apart from benevolence and righteousness? The intent of the author of the Record is, presumably, that ritual and music cannot be free of failings, and that remedying those failings requires a method. The former kings had indeed already used ritual and music to remedy them.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
又嘗懸之以賞罰矣然猶以法久而易玩非輔
之以仁義不可也彼仁主於愛禮主於敬宜若
無所與矣孰知禮勝則離由其愛之不足也故
必本仁以愛之根之以惻怛之眞而章程顯設
之餘莫非至情之浹洽敦之以慈祥之懿而等
威分辨之際莫非實意之充周以天合者則因
心以致愛而情不可解也以人合者則推心以
廣愛而情無所忤也分雖判於迹之異而心則
孚以理之同則禮非强世而所以嘉天下之會
===
者在是矣尚何患於偏勝而離也哉義主於正
樂主於和宜若無所與矣孰知樂勝則流由其
正有所歉也故必陳義以正之嚴毅以立其防
而歡然以相與者恒寓夫裁制之體斟酌以協
其宜而怡然以相接者不涉於比暱之私或主
恩者不至以恩而掩義也或主義者必欲以義
而斷恩也雖情之所通者無間而分之所限者
甚嚴則樂非任情而所以平天下之心者在是
矣尚何患於偏勝而流也哉是知仁以愛之則
punctuated: 又嘗懸之以賞罰矣。然猶以法久而易玩，非輔之以仁義不可也。彼仁主於愛，禮主於敬，宜若無所與矣。孰知禮勝則離，由其愛之不足也。故必本仁以愛之，根之以惻怛之眞，而章程顯設之餘，莫非至情之浹洽；敦之以慈祥之懿，而等威分辨之際，莫非實意之充周。以天合者，則因心以致愛，而情不可解也；以人合者，則推心以廣愛，而情無所忤也。分雖判於迹之異，而心則孚以理之同，則禮非强世，而所以嘉天下之會者在是矣。尚何患於偏勝而離也哉！義主於正，樂主於和，宜若無所與矣。孰知樂勝則流，由其正有所歉也。故必陳義以正之，嚴毅以立其防，而歡然以相與者，恒寓夫裁制之體；斟酌以協其宜，而怡然以相接者，不涉於比暱之私。或主恩者，不至以恩而掩義也；或主義者，必欲以義而斷恩也。雖情之所通者無間，而分之所限者甚嚴，則樂非任情，而所以平天下之心者在是矣。尚何患於偏勝而流也哉！是知仁以愛之則
translation_en:
…They had also held out rewards and punishments. Yet they still considered that rules, long established, easily come to be disregarded, and that it was indispensable to supplement them with benevolence and righteousness. Benevolence centers on love, while ritual centers on reverence: the two might seem unrelated. Who would recognize that when ritual predominates, estrangement follows because love is insufficient? Thus one must take benevolence as the basis for loving others. Root this love in genuine compassion, and even amid the manifest establishment of rules and forms, the deepest feelings will everywhere permeate relations. Strengthen it through the excellence of kindness, and even as distinctions of rank and dignity are drawn, sincere intentions will everywhere prevail. For those joined by Heaven, love proceeds from the heart, and their affection cannot be dissolved; for those joined through human relationships, one extends one’s heart to broaden love, and affection encounters no discord. Although their respective stations are distinguished by differences in outward circumstances, their hearts trust one another through the principle they share. Ritual, then, does not coerce the world: herein lies its means of bringing the world’s associations to an excellent fulfillment. Why any longer fear that its one-sided predominance will produce estrangement?

Righteousness centers on rectitude, while music centers on harmony: the two might seem unrelated. Who would recognize that when music predominates, unrestrained indulgence follows because rectitude is deficient? Thus one must set forth righteousness to rectify it. Establish its safeguards through stern resolution, so that joyful dealings with others always embody due restraint; weigh circumstances to accord with what is fitting, so that pleasant interactions never descend into the partiality of cliques and excessive familiarity. Where affection takes precedence, it must not be allowed to obscure righteousness; where righteousness takes precedence, one must use it to cut off affection. Although feelings circulate without obstruction, the limits imposed by one’s proper station remain very strict. Music, then, does not give free rein to feeling: herein lies its means of bringing peace to the hearts of all under Heaven. Why any longer fear that its one-sided predominance will produce unrestrained indulgence? From this we know that when benevolence is employed to love others, then…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
嚴而能泰是謂至禮義以正之則和而有節是
謂至樂此先王經制之善而致民治之行也雖
然先王之禮樂固以仁義爲之輔而仁爲心之
全德尤爲禮樂之原也誠使吾心渾然天理而
肫肫其仁則自吾心之和順者發之卽爲樂自
吾心之恭敬者發之卽爲禮所以昭宣天地者
此也所以法天下而傳後世者此也若夫制度
聲容特其文具耳故樂記一書其說皆歸諸心
而孔子他日論禮樂亦惟屬之仁人旨哉
===
第貳場
論
聖人神化與天地同流
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭黃 批〔此是程子發明子貢之意曰立曰道曰綏曰動是聖化斯立斯行斯來斯和是聖化之神處題意本〕
〔大作者不知融會或失之亢或失之支獨此篇只就本文發揮而聖〕
〔人神化同流寫得宛然如探淵海而得玄珠者奇士也允宜首選〕
考試官學正吳 批〔理性論似此者絶少〕
punctuated:
嚴而能泰，是謂至禮；義以正之，則和而有節，是謂至樂。此先王經制之善，而致民治之行也。雖然，先王之禮樂固以仁義爲之輔，而仁爲心之全德，尤爲禮樂之原也。誠使吾心渾然天理，而肫肫其仁，則自吾心之和順者發之，卽爲樂；自吾心之恭敬者發之，卽爲禮。所以昭宣天地者，此也；所以法天下而傳後世者，此也。若夫制度聲容，特其文具耳。故《樂記》一書，其說皆歸諸心，而孔子他日論禮樂，亦惟屬之仁人。旨哉！

第貳場
論
聖人神化與天地同流
潘雲祥

同考試官教諭黃批〔此是程子發明子貢之意：曰立，曰道，曰綏，曰動，是聖化；斯立，斯行，斯來，斯和，是聖化之神處。題意本〕〔大，作者不知融會，或失之亢，或失之支。獨此篇只就本文發揮，而聖〕〔人神化同流寫得宛然，如探淵海而得玄珠者。奇士也，允宜首選。〕
考試官學正吳批〔理性論似此者絶少。〕
translation_en:
…stern yet at ease: this is called consummate ritual. When righteousness rectifies it, harmony has proper limits: this is called consummate music. Such was the excellence of the former kings’ institutions and the practice by which they brought the people to good order. Nevertheless, although the former kings’ ritual and music were supported by benevolence and righteousness, benevolence, as the complete virtue of the heart, is above all the source of ritual and music. If our hearts were wholly imbued with heavenly principle and utterly sincere in benevolence, what issued from their harmony and accord would become music, and what issued from their reverence and respect would become ritual. This is how Heaven and Earth are made manifest; this is what serves as a model for all under Heaven and is transmitted to later generations. As for regulations, sounds, and ceremonial bearing, these are merely their outward forms. Thus the teachings throughout the Record of Music all lead back to the heart; and when Confucius spoke of ritual and music on another occasion, he likewise entrusted them solely to the benevolent person. How profound!

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage’s Numinous Transformation Flows Together with Heaven and Earth”
Pan Yunxiang

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “This is Master Cheng’s elucidation of Zigong’s meaning. ‘Establishing,’ ‘guiding,’ ‘reassuring,’ and ‘stirring’ constitute the sage’s transforming influence; ‘thereupon standing firm,’ ‘thereupon proceeding,’ ‘thereupon coming,’ and ‘thereupon becoming harmonious’ are where its numinous efficacy lies. The topic is inherently vast. Writers who do not know how to comprehend and integrate its meaning err either through overreaching or through digression. This essay alone develops its argument directly from the original text, vividly depicting how the sage’s numinous transformation flows together with Heaven and Earth. Its author is like someone who probes the ocean depths and obtains the dark pearl. An exceptional talent indeed, fully deserving first place.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Discourses on principle and human nature like this are exceedingly rare.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授吳　批〔發然可愛〕
天地之化至神也聖人所以妙感應而無間者
其必有合德者矣神矣哉天地之化乎盡萬物
而覆載之物之生成熙熙然相忘於其化而不
自知其至神之所爲乎聖人何以能同之盖天
地盡物聖人盡民其道一也聖人方且承天地
之責以生萬民天下之化將聖人是賴而聖人
必以其德先之以爲鼓舞感動之機初非有意
於必吾之從之也然德之所至化亦至焉化之
===
所感民斯應焉不疾而速不行而至天下
亦歸於聖人之化而不知此其感應之妙眞與
天地同流者也非合德於天地者其孰能與於
此子貢智足以知聖人者也乃贊之曰立之斯
立道之斯行綏之斯來動之斯和程子釋之以
聖人神化上下與天地同流嗚呼其善觀聖人
者與世之論聖人者必擬諸天地何也意以聖
人之生乃天地所獨厚而輔相參贊以助其所
不及者也故觀天地則知聖人矣易有之曰大
punctuated:
考試官教授吳，批〔發然可愛〕

天地之化至神也，聖人所以妙感應而無間者，其必有合德者矣。神矣哉，天地之化乎！盡萬物而覆載之，物之生成，熙熙然相忘於其化，而不自知其至神之所爲乎！聖人何以能同之？盖天地盡物，聖人盡民，其道一也。聖人方且承天地之責以生萬民，天下之化將聖人是賴，而聖人必以其德先之，以爲鼓舞感動之機，初非有意於必吾之從之也。然德之所至，化亦至焉；化之所感，民斯應焉。不疾而速，不行而至，天下亦歸於聖人之化而不知。此其感應之妙，眞與天地同流者也。非合德於天地者，其孰能與於此？子貢，智足以知聖人者也，乃贊之曰：「立之斯立，道之斯行，綏之斯來，動之斯和。」程子釋之以「聖人神化，上下與天地同流」。嗚呼，其善觀聖人者與！世之論聖人者，必擬諸天地，何也？意以聖人之生，乃天地所獨厚，而輔相參贊，以助其所不及者也。故觀天地則知聖人矣。《易》有之曰：「大
translation_en:
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Striking and delightful [?].〕

The transforming power of Heaven and Earth is supremely numinous. That the sage achieves such wondrous, uninterrupted stimulus and response must be because his virtue accords with theirs. How numinous is the transformation wrought by Heaven and Earth! They shelter and sustain all things; things come into being and mature, flourishing contentedly, oblivious to this transforming power and unaware of what its supreme numinosity accomplishes. How can the sage equal it? Heaven and Earth bring all things to fulfillment, and the sage brings all the people to fulfillment: their Way is one. The sage assumes the responsibility of Heaven and Earth for nurturing the myriad people. The transformation of all under Heaven will depend upon him, and he must lead them with his virtue, making it the source of their inspiration and awakening. From the outset, he has no intention of insisting that they follow him. Yet wherever his virtue reaches, transformation also reaches; wherever that transformation moves them, the people respond. Without haste, it is swift; without traveling, it arrives. All under Heaven likewise come under the sage’s transforming influence without knowing it. Such is the wonder of his stimulus and their response: it truly flows together with Heaven and Earth. Who could participate in this without possessing virtue that accords with Heaven and Earth?

Zigong, whose wisdom was sufficient to understand the sage, praised him thus: “When he establishes them, they stand established; when he guides them, they proceed; when he brings them peace, they come to him; when he rouses them, they become harmonious.” Master Cheng explained this as “the sage’s numinous transformation, flowing together with Heaven and Earth above and below.” Ah, how well he discerned the sage! Why do those who discuss the sage invariably compare him to Heaven and Earth? Presumably because, in his birth, the sage is uniquely favored by Heaven and Earth, and assists and participates in their work, supplementing what they do not accomplish. Thus, by observing Heaven and Earth, one can understand the sage. The Book of Changes says: “Great…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
哉乾元萬物資始至哉坤元萬物資生天統元
氣地統元形其命則於穆其載則無聲臭似若
無所見者然沖漠無朕太極淵涵二五妙其用
六子效其能相禪而相濟以動以散以潤以暄
以止以說而萬物生成其間雖跂行喙息煦嫗
昭蘇莫不取足於天地之化而含美利於不言
竟莫得其所以然者謂非其化之神不可也故
曰陰陽不測之謂神又曰合一不測爲神聖人
者固天地之心之所寄也其德則與之合焉者
===
其視天下之大兆民之衆亦猶天地之於物也
然聖莫如孔子雖甚盛德蔑以加矣卽其未試
之效而預推之使得邦家居可致之位操可致
之權所以體天地之化而達之於政治者豈能
忘情於天下也哉故嘗欲立之以遂生養矣而
耕鑿樹畜以若於其天者未必其卽立也欲道
之以明倫理矣而敦典敘倫以迪於其敎者未
必其卽行也欲綏之以寧謐動之以興起矣而
不應徯志於變時雍者未必其卽來卽和也吾
punctuated:
哉乾元，萬物資始；至哉坤元，萬物資生。天統元氣，地統元形，其命則於穆，其載則無聲臭，似若無所見者。然沖漠無朕，太極淵涵，二五妙其用，六子效其能，相禪而相濟，以動以散，以潤以暄，以止以說，而萬物生成其間。雖跂行喙息，煦嫗昭蘇，莫不取足於天地之化，而含美利於不言，竟莫得其所以然者，謂非其化之神不可也。故曰：「陰陽不測之謂神。」又曰：「合一不測爲神。」

聖人者，固天地之心之所寄也，其德則與之合焉者。其視天下之大、兆民之衆，亦猶天地之於物也。然聖莫如孔子，雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣。卽其未試之效而預推之，使得邦家，居可致之位，操可致之權，所以體天地之化而達之於政治者，豈能忘情於天下也哉？故嘗欲立之以遂生養矣，而耕鑿樹畜以若於其天者，未必其卽立也；欲道之以明倫理矣，而敦典敘倫以迪於其敎者，未必其卽行也；欲綏之以寧謐，動之以興起矣，而不應徯志、於變時雍者，未必其卽來卽和也。吾
translation_en:
…great is the originating power of Qian: all things depend on it for their beginning! Consummate is the originating power of Kun: all things depend on it for their birth! Heaven governs primordial vital energy; Earth governs primordial form. Their mandate is profound and majestic; their workings have neither sound nor smell, seemingly offering nothing perceptible. Yet, empty and still, without any trace, the Supreme Ultimate holds all within its depths. The two forces and five phases exercise their wondrous functions; the six children—the six derivative trigrams—display their powers. They succeed and complement one another, moving and dispersing, moistening and warming, bringing rest and joy, while the myriad things are born and mature amid them. Even creatures that crawl or breathe through beaks are warmed, nurtured, and brought to flourishing life. All obtain their sufficiency from the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth and receive its excellent benefits without a word being spoken. Yet none can fathom how this comes about. One cannot deny that this transformation is numinous. Thus it is said: “The unfathomable operation of yin and yang is called numinous.” It is also said: “Their union as one, beyond fathoming, constitutes the numinous.”

The sage is indeed where the heart of Heaven and Earth resides; his virtue accords with theirs. He regards the vast realm and its teeming people just as Heaven and Earth regard all things. Yet no sage equals Kongzi: even those of the most abundant virtue cannot surpass him. If we anticipate what he could accomplish, though his efficacy had not yet been put to the test, and suppose that he obtained a state or domain, occupied a position from which his aims could be realized, and wielded the authority to realize them, how could he, in embodying the transforming activity of Heaven and Earth and extending it to government, ever cease to care for the world? Thus, suppose he wished to establish the people so that they could sustain and nurture life: those who ploughed, dug wells, planted, and raised livestock in accordance with their Heaven-given endowment would not necessarily become established at once. Suppose he wished to guide them so as to clarify ethical relationships: those who upheld the enduring norms and ordered human relationships in accordance with his teaching would not necessarily follow at once. Suppose he wished to pacify them into tranquillity and stir them into action: those described as “not responding, awaiting his intent” [?] and becoming transformed into harmony would not necessarily come to him and become harmonious at once. I …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
有作爲運動之勞而天下未必皆應或應之而
未必速焉天下且得以窺其心之所存而吾之
化未至也奚足以同天地之神耶惟聖人之心
與天地爲一其德與天地相合德之所積者旣
盛故化之所感者自神聖人雖不必天下之化
而德自孚天下雖不知聖德之神而機自應立
之斯立無弗若於其天也道之斯行無弗迪於
其敎也綏之斯來動之斯和無弗丕應而雍以
穆也是其精神之所鼓舞風聲之所感召立之
===
道之綏之動之聖人所以感之者無心也斯立
斯行斯來斯和天下所以應之者亦無心也無
心之化其神乎斯與天地同流而無間者乎古
今言盛治者必曰堯舜巍巍則天大哉堯之爲
君也重華協帝虞舜之不可及也其曰萬邦協
和四方風動云者亦可見其化之神矣然欽明
文思與夫濬哲文明書特首著之二帝所以盛
者無乃出於此與夫子脩書斷自唐虞雖不位
堯舜之位也祖述之而道在焉則嘗遊觀上曹
punctuated:
有作爲運動之勞，而天下未必皆應，或應之而未必速焉。天下且得以窺其心之所存，而吾之化未至也，奚足以同天地之神耶？惟聖人之心與天地爲一，其德與天地相合。德之所積者旣盛，故化之所感者自神。聖人雖不必天下之化，而德自孚；天下雖不知聖德之神，而機自應。立之斯立，無弗若於其天也；道之斯行，無弗迪於其敎也；綏之斯來，動之斯和，無弗丕應而雍以穆也。是其精神之所鼓舞，風聲之所感召。立之、道之、綏之、動之，聖人所以感之者無心也；斯立、斯行、斯來、斯和，天下所以應之者亦無心也。無心之化，其神乎！斯與天地同流而無間者乎！
古今言盛治者必曰堯舜。「巍巍則天」，大哉堯之爲君也！「重華協帝」，虞舜之不可及也！其曰「萬邦協和」、「四方風動」云者，亦可見其化之神矣。然「欽明文思」與夫「濬哲文明」，《書》特首著之。二帝所以盛者，無乃出於此與？夫子脩《書》，斷自唐虞，雖不位堯舜之位也，祖述之而道在焉。則嘗遊觀上曹
translation_en:
…bear the toil of taking action and setting things in motion, yet not everyone under Heaven necessarily responds; even those who respond may not do so promptly. People can moreover discern the intentions harbored in my heart, while my transforming influence has yet to reach them. How could this suffice to equal the wondrous efficacy of Heaven and Earth? Only the sage’s heart is one with Heaven and Earth, and his virtue accords with theirs. Since his accumulated virtue is abundant, the influence of his transforming power is naturally wondrous. Although the sage does not insist that all under Heaven be transformed, his virtue naturally wins their trust; although they do not understand the wondrous power of his virtue, their inner impulses naturally respond. When he establishes them, they become established, all conforming to their Heaven-endowed nature. When he guides them, they proceed, all following his teaching. When he brings them peace, they come to him; when he stirs them, they become harmonious. All respond fully, in harmony and reverence. Such is the inspiration imparted by his spirit and the response elicited by the report of his influence. In establishing, guiding, pacifying, and stirring them, the sage influences them without deliberate intent. In becoming established, proceeding, coming to him, and becoming harmonious, all under Heaven likewise respond without deliberate intent. How wondrous is transformation without deliberate intent! Does it not flow together with Heaven and Earth, without any separation?
Whenever people, past or present, speak of flourishing government, they invariably name Yao and Shun. “Lofty indeed, taking Heaven as his model”: how great was Yao as a ruler! “Chonghua accorded with the sovereign”: such was the unattainable excellence of Shun of Yu! The statements that “the myriad states were brought into harmony” and that “the four quarters were stirred as by the wind” likewise reveal the wondrous efficacy of their transforming influence. Yet the Book of Documents expressly places “reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful” and “profoundly wise, accomplished, and enlightened” at the beginning of its accounts. Might not the flourishing achievements of these two sovereigns have sprung from these qualities? When the Master edited the Book of Documents, he chose to begin with Tang and Yu. Although he did not occupy the position of Yao and Shun, he transmitted and followed their example, and their Way was present in him. He once went to observe at Shangcao [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
然而歎志大道之行矣及老而東周之志莫遂
乃以其所未試者洩之於徒既庶而富而教以
告冉有與子路言志而曰老安少懷朋友信之
其意可見即紀傳所載如攝相而魯大治也郠
讙以侵田歸也會夾谷而却萊夷也墮三都以
强公室也男女别途而羔豚弗飾賈也是其兆
足以行而神化之微巳微露其機矣苟有用我
三年有成將與協和風動比隆不又有賢於堯
舜者乎宜子貢極其形容之而子禽不足以知
===
此也論再至此恍然如遊洙泗聆天階日月之
喻聽衮衣章甫惠我無私之歌頌而綏來動和
氣象亦可想見其盛矣至其化之所以神者吾
終不可得而知也是豈可以易及哉雖然聖人
之化非特當時稱之而巳六經刪述四代禮樂
以垂百王之大法天下後世皆被其澤矣孰非
神化之所及乎周子曰道德高厚教化無窮與
天地參而四時同者其惟孔子乎觀此則夫子
之神化益可識矣
punctuated:
然而歎，志大道之行矣。及老而東周之志莫遂，乃以其所未試者洩之於徒。既庶而富而教，以告冉有；與子路言志，而曰老安少懷，朋友信之。其意可見。即紀傳所載，如攝相而魯大治也，郠、讙以侵田歸也，會夾谷而却萊夷也，墮三都以强公室也，男女别途而羔豚弗飾賈也，是其兆足以行，而神化之微巳微露其機矣。苟有用我，三年有成，將與協和風動比隆，不又有賢於堯舜者乎？宜子貢極其形容之，而子禽不足以知此也。
論再至此，恍然如遊洙泗，聆天階日月之喻，聽衮衣章甫、惠我無私之歌頌，而綏來動和氣象，亦可想見其盛矣。至其化之所以神者，吾終不可得而知也，是豈可以易及哉？雖然，聖人之化，非特當時稱之而巳。六經刪述，四代禮樂，以垂百王之大法，天下後世皆被其澤矣，孰非神化之所及乎？周子曰：「道德高厚，教化無窮，與天地參而四時同者，其惟孔子乎！」觀此，則夫子之神化益可識矣。
translation_en:
…and sighed, setting his heart on the practice of the Great Way. When, in old age, his aspiration to establish a Zhou in the east remained unfulfilled, he communicated to his disciples what he had never had the opportunity to put into practice. He told Ran You that once the people were numerous, they should be enriched and then instructed. Discussing his aspirations with Zilu, he spoke of bringing peace to the aged, cherishing the young, and enjoying the trust of friends. His intention is evident. Consider also the records in histories and biographies: when he acted as chief minister, Lu became well governed; Geng and Huan were returned along with the encroached lands; at the meeting at Jiagu he repelled the Lai tribesmen; he dismantled the walls of the three cities to strengthen the ducal house; men and women took separate paths, and sellers of lambs and piglets did not inflate their prices. These were signs sufficient to show that his way could be put into practice [?], and the subtle workings of his wondrous transforming influence had already begun to reveal themselves. “If anyone were to employ me,” he said, “in three years there would be accomplishments.” These would have rivaled the flourishing achievements of bringing the myriad states into harmony and moving the four quarters as the wind moves things. Would there not then have been someone even worthier than Yao and Shun? It was fitting that Zigong should describe him in the highest terms, while Ziqin was incapable of understanding this.
As the discourse again reaches this point [?], I suddenly feel as though I were wandering beside the Zhu and Si rivers, hearing the comparisons to a stairway to Heaven and to the sun and moon, and listening to songs of praise about ceremonial robes and the zhangfu cap, and about kindness bestowed upon us without partiality. One can also imagine the full splendor of that influence through which people found peace, came willingly, were stirred to action, and lived in harmony. Yet what made his transforming influence wondrous is something I can never fully comprehend. How could such a level easily be attained? Nevertheless, the sage’s transforming influence was not acclaimed only in his own day. Through his editing and transmission of the Six Classics and the rites and music of the four dynasties, he bequeathed great standards for a hundred generations of kings. All the world and later ages have received his beneficence. What lies beyond the reach of his wondrous transforming influence? Master Zhou said: “Whose Way and virtue are lofty and profound, whose teaching and transforming influence are inexhaustible, who stands alongside Heaven and Earth and accords with the four seasons—surely this is Confucius alone!” In light of this, the Master’s wondrous transforming influence can be understood still more clearly.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
表
擬禮部右侍郎丘濬
進大學衍義補表〔成化二十三年〕
同考試官教諭侯　批
趙于敏
〔文莊平生經濟之畧備在此書子能悉其忠悃之實而發以駢儷之詞可謂曲盡其心事者矣宜録〕
以式
考試官學正吳　批〔典則之文不事雕繪可取〕
考試官教授吳　批〔得進書之體〕
===
成化二十三年某月某日國子監掌監事
禮部右侍郎臣丘濬謹以所撰大學衍義
補上
進者伏以
聖治統天必盡彌綸之大儒臣稽古貴該體用
之全因往哲之遺編託愚忠以自效續貂
知媿測蠡奚裨臣濬誠惶誠恐稽首頓首
上言竊惟
帝王之治本於道必考古斯可以證今
punctuated:
表
擬禮部右侍郎丘濬進大學衍義補表〔成化二十三年〕
同考試官教諭侯　批
趙于敏
〔文莊平生經濟之畧，備在此書。子能悉其忠悃之實，而發以駢儷之詞，可謂曲盡其心事者矣。宜録〕以式。
考試官學正吳　批〔典則之文，不事雕繪，可取。〕
考試官教授吳　批〔得進書之體。〕
成化二十三年某月某日，國子監掌監事、禮部右侍郎臣丘濬，謹以所撰《大學衍義補》上進者。伏以：聖治統天，必盡彌綸之大；儒臣稽古，貴該體用之全。因往哲之遺編，託愚忠以自效。續貂知媿，測蠡奚裨？臣濬誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首，上言：竊惟帝王之治，本於道，必考古斯可以證今，
translation_en:
Memorial
A simulated memorial by Qiu Jun, Right Vice Minister of Rites, submitting the Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi bu). 〔Twenty-third year of Chenghua [1487].〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Hou, Instructor.
Zhao Yumin [author of the model answer].
〔Wenzhuang [Qiu Jun’s posthumous title] set out fully in this book the statecraft he developed over his lifetime. You have comprehended the substance of his loyal sincerity and expressed it in parallel prose. You may truly be said to have conveyed every aspect of his aspirations. This should be selected〕 to serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: 〔A composition that accords with classical standards, without elaborate ornamentation; worthy of selection.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Instructor: 〔It achieves the proper form for submitting a book.〕
On a certain day of a certain month in the twenty-third year of Chenghua, your servant Qiu Jun, Right Vice Minister of Rites, administering the affairs of the Directorate of Education, respectfully submits the Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, which he has composed.
I humbly consider that sage governance, ruling in accord with Heaven, must fully encompass the vast scope of all affairs; a Confucian minister’s study of antiquity should embrace the entirety of both underlying principles and practical application. Drawing on the writings left by earlier wise men, I entrust to this work my humble loyalty, seeking thereby to render service. I know the shame of appending an inferior tail to fine sable; what benefit can come from measuring the sea with a gourd? Your servant Jun, in deepest fear and apprehension, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows, submitting these words:
I venture to reflect that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and that only by examining antiquity can one assess the present …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖人之德徵諸民雖篤近尤貴於舉遠惟玆大
學實備宏規十傳翼一經六籍之精微具
載三綱統八目百王之楷法斯存雖以格
致爲肇端要在治平爲極致經遺魯壁歷
漢唐而政教無聞星聚奎垣得程朱而表
章斯備逮建安之眞氏作衍義之成書首
列大綱繼開衆目聖賢性命道德之旨心
法粲然古今安危治亂之原指歸具矣用
以闡千年之學庶幾爲一代之經
===
皇祖開基爰大書於
殿壁
列聖繼統每進講於
經筵皆由躬行心得之餘以致俗美治隆之
盛顧〔臣〕一介濫廁
兩朝窮經未究於螢編執戟屢塵於
虎觀紬觀衍義之四要義若無餘尚遺治平
之二條事如有待蓋從理無間於家國而
規爲備載乎典章必須講之事事合其機
punctuated:
聖人之德徵諸民，雖篤近，尤貴於舉遠。惟玆大學，實備宏規。十傳翼一經，六籍之精微具載；三綱統八目，百王之楷法斯存。雖以格致爲肇端，要在治平爲極致。經遺魯壁，歷漢唐而政教無聞；星聚奎垣，得程朱而表章斯備。逮建安之眞氏作衍義之成書，首列大綱，繼開衆目。聖賢性命道德之旨，心法粲然；古今安危治亂之原，指歸具矣。用以闡千年之學，庶幾爲一代之經。
皇祖開基，爰大書於殿壁；列聖繼統，每進講於經筵。皆由躬行心得之餘，以致俗美治隆之盛。顧〔臣〕一介，濫廁兩朝，窮經未究於螢編，執戟屢塵於虎觀。紬觀衍義之四要，義若無餘；尚遺治平之二條，事如有待。蓋從理無間於家國，而規爲備載乎典章，必須講之事事合其機
translation_en:
The virtue of the sage is verified among the people: although he gives earnest attention to those nearby, he especially values extending his influence to those far away. The Great Learning fully contains this grand design. Its ten commentaries support the single classic, recording in full the subtle essence of the Six Classics; its three guiding principles govern its eight steps, preserving the exemplary standards of the kings of successive ages. Although it begins with investigating things and extending knowledge, its ultimate aim lies in governing the state and bringing peace to the world. The classic survived within the wall at Lu, yet through the Han and Tang its application to government and moral instruction went unheard. When the stars gathered in the Kui enclosure, it found in the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi those who fully elucidated and honored it. Later, Master Zhen of Jian’an completed his Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, first setting out the main principles and then unfolding the subsidiary topics. In its treatment of the sages’ and worthies’ teachings on human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and virtue, the methods for cultivating the mind shine clearly; in its treatment of the sources of security and danger, order and disorder, past and present, its guidance is complete. By elucidating the learning of a thousand years, it might well serve as a canon for an entire age.
When the imperial ancestor founded the dynasty, he had it written in large characters on the palace walls. As the successive sage emperors inherited the throne, it was regularly expounded at the Classics Colloquium. All drew upon their personal practice and inward understanding to bring about flourishing government and admirable customs. Yet 〔your servant〕, an insignificant man, has undeservedly held office under two reigns. In studying the classics by the light of fireflies, I have yet to fathom their depths; bearing a halberd, I have repeatedly sullied the Tiger Observatory with my presence. On closely examining the four essentials of the Extended Meaning, its exposition of principles seems to leave nothing outstanding. Yet it still omits the two steps of governing the state and bringing peace to the world, leaving practical matters seemingly awaiting further treatment. For in principle [?] there is no division between family and state, while the arrangements for action are fully recorded in institutions and regulations. These must be studied so that each and every undertaking accords with its appropriate circumstances…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
宜然後施之人人得其分願乃敢忘其僭
踰綴以緒餘間亦竊附見聞補其闕略自
正朝廷而成功化總規模次第之詳由正
百官以馭戎夷備內外安攘之策損益畢
徵諸
昭代體例一準於前文雖傚竭於涓埃詎何
裨乎
海嶽玆蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
===
德懋重華
道隆至聖
神明首出同
堯舜之繼天
睿智有臨作
君師而立極
離照中開於五位
乾綱總攬於萬機
成俗化民
punctuated:
宜，然後施之，人人得其分。願乃敢忘其僭踰，綴以緒餘，間亦竊附見聞，補其闕略。自正朝廷而成功化，總規模次第之詳；由正百官以馭戎夷，備內外安攘之策。損益畢徵諸昭代，體例一準於前文。雖傚竭於涓埃，詎何裨乎海嶽？
玆蓋恭遇皇帝陛下，德懋重華，道隆至聖，神明首出，同堯舜之繼天；睿智有臨，作君師而立極。離照中開於五位，乾綱總攬於萬機，成俗化民，
translation_en:
…the appropriate circumstances; only then can they be put into practice so that everyone receives their proper due. I have therefore ventured [?], overlooking my own presumption, to append these remaining observations, occasionally taking the liberty of adding what I have seen and heard to fill omissions and supply missing detail. From rectifying the court to bringing transformative teaching to fruition, I gather the details of the overall framework and its successive stages; from rectifying the officials to governing the Rong and Yi peoples, I provide policies for securing order within and repelling threats from without. All additions and omissions are grounded in the illustrious reigning dynasty, while the arrangement follows the preceding work throughout. Though I exhaust my efforts in contributing a drop of water or a speck of dust, how could this benefit the seas and mountains?
For I have reverently had the good fortune to encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, whose virtue rivals Chonghua [Shun] and whose Way attains the eminence of the supreme sage. Foremost in divine intelligence, you equal Yao and Shun in carrying on Heaven’s work; presiding with sagely wisdom, you serve as ruler and teacher and establish the ultimate standard. The radiance of Li shines forth centrally in the fifth position [the sovereign’s place in the hexagram]; the governing power of Qian [Heaven] embraces the myriad affairs of state. You perfect customs and transform the people…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
制禮作樂於凡
大政之所措注一皆
舊日之所講求雖曰
能自得師殆不同於章布然而事
君以道亦多賴於簡編義取湯銘事存殷鑒〔臣〕
濬質賦下愚之陋生當窮海之陬逮事
先朝乂玷詞林之妙選躬逢
明主更叨
胄子之清階稟祿媿虛糜莫試懷鉛之用
===
寵榮誠過分徒嬰借箸之譏竭精力於平生慶
遭逢於
盛世徒以識慙膚謭折衷未合於聖人年逼
桑榆考獵或乖於故實第食芹而思
獻終覆瓿以何辭伏願
俯俟燕閒
躬垂省覽
鑒微〔臣〕之忠悃縻其百一之愚
酌古事之便宜取其二三之策豈敢謂不煩
punctuated: 制禮作樂。於凡大政之所措注，一皆舊日之所講求。雖曰能自得師，殆不同於章布，然而事君以道，亦多賴於簡編。義取湯銘，事存殷鑒。〔臣〕濬質賦下愚之陋，生當窮海之陬，逮事先朝，乂玷詞林之妙選，躬逢明主，更叨胄子之清階。稟祿媿虛糜，莫試懷鉛之用；寵榮誠過分，徒嬰借箸之譏。竭精力於平生，慶遭逢於盛世。徒以識慙膚謭，折衷未合於聖人；年逼桑榆，考獵或乖於故實。第食芹而思獻，終覆瓿以何辭？伏願俯俟燕閒，躬垂省覽，鑒微〔臣〕之忠悃，縻其百一之愚；酌古事之便宜，取其二三之策。豈敢謂不煩
translation_en:
…establishing rites and making music. In every matter to which Your Majesty directs attention in the great affairs of government, all draws upon what you studied and investigated in former days. Although it may be said that you can find a teacher for yourself, this is surely different from “zhang bu” [?]. Nevertheless, serving the ruler according to the Way also depends greatly upon written texts. In their moral import, these take inspiration from Tang’s inscription; in the events they record, they preserve the admonitory example of Yin.

Your servant Jun, endowed with the deficiencies of the dullest understanding, was born in a remote corner by the sea. I lived to serve the preceding reign and was also [?] undeservedly included among the distinguished selections for the Hanlin Academy. Personally encountering an enlightened ruler, I further received, beyond my deserts, an honored rank connected with the education of the sons of the state. Receiving my stipend, I am ashamed to consume it without useful service, having had no opportunity to put my writing skills to the test. The favor and honor bestowed on me truly exceed my deserts; I merely incur the reproach of presuming to offer counsel, like one borrowing chopsticks to explain a plan. I have exhausted my lifelong energies and rejoice to have encountered this flourishing age. Yet I am ashamed of my shallow and limited understanding: my judgments do not accord with those of the sages. My years approach their evening, and my investigations may depart from historical precedent. Still, like one who tastes celery and wishes to present it to his ruler, I wish to offer what little I have. If this work should ultimately serve only to cover a jar, what objection could I make?

I humbly hope that, when a moment of leisure permits, Your Majesty will personally deign to examine it, recognize the loyal sincerity of your insignificant servant, and give consideration to even a hundredth part of his foolish efforts [?]. Weigh which precedents from antiquity are suited to present circumstances, and adopt two or three of their measures. How could I dare claim that it would require no trouble…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
窺牖或尚可借以識途
必格致誠正之功必以徵諸實踐
懋齊治均平之效不徒託之空言
好惡協於羣情四海仰
聖神之化
新明止於至善萬年蒙
樂利之休〔臣〕無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰大學衍義補一百
===
六十卷補前書一卷目錄三卷隨
表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭李　批〔我〕
punctuated:
窺牖，或尚可借以識途。必格致誠正之功，必以徵諸實踐；懋齊治均平之效，不徒託之空言。好惡協於羣情，四海仰聖神之化；新明止於至善，萬年蒙樂利之休。〔臣〕無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《大學衍義補》一百六十卷、補前書一卷、目錄三卷，隨表上進以聞。

第叁場
策五道
第一問
潘雲祥
同考試官教諭李　批〔我〕
translation_en:
…looking out through a window, perhaps this may still serve to show the way. The work of investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind must assuredly be verified in actual practice. Strive for results in ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing equity and peace to the realm; do not entrust these merely to empty words. When your likes and dislikes accord with the sentiments of the people, all within the Four Seas will look up to your sagely and divine transforming influence. When renewal and illumination come to rest in the highest good, generations for ten thousand years will enjoy the blessings of happiness and prosperity. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his fervent emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully submit herewith, accompanying this memorial for Your Majesty’s attention, my Supplement to the Expanded Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi bu), in 160 juan, together with one juan supplementing the earlier work and three juan of contents.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Pan Yunxiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Our …〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
成祖
列宗貽謨啓緒之善備在典誌
皇上德兼仁孝道隆述作爰
命臣工校集成編布之天下以及萬世眞有未易言者此獨能傳誦萬一於二書未布之前
且敷陳推暢與至理渾融足占
聖化入人之神且遠也宜錄以
獻
考試官學正吳　批〔二書乃〕
道德淵微攸會哉
===
皇上所以闡繹敢先對揚大烈者端在於是子能得於傳誦而究極明備非蘊藉之深者耶
考試官教授吳　批〔此篇敷揚〕
典誌奧旨及我
皇上命臣校錄以光昭
世德至意咸煥發於詞表矣子其三吾之英也
帝王有啓後之仁也必善作於前而後可
以立垂裕之宏規帝王有承先之孝也必
善述於後而後可以成光昭之偉烈蓋前
聖後聖其心一也作聖述明其道同也是
punctuated:
成祖、列宗貽謨啓緒之善，備在典誌。皇上德兼仁孝，道隆述作，爰命臣工校集成編，布之天下以及萬世，眞有未易言者。此獨能傳誦萬一於二書未布之前，且敷陳推暢，與至理渾融，足占聖化入人之神且遠也。宜錄以獻。
考試官學正吳批〔二書乃〕道德淵微攸會哉！皇上所以闡繹，敢先對揚大烈者，端在於是。子能得於傳誦而究極明備，非蘊藉之深者耶？
考試官教授吳批〔此篇敷揚〕典誌奧旨，及我皇上命臣校錄以光昭世德至意，咸煥發於詞表矣。子其三吾之英也！
帝王有啓後之仁也，必善作於前，而後可以立垂裕之宏規；帝王有承先之孝也，必善述於後，而後可以成光昭之偉烈。蓋前聖後聖，其心一也；作聖述明，其道同也。是
translation_en:
…The excellence of Chengzu and the successive emperors in bequeathing counsels and laying foundations for their successors is fully recorded in the canonical records. His Majesty combines benevolence and filial devotion in his virtue, and exalts the Way through both transmitting and creating. He therefore commanded his officials to collate and compile these writings into complete volumes, to circulate throughout the realm and endure for ten thousand generations. Their significance is indeed not easily expressed. This essay alone succeeds in conveying something of them before the two books have been circulated. Moreover, its exposition and elaboration blend seamlessly with the highest principles, sufficiently demonstrating how wondrously and profoundly the sage ruler’s transforming influence penetrates people’s hearts. It should be transcribed and presented to the throne.
Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: 〔The two books are〕 indeed where the profound subtleties of the Way and virtue converge! His Majesty’s purpose in elucidating them, and the grounds for venturing to be first to extol his great achievements [?], lie precisely here. You have grasped their meaning through recitation and transmission, and explored it with utmost clarity and completeness. Does this not show the depth of your cultivated learning?
Comment by Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Instructor: 〔This essay expounds〕 the profound meaning of the canonical records. Together with our emperor’s deepest intention in ordering his officials to collate and transcribe them so as to illuminate the virtue of successive generations, all this shines forth beyond the words themselves. You must be an outstanding talent of our region [? 三吾]!
