title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
賂而照弗能辨范鎮聽房庶以黍定律司
馬光嘗病其拘矣乃駁其失然尺長丈二
而鎮弗之察若和峴阮逸胡瑗或以量求
音或以黍生尺徒爲議論之紛紛也求其
卓然可據者吾有取於蔡季通之新書焉
如九分爲寸准南司馬可推五聲二變杜
氏通典可考黄鍾圍徑本漢斛之積分變
徵非調出孔氏之禮疏而因律以生尺先
求聲氣之元眞定律作樂之本也朱子稱
===
其明白淵密言雖出於近世無一字不本
於古人已試之法眞可折羣淆而快千古
矣朱子又與門人考禮樂著通解鍾律前
篇凡七條自十二律陰陽相生次第以至
旋宫八十四聲六十四調後篇凡六條自
明五聲之義以至黄鍾生十一律數法大
抵與元定相發明者觀其與元定書云但
用古書附以己意務簡約周盡則元定亦
有所受之也嗚呼可謂精矣我
punctuated: 賂，而照弗能辨。范鎮聽房庶以黍定律，司馬光嘗病其拘矣，乃駁其失，然尺長丈二，而鎮弗之察。若和峴、阮逸、胡瑗，或以量求音，或以黍生尺，徒爲議論之紛紛也。求其卓然可據者，吾有取於蔡季通之新書焉。如九分爲寸，准南司馬可推；五聲二變，杜氏通典可考；黄鍾圍徑，本漢斛之積分；變徵非調，出孔氏之禮疏。而因律以生尺，先求聲氣之元，眞定律作樂之本也。朱子稱其明白淵密，言雖出於近世，無一字不本於古人已試之法，眞可折羣淆而快千古矣。朱子又與門人考禮樂，著通解。鍾律前篇凡七條，自十二律陰陽相生次第，以至旋宫八十四聲、六十四調；後篇凡六條，自明五聲之義，以至黄鍾生十一律數法，大抵與元定相發明者。觀其與元定書云：「但用古書，附以己意，務簡約周盡。」則元定亦有所受之也。嗚呼！可謂精矣！我
translation_en:
…bribes, yet Li Zhao could not detect it. Fan Zhen followed Fang Shu in determining the pitch standards by millet grains. Sima Guang criticized the rigidity of this approach and refuted its errors; nevertheless, the measuring rule was one zhang and two chi long [?], and Fan Zhen failed to notice. As for He Xian, Ruan Yi, and Hu Yuan, some sought pitches through measures of capacity, while others derived the measuring rule from millet grains. They merely generated a welter of disputation.

Seeking something outstanding and dependable, I find much to commend in Cai Jitong’s New Book. For example, the rule that nine fen make one cun can be deduced from Huainan and Sima [?]; the five tones and two altered tones can be investigated in Du’s Comprehensive Institutions; the circumference and diameter of the Huangzhong pitch pipe are based on the calculated volume of the Han hu measure; and the proposition that the altered zhi tone does not constitute a mode comes from Kong’s subcommentary on the rites. To derive the measuring rule from the pitch standards, first seeking the source of sound and vital breath, is truly the foundation for establishing pitch standards and creating music. Master Zhu praised the book’s clarity, profundity, and precision: although its statements originated in recent times, not a single word lacked a basis in methods already tested by the ancients. It could truly resolve the many confusions and bring satisfaction to readers through the ages.

Master Zhu also investigated ritual and music with his disciples and composed the Comprehensive Explanations. The first part on bells and pitch standards contains seven sections, proceeding from the sequence in which the twelve pitch standards generate one another through yin and yang to the eighty-four notes and sixty-four modes produced by rotating the gong tone. The second part contains six sections, proceeding from an explanation of the meaning of the five tones to the numerical methods by which Huangzhong generates the other eleven pitch standards. These largely elucidate, and are elucidated by, the work of Yuanding [Cai Jitong]. His letter to Yuanding says: “Simply use the ancient books and append your own understanding, striving for concision and completeness.” Thus Yuanding, too, received guidance. Ah! This may indeed be called meticulous! Our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
國朝禮樂明備斟酌前代固已盡善盡美然
禮制最詳而樂章自本太初以下止於九
奏鍾律尚未考定何也豈禮先樂後而猶
有所待耶方今
聖明在上茂建中和秉總條貫禮敘樂和列
神化翔洽百嘉鬯遂瑞應駢臻煥焉盛矣即今
大樂所陳搞以九章協以九歌其器亦古
也其音亦雅也凡側耳於朱絃天球之下
者恍若聆鈞韶而聞雲和洋洋乎與虞周
===
同一揆矣執事猶欲復古登雅樂用之愚
何所容其喙乎雖然窮本知變樂之情也
古謂其數可陳其義難知愚以爲樂之義
具於書通經學古者尚可因文以求之而
制度聲律弗傳已久雖老師宿儒不能通
曉一旦以不試之學求合古人之制難矣
夫古之善作樂必曰后夔審音必曰師曠
然其人不世出而夔之心曠之耳人所同
有也蓋樂之本同而其變異因異以統之
punctuated: 國朝禮樂明備，斟酌前代，固已盡善盡美。然禮制最詳，而樂章自本太初以下止於九奏，鍾律尚未考定，何也？豈禮先樂後，而猶有所待耶？方今聖明在上，茂建中和，秉總條貫，禮敘樂和，列神化翔洽，百嘉鬯遂，瑞應駢臻，煥焉盛矣！即今大樂所陳，搞以九章，協以九歌，其器亦古也，其音亦雅也。凡側耳於朱絃天球之下者，恍若聆鈞韶而聞雲和，洋洋乎與虞周同一揆矣。執事猶欲復古登雅，樂用之，愚何所容其喙乎？雖然，窮本知變，樂之情也。古謂其數可陳，其義難知。愚以爲樂之義具於書，通經學古者尚可因文以求之，而制度聲律弗傳已久，雖老師宿儒不能通曉。一旦以不試之學求合古人之制，難矣！夫古之善作樂必曰后夔，審音必曰師曠，然其人不世出，而夔之心、曠之耳，人所同有也。蓋樂之本同，而其變異，因異以統之
translation_en:
…our dynasty’s rites and music are clearly established and complete. Drawing judiciously upon preceding dynasties, they have indeed attained perfection in both goodness and beauty. Yet, while the ritual institutions are most fully elaborated, the musical movements, beginning with “Rooted in the Great Beginning” (Ben Taichu), amount to only nine performances, and the pitches of the bells have still not been investigated and settled. Why is this? Could it be that rites come first and music afterward, and that something remains to be awaited?

Now our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, abundantly establishing equilibrium and harmony and holding together the guiding principles and their particulars. Rites bring order and music brings harmony; the arrayed spirits’ transforming influence spreads everywhere [?], all auspicious things flourish freely, and favorable portents arrive in profusion. How brilliant and flourishing it is! As for the grand music now performed, it is arranged [?] in nine movements and harmonized with nine songs. Its instruments are ancient, and its sounds are refined. All who incline their ears beneath the vermilion strings and the celestial jade chimes feel as though they were listening to Jun and Shao music and hearing the instruments of Yunhe. In its overflowing grandeur, it follows the very same standard as the ages of Yu and Zhou.

Yet you, honored examiners, still wish to restore antiquity, promote refined music, and put it into use. What room is there for an ignorant man like me to offer a word? Nevertheless, to probe its foundation and understand its changes is to grasp the true nature of music. The ancients said that its numerical relations could be set forth, but its meaning was difficult to understand. I believe that the meaning of music is fully contained in books: those versed in the classics and devoted to ancient learning can still seek it through the texts. But its institutional forms and tonal standards have long ceased to be transmitted. Even venerable teachers and seasoned scholars cannot understand them thoroughly. To seek suddenly, through untested learning, to accord with the institutions of the ancients is difficult indeed!

Of the ancients skilled in creating music, one invariably names Hou Kui; of those skilled in discerning tones, one invariably names Shi Kuang. Such men do not appear in every age, yet Kui’s mind and Kuang’s ear are faculties that all people share. For music has a common foundation, though its variations differ; through these differences one may bring it into unity …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
同由𪓟以會厥精其庶幾乎宜及此時
明詔天下求知音律者令文學掌故博采樂書
相與講求即今世所奏之樂所歌之詞正
宮越調以求古人淸宮淸商之類被之於
樂器使其音皆諧和如宋人所謂由今之
器寄古之聲去怗懘靡曼而歸之於中和
雅正然後按古鍾律之法即蔡氏律呂新
書朱子通解鍾律依其說而究其意築室
布灰如其候氣之法截竹爲管以求黃鍾
===
之聲凡律長則聲濁而氣先至極長則不
成聲而氣不應律短則聲淸而氣後至極
短則不成聲而氣不應莫若截管或極其
短或極其長長短之內每差一分以爲一
管即其長權爲九寸如古法實以秬黍度
其圍徑如此更迭以吹則中聲可得淺深
以別則中氣可驗茍聲和氣應則黃鍾可
信而十二律度量權衡皆定矣昔太史公
論律不言用兵而言兵之偃當孝文之世
punctuated: 同，由𪓟以會厥精，其庶幾乎？宜及此時，明詔天下，求知音律者，令文學掌故博采樂書，相與講求。即今世所奏之樂、所歌之詞，正宮越調，以求古人淸宮淸商之類，被之於樂器，使其音皆諧和。如宋人所謂由今之器寄古之聲，去怗懘靡曼，而歸之於中和雅正。然後按古鍾律之法，即蔡氏《律呂新書》、朱子《通解》鍾律，依其說而究其意，築室布灰，如其候氣之法，截竹爲管，以求黃鍾之聲。凡律長則聲濁，而氣先至；極長則不成聲，而氣不應。律短則聲淸，而氣後至；極短則不成聲，而氣不應。莫若截管，或極其短，或極其長，長短之內，每差一分以爲一管，即其長權爲九寸，如古法實以秬黍，度其圍徑。如此更迭以吹，則中聲可得；淺深以別，則中氣可驗。茍聲和氣應，則黃鍾可信，而十二律、度量權衡皆定矣。昔太史公論律，不言用兵，而言兵之偃，當孝文之世，
translation_en: …unity; proceeding through [?] to comprehend its essence, might one not come close? This is the time to issue an explicit edict throughout the realm seeking those who understand musical pitches, and to direct men of learning and those versed in institutional precedents to collect musical writings widely and investigate them together. Taking the music performed and the lyrics sung today, including the zhenggong and yue modes, they should seek equivalents to the ancients’ clear gong and clear shang pitches and the like, and render them on musical instruments so that all their tones are harmonious. As men of the Song put it, one should convey ancient sounds through present-day instruments, removing discordance and seductive luxuriance and returning to balance, harmony, refinement, and correctness. Then one should examine the ancient methods governing bells and pitch standards, consulting Master Cai’s New Treatise on Pitch Pipes (Lülü xinshu) and the treatment of bells and pitch standards in Master Zhu’s Comprehensive Explanation (Tongjie). Following their explanations and investigating their meaning, one should construct a chamber and lay out ashes according to their method of observing the seasonal qi, and cut bamboo into pipes to seek the sound of the Yellow Bell (huangzhong) pitch. In general, when a pitch pipe is long, its sound is low and the qi arrives earlier; if excessively long, it produces no musical tone and the qi does not respond. When a pitch pipe is short, its sound is high and the qi arrives later; if excessively short, it produces no musical tone and the qi does not respond. The best course is to cut pipes ranging from extremely short to extremely long, making a pipe at every increment of one fen within that range. Provisionally reckon the length of each as nine cun, fill it with black millet according to the ancient method, and measure its circumference and diameter. By blowing these in succession, the properly balanced tone can be obtained; by distinguishing their shallow and deep placements, the properly balanced qi can be verified. If the sound is harmonious and the qi responds, the Yellow Bell pitch can be trusted, and the twelve pitch standards, together with the standards of length, capacity, and weight, can all be fixed. Formerly, when the Grand Astrologer discussed pitch standards, he spoke not of employing troops but of laying arms to rest: in the age of Emperor Xiaowen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
禁網疏闊海内富庶老人嬉戲如小兒狀
煙火萬里可謂和樂者乎此其本之有在
也若夫會道器於一原而達律呂之精緼
自有妙契神解者愚也管窺何足以知之
謹對
第四問
蔡子益奇
同考試官教諭羅　批〔昔程子云非欲字好即此是學可見文字聲韻亦學者所當講明子獨能考據折衷且敷陳正韻極〕
===
〔擧制而有得者博古通今佳士佳士　　爲詳書蓋服習〕
考試官學正吳　批〔有識見有議論〕
考試官教授吳　批〔博洽之學〕
彰天下之用者其惟文而已乎是故考文
以審聲固學者之所當究心也蓋時有古
今文以代變而聲韻因之有所作於前斯
有所述於後體製既殊音韻亟異不能無
不失於其間矣自夫字不師古而違趣於
punctuated:
禁網疏闊，海内富庶，老人嬉戲如小兒狀，煙火萬里，可謂和樂者乎？此其本之有在也。若夫會道器於一原，而達律呂之精緼，自有妙契神解者，愚也管窺，何足以知之？謹對。

第四問
蔡子益奇
同考試官教諭羅，批〔昔程子云：「非欲字好，即此是學。」可見文字聲韻，亦學者所當講明。子獨能考據折衷，且敷陳正韻極〕〔擧制而有得者，博古通今，佳士，佳士！爲詳書，蓋服習〕
考試官學正吳，批〔有識見，有議論。〕
考試官教授吳，批〔博洽之學。〕

彰天下之用者，其惟文而已乎？是故考文以審聲，固學者之所當究心也。蓋時有古今，文以代變，而聲韻因之。有所作於前，斯有所述於後。體製既殊，音韻亟異，不能無不失於其間矣。自夫字不師古，而違趣於
translation_en:
…restrictions were lax, and the realm was prosperous and well supplied. Old people played happily like little children, and the smoke of household hearths extended for ten thousand li. Could this be called harmony and joy? This had its foundation. As for uniting the Way and its concrete manifestations in a single source and comprehending the subtle profundities of the pitch standards, there are those who possess marvelous intuitive insight and spiritual understanding. With my foolish, narrow view, how could I know these things? Respectfully submitted.

Fourth Question
Master Cai Yiqi
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Cheng once said: “It is not that I want the characters to look good; this itself is learning.” We can see that written characters, sounds, and rhymes are also matters that scholars should elucidate. You alone have investigated the evidence and weighed competing views, and your exposition of Correct Rhymes is extremely…〕〔one who has gained understanding through the examination literary form [?]. Broadly versed in antiquity and conversant with the present—a fine scholar, a fine scholar! “In detail … the book … presumably practiced and studied” [?].〕
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔There is discernment, and there is reasoned argument.〕
Examiner Wu, Professor, comments: 〔Broad and comprehensive learning.〕

Is it not writing alone that makes manifest the practical workings of the world? Thus, examining written forms to ascertain their sounds is certainly something to which scholars should devote their attention. There are ancient and modern times; writing changes with each age, and sounds and rhymes follow those changes. What is created in an earlier age is transmitted in a later one. Once forms and structures differ, pronunciations and rhymes repeatedly change, and errors inevitably arise in the process [?]. Ever since written characters ceased to take antiquity as their model and turned instead toward…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
簡便韻莫考正而多失之錯謬人惟樂失
今文之便而踵乎韻學之謬故簡易之文
相習於後世而協和之音莫能正於天下
矣有志好古者可不考而審之乎執事當
文教大同之世乃以字學策諸生其用意可
謂勤矣敢不備述前代既往之迹而莊誦
我
國朝之盛制乎且文何從生哉天地一氣也
有氣而後有聲有聲而後有字維天有文
===
垂諸象矣維地有文顯諸形矣其粲然以
示人者無非文也顓頊之初太上忘言結
繩而治自龍馬出圖羲皇則之以列八卦
爲萬世鼻祖亦止於有畫而已猶未有文
也黃帝垂衣裳蒼頡觀鳥跡乃制文字而
書契始興焉擬蝌蚪之形所謂上古之文
也歷世寶之靡有易者周宣時史籀略變
古法更爲大篆所謂中古之文也其後李
斯更蒼史之舊加以損益遂變而爲小篆
punctuated: 簡便，韻莫考正，而多失之錯謬。人惟樂失今文之便，而踵乎韻學之謬，故簡易之文相習於後世，而協和之音莫能正於天下矣。有志好古者，可不考而審之乎？執事當文教大同之世，乃以字學策諸生，其用意可謂勤矣。敢不備述前代既往之迹，而莊誦我國朝之盛制乎？且文何從生哉？天地一氣也，有氣而後有聲，有聲而後有字。維天有文，垂諸象矣；維地有文，顯諸形矣。其粲然以示人者，無非文也。顓頊之初，太上忘言，結繩而治。自龍馬出圖，羲皇則之，以列八卦，爲萬世鼻祖，亦止於有畫而已，猶未有文也。黃帝垂衣裳，蒼頡觀鳥跡，乃制文字，而書契始興焉。擬蝌蚪之形，所謂上古之文也。歷世寶之，靡有易者。周宣時，史籀略變古法，更爲大篆，所謂中古之文也。其後李斯更蒼史之舊，加以損益，遂變而爲小篆。
translation_en:
…convenience; rhymes went unexamined and uncorrected, and errors and confusions proliferated. People merely delighted in the convenience of contemporary writing [?] and perpetuated the errors of rhyme scholarship. Thus simplified writing was transmitted through habitual use in later ages, while harmonious sounds could nowhere be set right. Can those devoted to antiquity fail to investigate and scrutinize this? You, honored Examiner, live in an age when literary instruction is universally shared, yet have chosen to question us students on the study of written characters. Your concern may indeed be called diligent. How could I fail to recount fully the precedents of earlier dynasties and reverently extol the magnificent institutions of our reigning dynasty?

From what, then, did writing arise? Heaven and earth are one vital force: only with vital force is there sound, and only with sound are there written characters. Heaven has its patterns, displayed in celestial phenomena; earth has its patterns, manifested in physical forms. Everything they reveal so brilliantly to human beings is patterned form. At the beginning of Zhuanxu’s time, in highest antiquity, words were forgotten and government was conducted through knotted cords. When the dragon-horse brought forth the diagram, the sovereign Fuxi took it as his model and arranged the Eight Trigrams, becoming the progenitor for all ages. Yet these were only drawn lines; writing did not yet exist. Huangdi let his upper and lower garments hang down, and Cangjie observed birds’ tracks and thereupon devised written characters. Written records and tallies then first arose. These characters imitated the shapes of tadpoles: this was what is called the writing of high antiquity. Successive generations treasured it, and none altered it. In the time of King Xuan of Zhou, the Scribe Zhou modified the ancient method slightly, transforming it into the large seal script: this was what is called the writing of middle antiquity. Later, Li Si revised the old forms of Cangjie and the Scribe Zhou, making omissions and additions, and thereby transformed them into the small seal script…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
程邈以篆文煩瑣復改爲隸書矣然字有
六義焉一曰象形二曰指事三曰諧聲四
曰會意五曰轉注六曰假借六書立而文
字之大義盡矣其後變更非一秦人燔滅
典籍易以八體如所謂大篆小篆刻符摹
印蟲書署書殳書隸書之類是也西漢之
末甄豐刊定六體如所謂古文奇字篆書
隸書繆書蟲書之類是也魏晉以還隸文
遂盛有蕭子良者備古今篆隸諸體有藁
===
書楷書蓬書塡書奠書鳥書龜書又有懸
針也垂露也飛白也虎爪也偃波也鶴頭
也象形篆也尚方篆也十二時書也蝌蚪
蟲書也鳳鳥之與龍虎也仙人之與芝英
也麒麟之與蚊角也倒薤之與金錯也凡
數十種大抵多出於六義八體而文字備
矣至謂篆之廢由於秦何也蓋其任刀筆
之吏衡石程書以苛爲能喜其隸之便而
篆學始孤矣宋之能多於唐何也蓋其尋
punctuated:
程邈以篆文煩瑣，復改爲隸書矣。然字有六義焉：一曰象形，二曰指事，三曰諧聲，四曰會意，五曰轉注，六曰假借。六書立，而文字之大義盡矣。其後變更非一，秦人燔滅典籍，易以八體，如所謂大篆、小篆、刻符、摹印、蟲書、署書、殳書、隸書之類是也。西漢之末，甄豐刊定六體，如所謂古文、奇字、篆書、隸書、繆書、蟲書之類是也。魏晉以還，隸文遂盛。有蕭子良者，備古今篆隸諸體，有藁書、楷書、蓬書、塡書、奠書、鳥書、龜書，又有懸針也、垂露也、飛白也、虎爪也、偃波也、鶴頭也、象形篆也、尚方篆也、十二時書也、蝌蚪蟲書也，鳳鳥之與龍虎也，仙人之與芝英也，麒麟之與蚊角也，倒薤之與金錯也，凡數十種。大抵多出於六義八體，而文字備矣。
至謂篆之廢由於秦，何也？蓋其任刀筆之吏，衡石程書，以苛爲能，喜其隸之便，而篆學始孤矣。宋之能多於唐，何也？蓋其尋
translation_en:
Cheng Miao, finding seal script cumbersome, further altered it to create clerical script. Written characters, however, have six principles: first, pictographic representation; second, indication of an abstract idea; third, combination of semantic and phonetic elements; fourth, combination of meanings; fifth, derivative extension; and sixth, phonetic borrowing. With these six categories established, the fundamental principles of writing were fully encompassed. Subsequent changes were numerous. The people of Qin burned and destroyed the canonical texts and replaced the scripts with eight forms: the so-called large seal, small seal, tally-cutting, seal-impression, insect, inscription, spear-shaft, and clerical scripts. At the end of the Western Han, Zhen Feng revised and standardized six forms: the so-called ancient script, unusual characters, seal script, clerical script, intertwined script, and insect script. From the Wei and Jin onward, clerical writing consequently flourished. A certain Xiao Ziliang assembled the various ancient and contemporary forms of seal and clerical writing. These included draft script, standard script, peng or ‘tumbleweed’ script [?], filled-in script, dian or ‘offering’ script [?], bird script, and tortoise script. There were also suspended-needle, hanging-dewdrop, flying-white, tiger-claw, reclining-wave, crane-head, pictographic seal, Imperial Manufactories seal, twelve-hours, and tadpole-and-insect scripts; phoenix-bird and dragon-and-tiger scripts; immortal and numinous-fungus-blossom scripts; qilin and mosquito-horn [?] scripts; and inverted-scallion and gold-inlay scripts—several dozen varieties in all. Most broadly derived from the six principles and eight forms, and thus the forms of writing became complete.
As for the claim that the abandonment of seal script originated under the Qin, why is this? Because the Qin employed clerks skilled with the knife and writing brush, measured their daily quota of documents by weight, and regarded severity as competence. They welcomed the convenience of clerical script, and the study of seal script began to languish. Why were there more accomplished practitioners under the Song than under the Tang? Because they sought…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
斯籀之緒唐之能者雖超於宋惟宋人好
古而能者尤多矣晉人書法體尚姿媚若
逸少獻之輩能擅一代之長而聖於書矣
吳氏臨川頗不取乎晉無亦以其妍巧失
眞乎宋人能書字有法度若蔡襄米芾者
獨來朱子之取而極其美矣予贍嘗直俱
爲所病無乃以其不甚理會乎蓋文字之
體古今之不可盡同者亦時之變爲之也
然依類象形謂之文形聲相益謂之字有
===
文字自有音韻苟辨之弗精一字訛其餘
皆謬而弊有不可言者矣呼吸之間其音
有五曰脣聲舌聲齒聲牙聲喉聲清濁自
分而爲宮商角徵羽也字韻之別其聲有
四平聲哀而安上聲厲而舉去聲清而遠
入聲直而促也單出爲聲成文爲音韻者
聲之餘也音者韻之始也三十六字母古
來所以切字之法也吳臨川以俗本傳訛
羣當易以芹非當易以威知徹牀娘四字
punctuated:
斯籀之緒，唐之能者雖超於宋，惟宋人好古而能者尤多矣。晉人書法，體尚姿媚，若逸少、獻之輩，能擅一代之長而聖於書矣。吳氏臨川頗不取乎晉，無亦以其妍巧失眞乎？宋人能書，字有法度，若蔡襄、米芾者，獨來朱子之取而極其美矣。予贍嘗直俱爲所病，無乃以其不甚理會乎？蓋文字之體，古今之不可盡同者，亦時之變爲之也。然依類象形謂之文，形聲相益謂之字。有文字，自有音韻，苟辨之弗精，一字訛，其餘皆謬，而弊有不可言者矣。
呼吸之間，其音有五，曰脣聲、舌聲、齒聲、牙聲、喉聲，清濁自分而爲宮商角徵羽也。字韻之別，其聲有四：平聲哀而安，上聲厲而舉，去聲清而遠，入聲直而促也。單出爲聲，成文爲音。韻者，聲之餘也；音者，韻之始也。三十六字母，古來所以切字之法也。吳臨川以俗本傳訛，羣當易以芹，非當易以威，知徹牀娘四字
translation_en:
…the tradition of Si and Zhou. Although the accomplished calligraphers of the Tang surpassed those of the Song, the people of the Song cherished antiquity, and accomplished practitioners were especially numerous. In Jin calligraphy, elegance and charm were prized. Men such as Yishao and Xianzhi excelled in their age and attained sagehood in calligraphy. Master Wu of Linchuan was rather dismissive of Jin calligraphy: was this perhaps because its beauty and artifice compromised its authenticity? The accomplished calligraphers of the Song wrote with established standards. Men such as Cai Xiang and Mi Fu alone won Master Zhu’s approval and highest praise. Those whose names are transcribed as 予贍 and 嘗直 [?] were both criticized by him: was this perhaps because they did not understand the principles sufficiently? That the forms of writing cannot be entirely the same in antiquity and today is also a consequence of changes over time. Nevertheless, forms that depict things according to their categories are called wen; combinations in which form and sound complement one another are called zi. Wherever there is writing, there are naturally sounds and rhymes. If these are not distinguished precisely, an error in one character leads to errors in all the rest, with consequences beyond telling.
In breathing out and in, there are five kinds of articulation: labial, lingual, dental, velar, and guttural. These naturally divide into clear and voiced sounds and constitute the five notes gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu. In the distinctions of character rhymes, there are four tones: the level tone is plaintive and calm; the rising tone is forceful and lifted; the departing tone is clear and far-reaching; and the entering tone is direct and abrupt. A sound produced singly is sheng; when patterned, it is yin. Rhyme is what remains of a sound; articulated sound is the beginning of rhyme. The thirty-six initial categories are the traditional means of indicating a character’s pronunciation by the fanqie method. Wu of Linchuan held that commonly circulating editions had transmitted errors: 羣 (qun) should be replaced with 芹 (qin), and 非 (fei) with 威 (wei); the four characters 知 (zhi), 徹 (che), 牀 (chuang), and 娘 (niang)…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
宜廢圭缺羣危四字宜增考之陳音翁切
韻須知於照穿數字註已見某字母下經
堅數字別出偏涓之文其廢與增可知也
禮部韻略唐人以爲試士之用也梁沈約
拘以四聲號曰類譜殊不知五方風氣異
齊有剽疾重遲之異約乃盡以吴音限之
但知縱有四聲不知衡有七音故經緯不
交而失立韻之原自唐以來脩詞之子皆
弗能易獨吴棫深患作補韻以明約之失
===
朱子亦據其說以協三百篇之音也司馬
光曰備萬物之體用者莫過於字包衆字
之形聲者莫過於韻所以載道紀事治百
官察萬民通貫三才昭顯象類其用甚大
矣是可忽焉而不加之意乎嗟乎蝌蟲跡
息古文絕響久矣魯魚帝虎舛訛相沿不
但文字而聲韻亦失之也神而明之則存
乎其人爾我
明統運苐俫離之陋以還中華之音
punctuated:
宜廢，圭、缺、羣、危四字宜增。考之陳音翁《切韻須知》，於照、穿數字註「已見某字母下」，經、堅數字別出偏、涓之文，其廢與增可知也。《禮部韻略》，唐人以爲試士之用也。梁沈約拘以四聲，號曰《類譜》。殊不知五方風氣異齊，有剽疾、重遲之異，約乃盡以吴音限之，但知縱有四聲，不知衡有七音，故經緯不交，而失立韻之原。自唐以來，脩詞之子皆弗能易，獨吴棫深患，作《補韻》以明約之失。朱子亦據其說，以協三百篇之音也。司馬光曰：「備萬物之體用者，莫過於字；包衆字之形聲者，莫過於韻。」所以載道紀事，治百官，察萬民，通貫三才，昭顯象類，其用甚大矣。是可忽焉而不加之意乎？嗟乎！蝌蟲跡息，古文絕響久矣。魯魚帝虎，舛訛相沿，不但文字，而聲韻亦失之也。神而明之，則存乎其人爾。
我明統運，苐俫離之陋，以還中華之音。
translation_en:
…should be abolished, and the four characters gui 圭, que 缺, qun 羣, and wei 危 should be added. Examining Chen Yinweng’s Essential Knowledge of Phonetic Spelling (Qieyun Xuzhi), we find that entries for zhao 照, chuan 穿, and several other characters are annotated “already appears under such-and-such an initial,” while entries for jing 經, jian 堅, and several others separately give forms such as pian 偏 and juan 涓. From this one can understand the proposed deletions and additions. The Tang used the Ministry of Rites’ Abridged Rhymes (Libu Yunlüe) to examine candidates. Shen Yue of the Liang confined sounds to four tones, calling his work the Classified Tables (Leipu). He failed to understand that the prevailing airs of the five regions differ [?], some being brisk and rapid, others heavy and slow. Yet Shen Yue restricted everything to the pronunciation of Wu. He knew only that there were four tones along the vertical axis, without knowing that there were seven categories of articulation along the horizontal. Thus warp and weft did not intersect, and the original principles of establishing rhymes were lost. Since the Tang, writers had all been unable to alter this. Wu Yu alone was deeply troubled by it and wrote the Supplement to Rhymes (Buyun) to expose Shen Yue’s errors. Master Zhu also drew on his account to harmonize the sounds of the Three Hundred Odes.

Sima Guang said: “For encompassing the substance and function of all things, nothing surpasses written characters; for embracing the forms and sounds of the multitude of characters, nothing surpasses rhymes.” They convey the Way and record events, bring order to the officials and scrutiny to the people, link the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humankind—and illuminate phenomena and their categories. Their usefulness is immense. Can this be neglected and left without attention? Alas! The traces of tadpole and insect scripts have vanished, and the ancient writing has long fallen silent. Confusions between lu 魯 and yu 魚, and between di 帝 and hu 虎, have been perpetuated through successive copying. Errors afflict not only written characters but sounds and rhymes as well. To grasp these things with spiritual insight and make them clear rests with the individual.

Our Ming dynasty assumed the succession of Heaven’s mandate, [discarding?] the crudities of alien speech [?], thereby restoring the sounds of the Central Realm…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖崇文弘化凡
制誥詔令之頒所以諭臣下播海宇者
宸翰揮灑羣臣環視拱手欽矚其於聲音點畫
不假文字之麤而自有獨得之趣所謂天
地自然之文也眞可以昭回雲漢而斧藻
百王矣乃於
萬幾之暇猶慮韻學多謬特
諭詞臣宋濂等曰韻學起於江左殊失正音
當廣詢通音韻者重刋定之諸臣奉
===
詔悉心考訂於音諧而韻協者併入之否則析
之義同字同而兩見者合之避宋諱不入
者今補之如東冬青清之類當爲通用虞
模麻遮之類當爲分析難以槩舉其點畫
俱以許愼說文爲正其註釋依毛晃父子
之舊而音韻之切則以中原雅音定之書
成
上之名曰洪武正韻誠萬世不刋之典也夫詩
三百篇皆雜出於列國與里巷歌謠孔子
punctuated: 聖祖崇文弘化，凡制誥詔令之頒，所以諭臣下、播海宇者，宸翰揮灑，羣臣環視，拱手欽矚。其於聲音點畫，不假文字之麤，而自有獨得之趣，所謂天地自然之文也，眞可以昭回雲漢而斧藻百王矣。乃於萬幾之暇，猶慮韻學多謬，特諭詞臣宋濂等曰：「韻學起於江左，殊失正音，當廣詢通音韻者，重刋定之。」諸臣奉詔，悉心考訂，於音諧而韻協者併入之，否則析之；義同字同而兩見者合之；避宋諱不入者，今補之。如東冬、青清之類，當爲通用；虞模、麻遮之類，當爲分析，難以槩舉。其點畫俱以許愼《說文》爲正，其註釋依毛晃父子之舊，而音韻之切，則以中原雅音定之。書成，上之，名曰《洪武正韻》，誠萬世不刋之典也。夫《詩》三百篇，皆雜出於列國與里巷歌謠，孔子
translation_en:
The sagely founder exalted letters and extended his transforming influence. Whenever imperial pronouncements, mandates, edicts, and orders were issued to instruct his subjects and be disseminated throughout the realm, his imperial brush moved freely, while the assembled ministers watched with hands respectfully clasped, gazing in reverence. In sounds and written strokes, he did not depend upon the coarse externals of writing, but possessed an understanding uniquely his own. This was what is called the spontaneous pattern of Heaven and Earth: it could truly shine through the celestial River of Stars and lend literary adornment to the hundred kings of antiquity.

Yet, in moments of leisure amid his myriad affairs, he remained concerned about the many errors in rhyme scholarship. He specifically instructed the literary official Song Lian and others: “Rhyme scholarship arose in Jiangzuo and departed greatly from correct pronunciation. You should consult widely with those versed in sounds and rhymes, and revise and settle the work anew.” Obeying the edict, the ministers devoted themselves to examination and revision. They merged entries whose sounds harmonized and whose rhymes agreed, and otherwise separated them. They combined duplicate entries with the same meaning and the same character, and now supplied those previously omitted to avoid Song imperial name taboos. Categories such as dong 東 and dong 冬, or qing 青 and qing 清, were to be used interchangeably; those such as yu 虞 and mo 模, or ma 麻 and zhe 遮, were to be distinguished. It is difficult to enumerate them all.

For the written strokes, they uniformly took Xu Shen’s Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters (Shuowen) as the standard. Their annotations followed the earlier work of Mao Huang and his son, while their fanqie pronunciation glosses were determined according to the cultivated pronunciation of the Central Plain. When the book was completed, they presented it to the throne. It was entitled Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Reign (Hongwu Zhengyun), truly a canon that would remain unalterable for ten thousand generations. Now, the three hundred poems of the Book of Odes originated variously in the several states and in the songs of lanes and alleys. Confucius…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
刪之惟取其音之協而已未甞如沈約之
拘也今正韻之集自可以依永和聲而協
之風雅矣自此書一布效古者不敢離其
體率意者不敢便其私體製聲韻孰有不
歸於一者乎昔子思稱周之盛曰車同軌
書同文行同倫仲尼贊以郁郁其文從之
蓋遵時制也况正韻古今字學已爲悉備
家傳人習同文之化未有如
今日之盛者矣雖然文有古今其體異矣而
===
道之在人無古今也誠使一道德以同風
俗凡業經脩詞者端其趨向而弗雜以奇
衺遵其體式而罔有乎背謬翕然於文教
之化矣又何必蒼史之求而徒泥於古也
哉
第五問
王　儒
同考試官教諭徐　批
〔守中事也此篇根極利害之源條答詳明經畫曲當用以籌邊可謂　禦戎之道惟戰與守其他皆戰〕
punctuated:
刪之，惟取其音之協而已，未甞如沈約之拘也。今正韻之集，自可以依永和聲，而協之風雅矣。自此書一布，效古者不敢離其體，率意者不敢便其私，體製聲韻，孰有不歸於一者乎？昔子思稱周之盛曰：「車同軌，書同文，行同倫。」仲尼贊以郁郁其文，從之，蓋遵時制也。况正韻古今字學已爲悉備，家傳人習，同文之化，未有如今日之盛者矣。雖然，文有古今，其體異矣，而道之在人無古今也。誠使一道德以同風俗，凡業經脩詞者，端其趨向而弗雜以奇衺，遵其體式而罔有乎背謬，翕然於文教之化矣。又何必蒼史之求，而徒泥於古也哉？

第五問
王　儒
同考試官教諭徐　批
〔守中事也。此篇根極利害之源，條答詳明，經畫曲當，用以籌邊，可謂　禦戎之道，惟戰與守，其他皆戰〕
translation_en:
…in editing them, selected only for the harmony of their sounds; he was never as restrictive as Shen Yue. Now that the Correct Rhymes has been compiled, one can use it to harmonize sounds with sustained singing and bring them into accord with the Airs and Odes. Once this book is circulated, those who emulate antiquity will not dare depart from its forms, and those who write as inclination takes them will not dare indulge their private preferences. What forms of composition, sounds, or rhymes could fail to be brought into unity?

In the past, Zisi described the flourishing Zhou dynasty by saying: “Carriages have the same wheel gauge, writing uses the same script, and conduct follows the same norms.” Zhongni praised its splendid cultural refinement and chose to follow it, thereby observing the institutions of his time. Moreover, the Correct Rhymes comprehensively encompasses the study of characters, ancient and modern. Transmitted in every household and studied by every person, the transforming influence of a common script has never flourished as it does today. Nevertheless, although writing has ancient and modern forms that differ, the Way as it exists in human beings has no ancient or modern distinctions. If moral teachings were truly unified so as to bring customs into agreement, all who study the classics and cultivate literary expression would set their aims aright, without admixtures of the bizarre or perverse, and follow the prescribed forms without deviation or error. They would be united under the transforming influence of literary instruction. Why, then, must one seek out the ancient scribe Cangjie and merely cling to antiquity?

Fifth Question
Wang Ru
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor:
〔…are matters within defense [?]. This essay probes to the very source of advantages and dangers. Its responses to the individual points are detailed and clear, and its planning is appropriate in every particular. Applied to planning for the frontier, it may be called—The methods of resisting the Rong consist only of fighting and defending; all the rest are fighting… [?]〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
得上策矣錄之
考試官學正吳　批〔筆力勁健條議剴切佳士也〕
考試官教授吳　批〔書生談兵切中石畫謂予爲莫之豪傑非耶〕
中國之禦夷狄也必先立久大之規而後
可以成制馭之績規之不立則在我無成
筭久大弗圖則雖施權宜以致勝猶未爲
萬全之策也故必遠覽遐思長慮却顧俾
凡立之我者皆非旦夕之謀則豺狼之性
===
雖變詐莫窮而吾備禦之嚴凜乎莫犯固
將應之而必克制之而必勝矣故曰明王
有道守在四夷言夷之不可以不防也又
曰訏謨定命遠猶辰告言議之不可以不
審也防邊之策誠
今日切時之要務經國之良圖矣愚無能抱
請纓之志也而明問所及敢不悉心以對
夫裔夷桀驁自古已然舜舞干羽而有苗
來格文王德盛而昆夷自服卓哉邈矣逮
punctuated:
得上策矣，錄之。
考試官學正吳批〔筆力勁健，條議剴切，佳士也。〕
考試官教授吳批〔書生談兵，切中石畫，謂予爲莫之豪傑，非耶？〕
中國之禦夷狄也，必先立久大之規，而後可以成制馭之績。規之不立，則在我無成筭；久大弗圖，則雖施權宜以致勝，猶未爲萬全之策也。故必遠覽遐思，長慮却顧，俾凡立之我者皆非旦夕之謀，則豺狼之性雖變詐莫窮，而吾備禦之嚴，凜乎莫犯，固將應之而必克，制之而必勝矣。故曰：「明王有道，守在四夷。」言夷之不可以不防也。又曰：「訏謨定命，遠猶辰告。」言議之不可以不審也。防邊之策，誠今日切時之要務，經國之良圖矣。愚無能，抱請纓之志也，而明問所及，敢不悉心以對？夫裔夷桀驁，自古已然。舜舞干羽而有苗來格，文王德盛而昆夷自服，卓哉邈矣！逮
translation_en:
…may be deemed a superior strategy. Record this essay.

Examiner Wu, School Instructor, comments: 〔The writing is vigorous and forceful, and the proposals are cogent and pertinent. A worthy scholar.〕

Examiner Wu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: 〔A scholar discusses warfare and hits upon sound strategic plans. To call me an outstanding man of “Mo zhi” [?]—is that not so?〕

In defending the Central Realm against the foreign peoples, one must first establish plans of lasting and comprehensive scope; only then can one achieve success in controlling them. Without such plans, we have no settled strategy. Without considering the long term and the larger picture, even victory achieved through expedients cannot constitute an entirely secure policy. We must therefore survey distant prospects, reflect deeply, consider the long term, and look back carefully, so that everything we establish is more than a plan for the moment. Then, although those of jackal-and-wolf disposition may devise endlessly changing deceptions, the stern rigor of our defenses will deter all encroachment. We shall assuredly prevail whenever we respond to them and win whenever we bring them under control. Thus it is said: “An enlightened king possesses the Way; his defenses lie among the peoples of the four quarters.” This means that precautions against foreign peoples cannot be neglected. It is also said: “Great counsels settle commands; far-reaching plans are announced at the proper time.” This means that deliberation cannot be other than thorough.

A policy for defending the frontiers is indeed an urgent task suited to present circumstances and a sound plan for governing the state. Though I am without ability, I cherish the ambition to request a cord with which to bind the enemy. Since your discerning question touches upon this matter, how could I dare reply without giving it my fullest attention?

The defiance of peoples on the distant margins has been so since antiquity. Shun performed the dance with shields and feathers, and the Youmiao came in submission; King Wen’s virtue flourished, and the Kunyi submitted of their own accord. How exalted, and how remote, were these achievements! When …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
周宣王時則薄伐玁狁至於太原雖以兵
威震疊而實不廢其自脩之道可謂得中
策焉及漢武末大將軍衛青收大河之南
邊關盡復蒙恬之域即秦故塞立爲隴西
北地上郡朔方雲中之五郡焉分處降虜
於此因其俗爲五屬國而金城河西南至
鹽澤空無匈奴唐中宗初朔方總管張仁
愿謂鎮與突厥以河爲境因乘虛取漠南
地於河北築三受降城中東西各距四百
===
餘里據其津要設烽堠千八百所首尾相
應以絶其南寇之路自是突厥不敢度山
畋牧朔方無復寇掠減鎮兵數萬人夫漢
設五郡專倚於戰而至幕南無王庭唐設
三城專主於守而與薛延陀有和議雖衛
青張仁愿建殊勳於邊鄙爲一時漢唐將
臣之選而上下規爲終未得夫久大之術
昔人謂漢爲下策而唐啓戎狄之禍是皆
歷代因仍弊習上策不復覩矣惟我
punctuated: 周宣王時，則薄伐玁狁，至於太原。雖以兵威震疊，而實不廢其自脩之道，可謂得中策焉。及漢武末，大將軍衛青收大河之南，邊關盡復蒙恬之域，即秦故塞立爲隴西、北地、上郡、朔方、雲中之五郡焉。分處降虜於此，因其俗爲五屬國，而金城河西南至鹽澤，空無匈奴。唐中宗初，朔方總管張仁愿謂鎮與突厥以河爲境，因乘虛取漠南地，於河北築三受降城，中東西各距四百餘里，據其津要，設烽堠千八百所，首尾相應，以絶其南寇之路。自是突厥不敢度山畋牧，朔方無復寇掠，減鎮兵數萬人。夫漢設五郡，專倚於戰，而至幕南無王庭；唐設三城，專主於守，而與薛延陀有和議。雖衛青、張仁愿建殊勳於邊鄙，爲一時漢唐將臣之選，而上下規爲，終未得夫久大之術。昔人謂漢爲下策，而唐啓戎狄之禍，是皆歷代因仍弊習，上策不復覩矣。惟我
translation_en:
…in the time of King Xuan of Zhou, he struck the Xianyun and advanced as far as Taiyuan. Although he overawed them with military might, he did not in fact abandon the way of cultivating his own virtue. This may be called a strategy of the middle rank. Toward the end of Emperor Wu of Han’s reign, General-in-Chief Wei Qing recovered the lands south of the Yellow River, and the frontier defenses once again encompassed all the territory held by Meng Tian. Following the old Qin frontier fortifications, five commanderies were established: Longxi, Beidi, Shangjun, Shuofang, and Yunzhong. The surrendered enemy were settled separately here, and five dependent states were established in accordance with their customs. From Jincheng and Hexi southward to Yanze [?], no Xiongnu remained.

Early in Emperor Zhongzong of Tang’s reign, Zhang Renyuan, Area Commander of Shuofang, stated that the garrison and the Turks took the Yellow River as their boundary [?]. He then exploited their lack of defenses to seize the territory south of the desert and built three “Accepting Surrender” cities north of the river. The eastern and western cities each lay more than four hundred li from the central one. Holding the crucial river crossings, he established eighteen hundred beacon posts, linked from end to end, to cut off the routes by which they raided southward. Thereafter the Turks dared not cross the mountains to hunt or pasture their herds; Shuofang suffered no further raids or plundering, and its garrison forces were reduced by several tens of thousands of men.

The Han established five commanderies and relied exclusively on warfare, eventually leaving no royal court south of the desert. The Tang established three cities and concentrated exclusively on defense, while negotiating peace with the Xueyantuo. Although Wei Qing and Zhang Renyuan won exceptional distinction on the frontier and ranked among the foremost military servants of the Han and Tang in their respective times, the plans and measures of rulers and subordinates ultimately failed to achieve a method of enduring and far-reaching effectiveness. Earlier writers called the Han approach a strategy of the lowest rank and held that the Tang opened the way to calamities brought by the Rong and Di. These were all pernicious practices perpetuated from dynasty to dynasty; a strategy of the highest rank was no longer to be seen. Only our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元廓清寰宇
成祖文皇帝三犂虜庭威震漠北於是畫疆築
塞以立華夏之防焉
累洽重熙民安物阜者二百年於玆夫何邇
歲以來邊防懈弛醜虜猖獗加之逋逃之
引誘間諜之潛通故內地虛實彼悉知之
我軍一遇侵突弱者望風解潰强者躡險
虛聲又彼之所以深憑陵而無忌憚者以
故山後諸夷句連漠北爲諸關之害而沿
===
邊一帶時被侵掠民物之羅於鋒刃至無
可控告焉夫兵家所恃惟戰與守即今兵
勢寡弱築堡蹂躙戰守不可恃矣議者謂
庸懦叨任而將帥非人尺籍無稽而戎伍
多缺連歲荐饑而芻糧不繼且士卒驕惰
法令姑息與夫技藝賞罰間諜之類漫不
之講然則
今日欲振復中國之威式遏狂胡之橫可易
易言哉一得之愚嘗稽往牒察時宜竊以
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡元，廓清寰宇；成祖文皇帝三犂虜庭，威震漠北，於是畫疆築塞，以立華夏之防焉。累洽重熙，民安物阜者二百年於玆。夫何邇歲以來，邊防懈弛，醜虜猖獗，加之逋逃之引誘、間諜之潛通，故內地虛實，彼悉知之。我軍一遇侵突，弱者望風解潰，强者躡險虛聲，又彼之所以深憑陵而無忌憚者。以故山後諸夷句連漠北，爲諸關之害，而沿邊一帶時被侵掠，民物之羅於鋒刃，至無可控告焉。
夫兵家所恃，惟戰與守。即今兵勢寡弱，築堡蹂躙，戰守不可恃矣。議者謂庸懦叨任，而將帥非人；尺籍無稽，而戎伍多缺；連歲荐饑，而芻糧不繼。且士卒驕惰，法令姑息，與夫技藝、賞罰、間諜之類，漫不之講。然則今日欲振復中國之威，式遏狂胡之橫，可易易言哉？一得之愚，嘗稽往牒，察時宜，竊以
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, swept away the Mongol Yuan and cleared the realm; Chengzu, the Cultured Emperor, thrice devastated the enemy’s court, his might shaking the lands north of the desert. Thereupon boundaries were drawn and frontier fortifications built to establish defenses for the Chinese realm. Successive reigns of peace and prosperity have now kept the people secure and resources abundant for two hundred years. Why, then, in recent years have frontier defenses grown lax and the vile enemy become rampant? Furthermore, fugitives entice and guide them, while spies communicate secretly with them, so that they know all the strengths and weaknesses of the interior. Whenever our troops encounter an incursion, the weaker ones scatter at the mere rumor of its approach, while the stronger ones take to difficult terrain and make an empty show of force [?]. This too accounts for the enemy’s deep incursions and unrestrained aggression. Consequently, the various tribes beyond the mountains have allied with those north of the desert, threatening the passes. The entire frontier region repeatedly suffers invasion and plunder; its people and possessions fall prey to the blade, with nowhere even to lodge a complaint.
Military men rely solely on fighting and holding defensive positions. Yet today our forces are few and weak, and the forts we have built are overrun: neither fighting nor defense can be relied upon. Those who discuss the matter say that mediocre cowards undeservedly occupy commands, leaving unsuitable men as generals; military registers go unchecked, leaving many vacancies in the ranks; and repeated famine year after year interrupts supplies of fodder and grain. Moreover, the soldiers are arrogant and idle, and enforcement of regulations is indulgent. Matters such as military skills, rewards and punishments, and espionage receive no serious attention. Can restoring China’s military prestige today and checking the wild aggression of the unruly northern peoples be spoken of so lightly? Foolish though I am, I may have one useful insight: I have examined past records and considered present circumstances, and humbly believe that…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
為將帥非人也而蒐羅之法不可以不廣
焉藍邊徼重地與中土異宜匆兩敵決機
矢石交下運籌制勝羽檄紛馳使非負非
常之略未有不顛錯而眩迷也今
廟堂懸格用人乃有世蔭武舉之選得人固
多然奇偉倜儻之才爲文法見繩資格見
阻者不盡無也故必大破常格特嚴推轂
之揀少寬細過以優任事之臣而一切資
序弗之拘焉則旌拔所加必有智謀豪傑
===
得行焉則存恤所至不必屑屑於清句解
發而戎籍自無缺矣匆糧不繼鹽屯之法
可復焉夫飛輓芻粟外裕邊鄙與屯足食
內省轉輸本
國家之良法也今計較析於秋毫預納倍於
正額則利微而商多不至屯地侵於勢府
屯丁役於豪門則籍在而弊莫可稽欲芻
糧之充難矣故必嚴加淸查議復開中仍
專責之於憲臣監司務求實效不以近利
punctuated:
為將帥非人也，而蒐羅之法不可以不廣焉。藍邊徼重地，與中土異宜，匆兩敵決機，矢石交下，運籌制勝，羽檄紛馳，使非負非常之略，未有不顛錯而眩迷也。今廟堂懸格用人，乃有世蔭、武舉之選，得人固多，然奇偉倜儻之才，爲文法見繩、資格見阻者，不盡無也。故必大破常格，特嚴推轂之揀，少寬細過，以優任事之臣，而一切資序弗之拘焉，則旌拔所加，必有智謀豪傑。
得行焉，則存恤所至，不必屑屑於清句解發，而戎籍自無缺矣。匆糧不繼，鹽屯之法可復焉。夫飛輓芻粟，外裕邊鄙，與屯足食，內省轉輸，本國家之良法也。今計較析於秋毫，預納倍於正額，則利微而商多不至；屯地侵於勢府，屯丁役於豪門，則籍在而弊莫可稽，欲芻糧之充難矣。故必嚴加淸查，議復開中，仍專責之於憲臣監司，務求實效，不以近利
translation_en:
…hold that the commanders are unsuitable, and that the means of seeking out talent must therefore be broadened. For [?] conditions at strategic frontier locations differ from those in the interior. When [?] two opposing forces reach the decisive moment, arrows and stones fall together, plans must be devised to secure victory, and urgent military dispatches fly back and forth, anyone lacking exceptional strategic ability will inevitably become confused and bewildered. The court now sets standards for recruitment, selecting men through hereditary privilege and the military examinations. These certainly yield many capable men; nevertheless, there are also outstanding, unconventional talents constrained by legal formalities and obstructed by eligibility requirements. Established rules must therefore be decisively relaxed, while the selection of men recommended for command must be especially rigorous. Minor faults should be treated with some leniency to support officials who undertake responsibilities, and seniority requirements should impose no restriction. Among those thus singled out and promoted, there will surely be resourceful and heroic men.
[The text appears discontinuous here.] …can be put into practice, then, wherever care and relief extend, there will be no need to fuss over checking military registers, tracking down men liable for service, and dispatching them to their units; the military rolls will naturally have no vacancies. When supplies of fodder [?] and grain fail, the methods of salt administration and military agricultural colonies can be restored. Transporting fodder and grain swiftly to provision the frontiers, together with producing sufficient food in military colonies to reduce transport requirements within the realm, were sound institutions of the state. Now calculations are exacted to the finest detail, and advance deliveries are twice the regular quota; profits are consequently slight, and many merchants do not come. Colony lands are encroached upon by powerful households, and colony soldiers are made to serve influential families. Thus, although the registers remain, abuses cannot be effectively investigated, and adequate supplies of fodder and grain are difficult to secure. Strict investigations must therefore be conducted, and restoration of the kaizhong system—granting salt-trading entitlements in return for deliveries of grain—must be considered. Specific responsibility should also be assigned to censorial officials and provincial surveillance officials, who must seek tangible results and not, for the sake of immediate profit…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
得行焉則存恤所至不必屑屑於清句解
發而戎籍自無缺矣芻糧不繼鹽屯之法
可復焉夫飛輓芻粟外裕邊鄙與屯足食
內省轉輸本
國家之良法也今計較析於秋毫預納倍於
正額則利微而商多不至屯地侵於勢府
屯丁役於豪門則籍在而弊莫可稽欲芻
糧之充難矣故必嚴加淸查議復開中仍
專責之於憲臣監司務求實效不以近利
===
自沮焉則權課可以補歲計之歉而屯種
可以收便宜之效芻糧有不繼者乎技藝
未閑事權之重可假焉夫舉措弗專兵機
斯紊文法制縛志慮莫伸此歷代之積蠹
也今邊臣行事動見齟齬將僚約束罕遵
士卒偷惰成習操閱頗勤則呼集騰謗而
將帥隱忍不敢究詰欲技藝之閑難矣故
必優假其權勿苛督責使得展布四體事
從軍法不爲浮言所惑焉則上有便宜之
punctuated:
得行焉，則存恤所至，不必屑屑於清句解發，而戎籍自無缺矣。芻糧不繼，鹽屯之法可復焉。夫飛輓芻粟，外裕邊鄙；與屯足食，內省轉輸，本國家之良法也。今計較析於秋毫，預納倍於正額，則利微而商多不至；屯地侵於勢府，屯丁役於豪門，則籍在而弊莫可稽，欲芻糧之充難矣。故必嚴加淸查，議復開中，仍專責之於憲臣監司，務求實效，不以近利自沮焉。則權課可以補歲計之歉，而屯種可以收便宜之效，芻糧有不繼者乎？

技藝未閑，事權之重可假焉。夫舉措弗專，兵機斯紊；文法制縛，志慮莫伸，此歷代之積蠹也。今邊臣行事，動見齟齬；將僚約束，罕遵；士卒偷惰成習。操閱頗勤，則呼集騰謗，而將帥隱忍，不敢究詰，欲技藝之閑難矣。故必優假其權，勿苛督責，使得展布四體，事從軍法，不爲浮言所惑焉。則上有便宜之
translation_en:
…is put into effect, then, wherever such care and relief reach, there will be no need to fuss over verifying military registrations, tracing those liable for service, and escorting them to their posts: the military rolls will naturally have no vacancies. If fodder and grain supplies fail, the salt and military agricultural colony systems can be restored. Transporting fodder and grain swiftly supplies the frontier, while agricultural colonies provide sufficient food [?] and reduce transport burdens within the country. These are sound institutions of the state. Now, however, calculations are scrutinized down to the finest detail, and advance deliveries are twice the regular quota; profits are consequently meager, and many merchants do not come. Colony lands are encroached upon by powerful households, and colony soldiers are made to labor for influential families. The registers remain, but abuses cannot be investigated; ensuring ample fodder and grain is therefore difficult. Rigorous inspections must be conducted, restoration of the system of exchanging grain deliveries for salt certificates must be considered, and specific responsibility must again be assigned to censorial officials and surveillance commissioners. They must seek practical results and not let immediate profits deter them. Then the revenue from these levies [?] can make up annual budget shortfalls, while cultivation in the military colonies can yield practical benefits. How could fodder and grain supplies still fail?

If military skills remain unpracticed, substantial authority to act can be entrusted to the commanders. When authority over operations is divided, military planning falls into disorder; when officials are bound by administrative rules, their intentions and plans cannot be carried out. These are longstanding abuses accumulated over successive dynasties. Today, frontier officials encounter obstruction whenever they act; their officers’ orders are seldom obeyed, and soldiers have grown habitually idle. If drills and inspections become at all frequent, they raise a clamor and spread slander, while commanders endure it silently and dare not investigate or call them to account. Under such conditions, proficiency in military skills is difficult to attain. Commanders must therefore be generously entrusted with authority and spared excessively harsh supervision and reproach, so that they can act freely, conduct affairs according to military law, and remain undistracted by groundless talk. Then those above will possess discretionary…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
權而法得行下消獷戾之習而志自定技
藝有不精者乎賞罰貴信也則欺蔽不可
以不嚴蓋功罪審則賞罰明欺蔽行則功
罪紊今襲套彌縫以虛作實巧文規避以
敗爲功或戎虜在門而曰驅除出境或全
軍覆沒而曰臨陣損傷肆莫詰之欺篤不
根之詐豈綜覈名實之意耶要必窮喪失
之由重報功之典敗衂可原欺蔽必戮如
此則功不遺於遠人無僥倖之望罪不阿
===
於近法無規避之圖而賞罰信矣間諜當
明也則優恤不可以不至葢責之深入虜
庭非死士無以應募而欲其作我腹心非
厚利無以中欲故投醪挾纊者成一匡之
功吮疽椎牛者著克敵之烈今衣糧之予
屢減役使之勞不息蹈睊胥讒豈干城腹
心之寄耶要必時給予以安其心豐犒賞
以作其氣如此則士心旣得軀命可捐使
之偵探足以得虜情瞭望可以得虜形而
punctuated:
權而法得行，下消獷戾之習而志自定，技藝有不精者乎？賞罰貴信也，則欺蔽不可以不嚴。蓋功罪審則賞罰明，欺蔽行則功罪紊。今襲套彌縫，以虛作實；巧文規避，以敗爲功。或戎虜在門而曰驅除出境，或全軍覆沒而曰臨陣損傷。肆莫詰之欺，篤不根之詐，豈綜覈名實之意耶？要必窮喪失之由，重報功之典。敗衂可原，欺蔽必戮。如此則功不遺於遠，人無僥倖之望；罪不阿於近，法無規避之圖，而賞罰信矣。
間諜當明也，則優恤不可以不至。葢責之深入虜庭，非死士無以應募；而欲其作我腹心，非厚利無以中欲。故投醪挾纊者成一匡之功，吮疽椎牛者著克敵之烈。今衣糧之予屢減，役使之勞不息，蹈睊胥讒，豈干城腹心之寄耶？要必時給予以安其心，豐犒賞以作其氣。如此則士心旣得，軀命可捐；使之偵探，足以得虜情；瞭望，可以得虜形，而
translation_en:
…authority to act as circumstances require, and military law can be enforced; those below will shed their unruly habits, and their resolve will naturally become settled. How could their military skills fail to be perfected? Rewards and punishments must be credible, so deception and concealment must be dealt with severely. When merit and culpability are carefully assessed, rewards and punishments are clear; when deception and concealment prevail, merit and culpability become confused. Nowadays, men follow conventional formulas to cover up shortcomings, presenting fiction as fact; they employ clever wording to evade responsibility, presenting defeat as achievement. Some report that the enemy has been driven beyond the frontier when he is at the gates; others report losses in battle when an entire army has been annihilated. They brazenly practice deception that goes unchallenged and persist in baseless fraud. Can this accord with the purpose of comprehensively checking reports against reality? The causes of losses must be thoroughly investigated, and the rules governing reports of military merit must be strictly enforced. Defeat may be pardoned; deception and concealment must be punished by execution. Thus merit will not go unrecognized because a man is distant, and no one will hope for an undeserved advantage; guilt will not be treated indulgently because a man is close, and there will be no prospect of evading the law. Rewards and punishments will then be credible.
Intelligence obtained through spies must be clear, so generous treatment and care for them must be carried to the utmost. For when they are required to penetrate deep into enemy territory, only men prepared to die will answer the call; and if we wish them to serve as our trusted confidants, only substantial benefits will satisfy their desires. Thus those who shared wine with their troops and made them feel as warm as if clad in padded garments achieved the restoration of order throughout the realm; those who sucked their soldiers’ abscesses and slaughtered oxen to feed them won distinction in defeating the enemy. Nowadays, allocations of clothing and provisions are repeatedly reduced, while the toil of service never ceases; resentment and mutual slander follow [?]. Is this how to treat those entrusted to serve as our shield and wall, our intimate confidants? Supplies must be issued on time to set their minds at ease, and provisions and rewards must be generous to raise their spirits. Once the soldiers’ loyalty has thus been secured, they will be ready to sacrifice life and limb. Employed in reconnaissance, they will be fully capable of discovering the enemy’s circumstances; posted as lookouts, they will be able to ascertain the enemy’s dispositions, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
間諜明矣凡此六者皆戰守之所必須而
邊計之不可一日缺焉者也然戰守之道
又不止此者蓋守可矣調兵以守恐滋費
也有聯土著之法焉彼窮邊之地千里蕭
條與豺狼爲鄰伍以戰鬭爲嬉游晝則荷
戈而耕夜則倚烽而覘自非生於其域習
於其風罕能狎其敵而寧其居也今誠因
其堡砦聯以什伍稍維之以約束弗爲句
集之煩簿書之櫌使人自爲兵家自爲戰
===
凡奪敵所有悉以與之則室家墳墓固其
效死之區而親戚比閭又無攘奪之患矣
而守不足恃乎戰可矣而孤軍以戰恐寡
弱也有齊應援之法焉蓋析圭儋爵均爲
王臣列宇提封一皆王土居常則聲援相
資臨敵則移兵策應自其宜也何至幸災
樂敗篤禍求安一鎮被兵而四鄰閉境一
營抗敵而列壁旁觀有甚於秦越之視哉
今誠齊其心力振去頹風提韁相及者守
punctuated:
間諜明矣。凡此六者，皆戰守之所必須，而邊計之不可一日缺焉者也。然戰守之道，又不止此者。蓋守可矣，調兵以守，恐滋費也，有聯土著之法焉。彼窮邊之地，千里蕭條，與豺狼爲鄰伍，以戰鬭爲嬉游，晝則荷戈而耕，夜則倚烽而覘。自非生於其域、習於其風，罕能狎其敵而寧其居也。今誠因其堡砦，聯以什伍，稍維之以約束，弗爲句集之煩、簿書之櫌，使人自爲兵，家自爲戰，凡奪敵所有，悉以與之，則室家墳墓，固其效死之區，而親戚比閭，又無攘奪之患矣。而守不足恃乎？

戰可矣，而孤軍以戰，恐寡弱也，有齊應援之法焉。蓋析圭儋爵，均爲王臣；列宇提封，一皆王土。居常則聲援相資，臨敵則移兵策應，自其宜也。何至幸災樂敗，篤禍求安，一鎮被兵而四鄰閉境，一營抗敵而列壁旁觀，有甚於秦越之視哉？今誠齊其心力，振去頹風，提韁相及者守
translation_en:
…and intelligence concerning the enemy will be clear. These six measures are all indispensable to fighting and defense, and frontier planning cannot dispense with them for even a single day. Yet the methods of fighting and defense do not end here. Defense may be practicable, but transferring troops to hold positions risks increasing expenditure. There is a method of organizing the local inhabitants together. In those remote frontier lands, desolate for a thousand li, people live alongside jackals and wolves and treat fighting as recreation. By day they carry weapons as they till the fields; by night they keep watch beside the beacon towers. Unless born in that region and accustomed to its ways, few can become familiar with its enemies and live there in security. If we now truly use their existing forts and stockades to organize them into groups of ten and five, maintaining modest discipline through regulations without the vexations of mustering or the burdens of paperwork [?], each person can serve as a soldier and each household fight for itself. Let them keep everything they seize from the enemy. Their homes and ancestral graves will assuredly be ground for which they fight to the death, while their relatives and neighbors will also be free from the danger of plunder. Could defense then fail to be dependable?

Fighting may be practicable, but an isolated force risks being too small and weak. There is a method of coordinating mutual support and reinforcement. Those who receive jade tablets of investiture and bear noble rank are equally servants of the sovereign; the allotted domains and their entire territories are all the sovereign’s land. In ordinary times they should sustain one another through mutual support; when confronting the enemy, they should transfer troops to provide coordinated assistance. This is naturally their duty. How could they go so far as to welcome others’ misfortunes and delight in their defeats, seeking their own security by deepening others’ calamities? When one garrison command comes under attack, its four neighbors close their borders; when one camp resists the enemy, the surrounding fortified positions merely look on. Is this not even worse than the indifference with which Qin and Yue regard one another? If we now truly unite their resolve and strength and shake off these degenerate habits, those who take up the reins and come to one another’s aid [?] will defend…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
擐相資幸禍樂觀者必誅罔赦則利已病
人之心息同舟共濟之功成矣而戰有不
足恃者乎夫流風積弊蠹壞已深起廢振
衰施功不易書生常談雖不足以盡邊計
之萬一然皆求所謂久大之規而意不欲
苟且因循於一時者也若夫究廢興利害
之源舉細大精麤之務亦惟慎擇節帥足
以盡之矣蓋節帥得人則人存政舉爲力
匪難端本澄源成功自易矣不是之思而
徒曰今日脩某邊明日罷某邊噫是誠厝
火積薪之下愚生不知邊事之弊將何所
底止也
punctuated: 擐相資，幸禍樂觀者必誅罔赦，則利已病人之心息，同舟共濟之功成矣，而戰有不足恃者乎？夫流風積弊，蠹壞已深；起廢振衰，施功不易。書生常談，雖不足以盡邊計之萬一，然皆求所謂久大之規，而意不欲苟且因循於一時者也。若夫究廢興利害之源，舉細大精麤之務，亦惟慎擇節帥，足以盡之矣。蓋節帥得人，則人存政舉，爲力匪難；端本澄源，成功自易矣。不是之思，而徒曰今日脩某邊，明日罷某邊，噫！是誠厝火積薪之下，愚生不知邊事之弊將何所底止也。
translation_en: …assist one another in taking up arms [?], and if those who welcome calamity and take pleasure in watching it are invariably executed without pardon, then the impulse to benefit oneself by harming others will cease, and all will succeed in joining forces, like passengers crossing a river in the same boat. How, then, could their fighting strength fail to be dependable? Entrenched habits and accumulated abuses have already caused profound decay. Restoring what has fallen into disuse and reviving what has declined are no easy accomplishments. Though these commonplace remarks of a scholar cannot encompass even a ten-thousandth part of frontier strategy, they all seek what might be called a comprehensive, enduring plan, with no intention of merely muddling along and following precedent for the moment. As for investigating the sources of decline and renewal, benefit and harm, and attending to matters great and small, detailed and general, all this can be accomplished simply by carefully selecting regional military commanders. If the right men are appointed, then with such men in office, sound administration will follow, and effective action will not be difficult. Set the foundations right and clear the sources, and success will naturally come easily. Instead of considering this, people merely say, ‘Today strengthen this frontier; tomorrow abandon that one.’ Alas! This is truly to place fire beneath a pile of firewood. I, an ignorant scholar, do not know where the resulting troubles in frontier affairs will end.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子之秋八月旣望山
西鄉試告竣曁第其士若文
爲錄以
獻制也〔迪〕以職事授簡綴言於末
乃進諸士告之曰惟晉多才
自古記之矣按其地大行恒
霍盤礴綿亙匯以洪河驚濤
吐吞元氣騰龍門下底柱而
===
東之美哉表裏河山斯冀幷
之故墟乎靈粹攸鍾自堯舜
以來代產聖哲在昔王以龍
興霸以虎視其間瑰瑋特達
顯功名於春秋者何可勝數
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子之秋八月旣望，山西鄉試告竣。曁第其士若文，爲錄以獻，制也。〔迪〕以職事授簡，綴言於末，乃進諸士告之曰：「惟晉多才，自古記之矣。按其地，大行、恒、霍盤礴綿亙，匯以洪河，驚濤吐吞，元氣騰龍門，下底柱而東之。美哉！表裏河山，斯冀幷之故墟乎！靈粹攸鍾，自堯舜以來，代產聖哲。在昔，王以龍興，霸以虎視，其間瑰瑋特達、顯功名於春秋者，何可勝數？
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In autumn of the jiazi year of the Jiajing reign [1564], on the sixteenth day of the eighth month, the Shanxi Provincial Examination concluded. Once the candidates and their essays had been ranked, a record was compiled for presentation to the throne, as prescribed by established regulation. I, 〔Di〕, was entrusted, by virtue of my official duties, with writing a few words at its end. I therefore summoned the candidates before me and addressed them:

“Jin’s abundance of talent has been recorded since antiquity. Survey its terrain: the Taihang [?], Heng, and Huo mountains extend in imposing, unbroken ranges, joined by the mighty Yellow River. Its surging waves swallow and disgorge; its primal force bounds through Longmen, descends past Dizhu, and flows eastward. How magnificent! Mountains within and the river without—is this not the ancient territory of Ji and Bing? Here numinous power and pure essence gather. Since the days of Yao and Shun, every age has produced sages and wise men. In former times, kings rose here like dragons, and hegemons surveyed their domains like tigers. Among them, how could one count all those extraordinary and outstanding men whose achievements and renown shone in the Spring and Autumn period? …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
不獨與地靈相雄長也迨我
國朝設科取士二百餘年凡抱
一才一藝者亦既羅而致之
矣以耳目所觀聞其瑰瑋特
達卓犖表樹可以塞
明詔當
上意贊太平之業者蓋僅見焉豈
===
不
古聖王所與興道資理將不
在茲與敷奏颺言唐虞不廢
舍科目孰從致之而謂文不
足以觀人者非是然有異者
山西地介戎狄年來有防胡
之役士枕戈負擔未暇曳裾
操鉛槧仰惟
punctuated: 不獨與地靈相雄長也。迨我國朝設科取士二百餘年，凡抱一才一藝者，亦既羅而致之矣。以耳目所觀聞，其瑰瑋特達、卓犖表樹，可以塞明詔、當上意、贊太平之業者，蓋僅見焉。豈不古聖王所與興道資理，將不在茲與？敷奏颺言，唐虞不廢，舍科目孰從致之？而謂文不足以觀人者，非是。然有異者，山西地介戎狄，年來有防胡之役，士枕戈負擔，未暇曳裾操鉛槧。仰惟
translation_en:
…Nor did they merely vie in preeminence with the spiritual potency of the land. For more than two hundred years since our dynasty established examinations to recruit men of ability, all who possessed even a single talent or accomplishment have been gathered in and brought into service. Yet, judging by what I have personally seen and heard, men of extraordinary distinction and outstanding achievement, capable of fulfilling the illustrious edicts, answering the sovereign’s intentions, and furthering the work of an age of peace, have been rarely seen. Could it be that those with whom the ancient sage kings would have advanced the Way and assisted in governance are not to be found here [?]? Presenting reports and publicly expounding one’s views were practices maintained under Tang and Yu. Apart from the examinations, by what means could such men be brought into service? Thus it is mistaken to say that literary compositions are insufficient for judging a person.
There is, however, a particular circumstance here: Shanxi borders the Rong and Di, and in recent years there has been military service to defend against the Hu. Scholars have slept with their weapons as pillows and shouldered burdens, with no leisure to wear scholars’ robes and take up writing implements. Reverently considering…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖天子經文緯武
玄化旁洽而封疆之臣咸共武服
繕治亭障用是境上桴鼓不
聞農狎於野穮蔉荐臻雖下
邑絕徼亦多絃誦聲矧嚮邇
畿輔聲敎所曁最先譬之暘谷
日升萬物卽被其光明也且
===
今歲賓興適逢甲子夫甲者
言萬物剖符甲而出也子者
言萬物之滋於下也陽氣用
事眞一元文明之會也士遘
昌辰豈非希曠之遇乎夫士有
才而不得試往往託爲文詞
以發其蘊今御史飭典戒事
punctuated:
聖天子經文緯武，玄化旁洽，而封疆之臣咸共武服，繕治亭障。用是境上桴鼓不聞，農狎於野，穮蔉荐臻。雖下邑絕徼，亦多絃誦聲。矧嚮邇畿輔，聲敎所曁最先，譬之暘谷日升，萬物卽被其光明也。
且今歲賓興，適逢甲子。夫甲者，言萬物剖符甲而出也；子者，言萬物之滋於下也。陽氣用事，眞一元文明之會也。士遘昌辰，豈非希曠之遇乎？夫士有才而不得試，往往託爲文詞，以發其蘊。今御史飭典戒事，
translation_en:
…the sage Son of Heaven orders civil affairs and marshals military power. His profound transforming influence reaches everywhere, while the officials guarding the frontiers all attend to their military duties, repairing watch posts and frontier defenses. Consequently, no alarm drums are heard along the border; farmers work at ease in the fields, and hoeing and earthing up proceed in succession [?]. Even in small towns and remote borderlands, the sounds of zithers and recitation are often heard. How much more so here, close to the capital region, among the first places reached by imperial instruction and influence: it is like the sun rising from the Valley of Sunrise, its radiance immediately covering all things.
Moreover, this year’s selection of worthy men falls precisely in a jiazi year. Jia signifies the myriad things splitting their husks [?] and emerging; zi signifies the myriad things multiplying below. Yang energy holds sway: truly this is a conjunction of renewed beginnings and cultural brilliance. For scholars to encounter such a flourishing age—is this not an exceptionally rare opportunity? Scholars who possess talent but have no chance to put it to the test often express themselves in literary compositions, bringing forth what they hold within. Now the Censor has put the regulations in order and issued instructions for the proceedings…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
祇承
德意以收羅之竭乃心力矣小大
百執事咸慎懋以從士誠懷
奇負異宜於此時自奮而出
固無所謂不得試而又安可
自誘溥也〔迪〕嘗讀古傳記見
其瑰瑋特達樹勳流聲未嘗
===
不廢書而歎誠慕之也乃今
稽文獻眺山川低徊聖帝之
鄉見其民淳朴好學信如延
陵思遠之論焉其士可知已
及縱觀厥文類能出入典謨
稱述堯舜要不詭於聖賢之
道者庶幾猶有唐虞氏之遺
punctuated: 祇承德意，以收羅之，竭乃心力矣。小大百執事咸慎懋以從。士誠懷奇負異，宜於此時自奮而出，固無所謂不得試，而又安可自誘溥也？〔迪〕嘗讀古傳記，見其瑰瑋特達、樹勳流聲，未嘗不廢書而歎，誠慕之也。乃今稽文獻，眺山川，低徊聖帝之鄉，見其民淳朴好學，信如延陵思遠之論焉，其士可知已。及縱觀厥文，類能出入典謨，稱述堯舜，要不詭於聖賢之道者，庶幾猶有唐虞氏之遺
translation_en:
…reverently receiving the imperial benevolent intent and exhausting his strength and care in gathering worthy men. All officials, great and small, have followed with diligence and caution. If scholars truly possess exceptional gifts and unusual abilities, they should exert themselves and come forward at this time. Certainly they cannot claim to lack an opportunity to be tested; how, then, could they mislead themselves [?]? I, 〔Di〕, have read ancient biographies and accounts and encountered men of extraordinary brilliance and distinction who established great achievements and left enduring reputations. Never have I failed to lay down the book and sigh in genuine admiration.

Now, examining the written records and the testimony of worthy men, gazing upon the mountains and rivers, and lingering in the homeland of the sage emperor, I find its people simple, honest, and devoted to learning. They truly accord with the observation of Yanling that their thoughts reached far; from this one can understand the character of their scholars. Surveying their writings, I find that most range freely through the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents and expound the deeds of Yao and Shun. In essentials, they do not depart from the Way of the sages and worthies. Perhaps there still survives among them a legacy of Tang and Yu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山西鄉試錄
text:
也乎嗚呼蹡景會以揚休光
者達觀之彥也斐英聲而騰
茂實者迪德之士也嚴義利
之辨審文質之宜究道德之
原弘皇王之略毅然以古人
自期以贊太平爲已任人將
曰此晉產也庶無點於河山
而可爲聖帝之鄉人矣若徒
以文相誇謝靜言而庸違
焉豈惟主司之責抑亦二三
子之咎
直隸河間府景州儒學學正
吳〔廸〕謹序
punctuated:
也乎？嗚呼！蹡景會以揚休光者，達觀之彥也；斐英聲而騰茂實者，迪德之士也。嚴義利之辨，審文質之宜，究道德之原，弘皇王之略，毅然以古人自期，以贊太平爲已任，人將曰：「此晉產也。」庶無點於河山，而可爲聖帝之鄉人矣。若徒以文相誇謝，靜言而庸違焉，豈惟主司之責，抑亦二三子之咎。
直隸河間府景州儒學學正吳〔廸〕謹序。
translation_en:
…might it not be so? Alas! Those who advance with this auspicious conjunction [?] and spread its glorious light are men of far-reaching vision; those who embellish their fine reputations and bring their substantial achievements to prominence are scholars who practice virtue. Distinguish strictly between righteousness and personal gain; carefully judge the proper balance between literary refinement and substance; investigate the source of the Way and virtue; and extend the grand designs of the ancient emperors and kings. Resolutely take the ancients as your standard and regard assisting in the attainment of Great Peace as your own responsibility. People will then say, “This man is a native of Jin.” Thus you may avoid bringing dishonor upon these rivers and mountains and prove worthy of being countrymen of the sage emperors. But if you merely vie with one another in literary display [?], speaking fine words while acting contrary to them, the responsibility will lie not only with the presiding examiners: the fault will also be yours, gentlemen.
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Di 吳廸, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region.
